README.md:217:- `~/.config/ghostty/config` - Ghostty/cmux terminal config (`macos-option-as-alt` for tmux Meta keybindings, disabled ligatures, explicit `clipboard-write = allow` / `clipboard-read = ask` for OSC 52) ([docs](docs/tools/ghostty.md))
README.md:228:- `~/.tmux.conf` - Tmux configuration with TPM plugins (resurrect, continuum, tmux-floax floating pane, tmux-fzf for fuzzy keybinding/session/pane search rebound to `prefix+?`, tmux-fzf-url, tmux-open), vim-style copy mode with clipboard yank, capture-pane helpers (`prefix+y`/`Y`/`C-y`), a native popup menu (`prefix+Space` or `prefix+e`, script-driven with submenus and height-aware trimming) with layout/resize/session management, popup shell (`prefix+\``) and lazygit popup (`prefix+G`), a glow-rendered cheatsheet (`prefix+Space` → `?`), vim-style pane nav, `Ctrl+1..9` quick window switching (CSI-u terminals), extended-keys for coding agents (including `Ctrl+/` in Neovim), sesh keybindings (`prefix+g` fzf picker, `prefix+T` television picker, `prefix+O` built-in picker, `prefix+W` window picker, `prefix+S` last), responsive Catppuccin status bar (adapts modules to terminal width for mobile), and config reload on `prefix+R` ([docs](docs/tools/tmux/README.md))
README.md:229:- `~/.dotfiles/bin/x` - Cross-platform terminal wrapper for `copy` / `copy-file` / `paste` / `open`; `x copy` has an OSC 52 fallback for SSH text copy, while `x copy-file` copies desktop file objects for Finder / Files paste ([docs](docs/tools/clipboard.md))
README.md:231:- `~/.dotfiles/bin/sms` - Huawei router SMS reader (HiLink XML API; verification-code extraction, clipboard integration, TV channel) ([docs](docs/tools/sms.md))

docs/shells/aliases.md:728:## Clipboard History
docs/shells/aliases.md:730:> Hybrid backend: **Maccy** on macOS (queries plaintext SQLite at `~/Library/Application Support/Maccy/Storage.sqlite`), **CopyQ** on Linux (uses the shipped `copyq` CLI). Autodetected at call time; override with `CLIP_BACKEND=copyq|maccy`. No-op with install hint on hosts without either tool (e.g. `ubuntu_server`). See [docs/tools/clipboard.md → Clipboard history](../tools/clipboard.md#clipboard-history-cb--cbl--cbe) for the why + threat-model notes.
docs/shells/aliases.md:734:| `cbl [N]` | function | `dot_config/shell/56_clipboard_history.sh` | List recent N clipboard items (default 20), tab-separated `<idx>\t<first-line>` |
docs/shells/aliases.md:735:| `cb` | function | `dot_config/shell/56_clipboard_history.sh` | fzf picker over `cbl 100` → copy selection to system clipboard |
docs/shells/aliases.md:736:| `cbe` | function | `dot_config/shell/56_clipboard_history.sh` | fzf picker → open selection in `$EDITOR` → write edited text back to clipboard |
docs/shells/aliases.md:752:| `abspath [-r] [-t] [PATH...]` | function | `dot_config/shell/58_abspath.sh` | Print absolute path(s): no args → logical cwd (like `pwd`); `PATH...` → one absolute path per line. Logical by default (normalizes `.`/`..`, keeps symlinks, existence not required); `-r`/`--resolve` → physical path (follows symlinks, must exist); `-t`/`--tilde` → abbreviate a `$HOME`-rooted result to `~`. stdout stays pipe-clean, so `abspath FILE \| x copy` grabs a path to the clipboard (fills the `realpath FILE \| x copy` hint in `x`'s help). Requires python3 |
docs/shells/aliases.md:753:| `cref [-a\|-c] [-L] [-n] [--] FILE[:LINE[-LINE]]` | function | `dot_config/shell/59_cref.sh` | Copy a Cursor/Claude-Code-style file mention (`@path`, `@path:12`, `@path:12-40`) to the clipboard — the shell twin of Neovim's `<leader>y` [copy-reference](../neovim/copy-reference.md) maps. Path flavor: default = **git-root-relative** (falls back to cwd/`~`/absolute the way nvim's `:~:.` does); `-a`/`--absolute` = machine-absolute; `-c`/`--cwd` = relative to `$PWD`. Line info comes from `FILE:LINE[-LINE]`, trailing positionals (`cref FILE 12 40`), or — with no FILE arg — the first stdin line in grep/ripgrep `FILE:LINE:…` format (`rg -n foo \| cref`); a trailing `:col[:text]` is dropped and `:12-12` collapses to `:12`. Copies via the `x` CLI (OSC 52, SSH-safe); `-n`/`--no-copy` prints only, `-L`/`--no-line` forces a bare `@path`. stdout stays pipe-clean; `Copied @…` toast on stderr. Requires python3 |
docs/shells/aliases.md:759:> Requires tmux + OSC 133 markers in the pane's scrollback (emitted by [`02_shell_integration.zsh`](../../dot_config/zsh/tools/02_shell_integration.zsh) — if missing, run `exec zsh` to reload). All three functions print to stdout (pipe-friendly: `cpout | grep ERROR`) AND copy to the system clipboard via tmux's OSC 52 bridge. Shell-level counterparts of the `prefix + M-y` / `M-i` tmux bindings — see [docs/tools/tmux/README.md → OSC 133](../tools/tmux/README.md#osc-133-command-boundary-navigation-warp-style).
docs/shells/aliases.md:766:| `tpath` | function | `dot_config/shell/63_tmux_path.sh` | Print (`target` / `pane_id` / `cwd`) + copy the current pane's `session:window.pane` target (e.g. `main:2.1`) to the clipboard — for reconnecting or telling an AI agent which pane to act on. stdout stays pipe-clean (`tpath \| head -1`); confirmation on stderr. GUI/keyboard twins: right-click pane → "Copy pane path", `prefix + M-p` menu, and `prefix + C-p`. |

4	#

252	# Strategy (in order):
253	#   1. PPA `ppa:appimagelauncher-team/stable` — preferred on 20.04/22.04.
254	#   2. GitHub `.deb` fallback — PPA is known-broken on Ubuntu 24.04 "noble"
255	#      as of 2026 (upstream has not published a noble release); the latest
256	#      GitHub `.deb` still installs cleanly.
257	#   3. AppImageLauncher **Lite** — a user-level AppImage that integrates
258	#      itself without root. Enabled when `gui_apps_linux_no_root=true`.
259	#
260	# Docs: see docs/tools/appimage.md for install paths, ail-cli usage, and
261	# the libfuse2 / AppArmor gotchas on recent Ubuntu.
262	# =============================================================================
263	
264	- name: Check if AppImageLauncher is installed (system-wide)
265	  when:
266	    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
267	    - target_architecture != 'armv7l'
268	  ansible.builtin.command: dpkg -s appimagelauncher
269	  register: ail_check
270	  changed_when: false
271	  failed_when: false
272	
273	- name: Install AppImageLauncher via PPA
274	  when:
275	    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
276	    - target_architecture != 'armv7l'
277	    - not (gui_apps_linux_no_root | bool)
278	    - ail_check.rc != 0
279	  become: true
280	  tags: [sudo]
281	  block:
282	    # deb822_repository (apt_repository is deprecated, removed in ansible-core
283	    # 2.25) doesn't support the ppa: shorthand — spell out the launchpad URI +
284	    # signing key. Fingerprint from
285	    # https://api.launchpad.net/devel/~appimagelauncher-team/+archive/ubuntu/stable
286	    # It also doesn't run `apt update` itself, so verify reachability and roll
287	    # the .sources file back on failure — a leftover broken source would fail
288	    # the base role's cache update on every later run.
289	    # Requires python3-debian (installed by the base role).
290	    - name: Remove legacy one-line AppImageLauncher PPA source (pre-deb822 format)
291	      ansible.builtin.file:
292	        path: /etc/apt/sources.list.d/appimagelauncher-team-stable.list
293	        state: absent
294	
295	    - name: Add AppImageLauncher PPA (deb822)
296	      ansible.builtin.deb822_repository:
297	        name: appimagelauncher-team-stable
298	        types: deb
299	        uris: https://ppa.launchpadcontent.net/appimagelauncher-team/stable/ubuntu
300	        suites: "{{ ansible_facts['distribution_release'] }}"
301	        components: main
302	        signed_by: https://keyserver.ubuntu.com/pks/lookup?op=get&search=0xACD802F535B6F55D365285574AF9B16F75EF2FCA
303	      ignore_errors: true
304	      register: ail_ppa
305	
306	    - name: Refresh apt cache (AppImageLauncher PPA)
307	      when: ail_ppa is succeeded
308	      ansible.builtin.apt:
309	        update_cache: true
310	      ignore_errors: true
311	
312	    # The apt module treats a partially-failed `apt update` (one unreachable
313	    # source, others fine) as SUCCESS-with-warnings, so probe the PPA
314	    # deterministically: package resolvable from the launchpad URI ⇒ keep +
315	    # install; otherwise roll the .sources file back (a leftover broken
316	    # source breaks/slows every later apt update) and let the GitHub .deb
317	    # fallback below take over.
318	    - name: Check appimagelauncher is resolvable from the PPA
319	      when: ail_ppa is succeeded
320	      ansible.builtin.command: apt-cache policy appimagelauncher
321	      register: ail_policy
322	      changed_when: false
323	      failed_when: false
324	
325	    - name: Remove AppImageLauncher PPA (broken or unreachable)
326	      when:
327	        - ail_ppa is succeeded
328	        - "'ppa.launchpadcontent.net/appimagelauncher-team' not in (ail_policy.stdout | default(''))"
329	      ansible.builtin.deb822_repository:
330	        name: appimagelauncher-team-stable
331	        state: absent
332	
333	    - name: Install appimagelauncher from PPA
334	      ansible.builtin.apt:
335	        name: appimagelauncher
336	        state: present
337	      when: "'ppa.launchpadcontent.net/appimagelauncher-team' in (ail_policy.stdout | default(''))"
338	      register: ail_apt_install
339	      ignore_errors: true
340	  rescue:
341	    - name: Warn AppImageLauncher PPA install failed
342	      ansible.builtin.debug:
343	        msg: "AppImageLauncher PPA install failed — trying GitHub .deb fallback next."
344	
345	- name: Install AppImageLauncher from GitHub .deb (fallback)
346	  when:
347	    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
348	    - target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'aarch64']
349	    - not (gui_apps_linux_no_root | bool)
350	    - ail_check.rc != 0
351	    - (ail_apt_install is not defined) or (ail_apt_install is not succeeded)
352	  become: true
353	  tags: [sudo]
354	  block:
355	    - name: Get latest AppImageLauncher release metadata
356	      ansible.builtin.uri:
357	        url: https://api.github.com/repos/TheAssassin/AppImageLauncher/releases/latest
358	        return_content: true
359	      register: ail_release
360	
361	    - name: Resolve AppImageLauncher .deb asset URL
362	      ansible.builtin.set_fact:
363	        ail_deb_url: >-
364	          {{ (ail_release.json.assets
365	              | selectattr('name', 'match', '^appimagelauncher_.*_' + ail_deb_arch + '\\.deb$')
366	              | map(attribute='browser_download_url')
367	              | list
368	              | first) | default('') }}
369	      vars:
370	        ail_deb_arch: "{{ {'x86_64': 'amd64', 'aarch64': 'arm64'}[target_architecture] }}"
371	
372	    - name: Download AppImageLauncher .deb
373	      when: ail_deb_url | length > 0
374	      ansible.builtin.get_url:
375	        url: "{{ ail_deb_url }}"
376	        dest: /tmp/appimagelauncher.deb
377	        mode: '0644'
378	        timeout: 180
379	
380	    - name: Install AppImageLauncher .deb
381	      when: ail_deb_url | length > 0
382	      ansible.builtin.apt:
383	        deb: /tmp/appimagelauncher.deb
384	        state: present
385	  rescue:
386	    - name: Warn AppImageLauncher .deb install failed
387	      ansible.builtin.debug:
388	        msg: "AppImageLauncher .deb install failed — the Lite user-level variant is still available via noRoot mode."
389	
390	- name: Install AppImageLauncher Lite (user-level, noRoot)
391	  when:
392	    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
393	    - target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'aarch64']
394	    - gui_apps_linux_no_root | bool
395	  block:
396	    - name: Ensure ~/Applications exists
397	      ansible.builtin.file:
398	        path: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/Applications"
399	        state: directory
400	        mode: '0755'
401	
402	    - name: Get latest AppImageLauncher release (for Lite variant)
403	      ansible.builtin.uri:
404	        url: https://api.github.com/repos/TheAssassin/AppImageLauncher/releases/latest
405	        return_content: true
406	      register: ail_lite_release
407	
408	    - name: Resolve AppImageLauncher Lite AppImage URL
409	      ansible.builtin.set_fact:
410	        ail_lite_url: >-
411	          {{ (ail_lite_release.json.assets
412	              | selectattr('name', 'match', '^appimagelauncher-lite-.*-' + target_architecture + '\\.AppImage$')
413	              | map(attribute='browser_download_url')
414	              | list
415	              | first) | default('') }}
416	
417	    - name: Download AppImageLauncher Lite
418	      when: ail_lite_url | length > 0
419	      ansible.builtin.get_url:
420	        url: "{{ ail_lite_url }}"
421	        dest: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/Applications/appimagelauncher-lite.AppImage"
422	        mode: '0755'
423	        timeout: 180
424	      register: ail_lite_dl
425	      ignore_errors: true
426	
427	    - name: Note how to finalise AppImageLauncher Lite integration
428	      when: ail_lite_dl is defined and ail_lite_dl is succeeded
429	      ansible.builtin.debug:
430	        msg: >-
431	          Downloaded AppImageLauncher Lite to ~/Applications/appimagelauncher-lite.AppImage.
432	          Run `~/Applications/appimagelauncher-lite.AppImage install` once to register
433	          the integration; see docs/tools/appimage.md for ail-cli usage.
434	
435	# =============================================================================
436	# Visual Studio Code — official Microsoft apt repository
437	# =============================================================================
438	
439	- name: Check if VSCode is installed
440	  when:
441	    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
442	    - target_architecture != 'armv7l'
443	  ansible.builtin.command: dpkg -s code
444	  register: vscode_check
445	  changed_when: false
446	  failed_when: false
447	
448	- name: Install VSCode via Microsoft apt repo
449	  when:
450	    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
451	    - target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'aarch64']
452	    - not (gui_apps_linux_no_root | bool)
453	    - vscode_check.rc != 0
454	  become: true
455	  tags: [sudo]
456	  block:
457	    - name: Ensure /etc/apt/keyrings exists
458	      ansible.builtin.file:
459	        path: /etc/apt/keyrings
460	        state: directory
461	        mode: '0755'
462	
463	    - name: Add Microsoft GPG key (dearmored)
464	      ansible.builtin.shell: |
465	        set -eu
466	        wget -qO- https://packages.microsoft.com/keys/microsoft.asc \
467	          | gpg --dearmor -o /etc/apt/keyrings/microsoft.gpg
468	      args:
469	        creates: /etc/apt/keyrings/microsoft.gpg
470	
471	    # apt_repository is deprecated (removed in ansible-core 2.25); deb822
472	    # doesn't run `apt update` itself, so refresh explicitly. A cache-update
473	    # failure lands in the rescue below, which rolls the .sources file back
474	    # so it can't break the base role's cache update on later runs.
475	    # Requires python3-debian (installed by the base role).
476	    - name: Remove legacy one-line VSCode source (pre-deb822 format)
477	      ansible.builtin.file:
478	        path: /etc/apt/sources.list.d/vscode.list
479	        state: absent
480	
481	    - name: Add VSCode apt repository (deb822)
482	      ansible.builtin.deb822_repository:
483	        name: vscode
484	        types: deb
485	        uris: https://packages.microsoft.com/repos/code
486	        suites: stable
487	        components: main
488	        architectures: "{{ {'x86_64': 'amd64', 'aarch64': 'arm64'}[target_architecture] }}"
489	        signed_by: /etc/apt/keyrings/microsoft.gpg
490	
491	    - name: Refresh apt cache (VSCode repo)
492	      ansible.builtin.apt:
493	        update_cache: true
494	
495	    - name: Install VSCode package
496	      ansible.builtin.apt:
497	        name: code
498	        state: present
499	  rescue:
500	    - name: Remove VSCode apt repository (install failed; avoid leaving a broken source)
501	      ansible.builtin.deb822_repository:
502	        name: vscode
503	        state: absent
504	      ignore_errors: true
505	
506	    - name: Warn VSCode install failed
507	      ansible.builtin.debug:
508	        msg: "VSCode install failed — rerun with --tags gui_apps after fixing network/GPG/apt issues."
509	
510	# =============================================================================
511	# Cursor — .deb from cursor.com
512	#
513	# The download API returns a redirect to the latest build for the given
514	# platform. The whole block is tolerant: a failed download is logged but
515	# does not fail the playbook. Users can always fall back to the AppImage
516	# path documented in docs/tools/appimage.md.
517	# =============================================================================
518	
519	- name: Check if Cursor is installed
520	  when:
521	    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
522	    - target_architecture != 'armv7l'
523	  ansible.builtin.command: dpkg -s cursor
524	  register: cursor_check
525	  changed_when: false
526	  failed_when: false
527	
528	- name: Install Cursor via .deb
529	  when:
530	    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
531	    - target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'aarch64']
532	    - not (gui_apps_linux_no_root | bool)
533	    - cursor_check.rc != 0
534	  become: true
535	  tags: [sudo]
536	  block:
537	    # cursor.com/api/download returns JSON ({downloadUrl, debUrl, rpmUrl, ...}),
538	    # not a redirect to the binary. Must resolve debUrl first, then fetch.
539	    - name: Fetch latest Cursor release metadata
540	      ansible.builtin.uri:
541	        url: >-
542	          https://cursor.com/api/download?platform=linux-{{
543	            {'x86_64': 'x64', 'aarch64': 'arm64'}[target_architecture]
544	          }}&releaseTrack=stable
545	        return_content: true
546	      register: cursor_meta
547	      ignore_errors: true
548	
549	    # downloads.cursor.com routes poorly from GFW-region networks and TCP
550	    # streams frequently drop mid-transfer ("Incomplete read" with partial
551	    # st_size). get_url has no native resume, so retry the whole fetch up
552	    # to 4 times — 4 x 174MB is cheaper than babysitting a failed install.
553	    - name: Download latest Cursor .deb
554	      when:
555	        - cursor_meta is defined
556	        - cursor_meta is succeeded
557	        - cursor_meta.json is defined
558	        - cursor_meta.json.debUrl is defined
559	      ansible.builtin.get_url:
560	        url: "{{ cursor_meta.json.debUrl }}"
561	        dest: /tmp/cursor.deb
562	        mode: '0644'
563	        timeout: 300
564	        force: true
565	      register: cursor_dl
566	      until: cursor_dl is succeeded
567	      retries: 4
568	      delay: 5
569	      ignore_errors: true
570	
571	    - name: Install Cursor .deb
572	      when: cursor_dl is defined and cursor_dl is succeeded
573	      ansible.builtin.apt:
574	        deb: /tmp/cursor.deb
575	        state: present
576	      ignore_errors: true
577	  rescue:
578	    - name: Warn Cursor .deb install failed
579	      ansible.builtin.debug:
580	        msg: >-
581	          Cursor .deb install failed. You can fall back to the AppImage flow —
582	          download from https://cursor.com/download and drop it under
583	          ~/Applications/; AppImageLauncher will auto-integrate. See
584	          docs/tools/appimage.md for the full recipe.
585	
586	# =============================================================================
587	# Google Chrome — official .deb, self-registering apt source
588	#
589	# Ubuntu ships no Chromium .deb (Canonical's `chromium-browser` is a snap
590	# shim), so a Chromium-engine browser has to come from upstream. Chrome's
591	# .deb postinst writes /etc/apt/sources.list.d/google-chrome.list plus its
592	# keyring, so `apt upgrade` keeps it current afterwards — the same trick
593	# Cursor/VSCode use, documented in docs/playbooks/linux-gui-apps.md
594	# "Why .deb auto-update works". That is why we do NOT add a deb822 source
595	# ourselves: doing both yields duplicate-source warnings on every apt run.
596	#
597	# x86_64 only — Google publishes no arm64 Linux build of Chrome (unlike
598	# VSCode/Cursor). aarch64 desktops fall through to Firefox/Zen.
599	# =============================================================================
600	
601	- name: Check if Google Chrome is installed
602	  when:
603	    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
604	    - target_architecture == 'x86_64'
605	  ansible.builtin.command: dpkg -s google-chrome-stable
606	  register: chrome_check
607	  changed_when: false
608	  failed_when: false
609	
610	- name: Install Google Chrome via .deb
611	  when:
612	    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
613	    - target_architecture == 'x86_64'
614	    - not (gui_apps_linux_no_root | bool)
615	    - chrome_check.rc is defined
616	    - chrome_check.rc != 0
617	  become: true
618	  tags: [sudo]
619	  block:
620	    - name: Download Google Chrome .deb
621	      ansible.builtin.get_url:
622	        url: https://dl.google.com/linux/direct/google-chrome-stable_current_amd64.deb
623	        dest: /tmp/google-chrome-stable.deb
624	        mode: '0644'
625	        timeout: 300
626	        force: true
627	      register: chrome_dl
628	      until: chrome_dl is succeeded
629	      retries: 4
630	      delay: 5
631	      ignore_errors: true
632	
633	    # `is not skipped` alongside `is succeeded` — a task skipped by its `when:`
634	    # also passes `is succeeded`, which is how the Zen block silently installed
635	    # nothing for months. See
636	    # pitfalls/ansible-folded-scalar-regex-empty-url-silent-skip.md
637	    - name: Install Google Chrome .deb
638	      when:
639	        - chrome_dl is defined
640	        - chrome_dl is not skipped
641	        - chrome_dl is succeeded
642	      ansible.builtin.apt:
643	        deb: /tmp/google-chrome-stable.deb
644	        state: present
645	      ignore_errors: true
646	
647	    - name: Remove downloaded Chrome .deb
648	      ansible.builtin.file:
649	        path: /tmp/google-chrome-stable.deb
650	        state: absent
651	  rescue:
652	    - name: Warn Google Chrome install failed
653	      ansible.builtin.debug:
654	        msg: >-
655	          Google Chrome install failed — rerun with --tags gui_apps after
656	          fixing network/apt issues, or grab the .deb by hand from
657	          https://www.google.com/chrome/. Zen and Firefox remain available
658	          in the meantime.
659	
660	# =============================================================================
661	# Discord — channel selectable via discord_channel ansible var (default: flatpak)
662	#
663	# Values (set by .discordChannel chezmoi prompt, plumbed via
664	# .chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl):
665	#   - flatpak: Flathub com.discordapp.Discord; auto-updates via `flatpak update`.
666	#              The recommended path — Discord .deb does NOT ship an apt-source
667	#              postinst, so .deb installs require manual re-deploy on every
668	#              release (the in-app updater pops a download modal but cannot
669	#              actually run dpkg). Flatpak side-steps that pain.
670	#   - deb:     Fetch the official .deb; only re-fetches when dpkg -s discord
671	#              fails. Keep this path for users who already standardized on the
672	#              .deb and don't want a Flatpak runtime on disk.
673	#   - none:    Skip — install Discord some other way (Vesktop, web app, etc.).
674	#
675	# Discord upstream only ships amd64 binaries; both .deb and Flathub follow.
676	# armhf is not supported by either path. See
677	# docs/playbooks/linux-gui-apps.md for the full decision tree.
678	# =============================================================================
679	
680	- name: Set Discord channel default
681	  when: ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
682	  ansible.builtin.set_fact:
683	    discord_channel: "{{ discord_channel | default('flatpak') }}"
684	
685	- name: Warn Discord is amd64-only on Linux (aarch64)
686	  when:
687	    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
688	    - target_architecture == 'aarch64'
689	    - discord_channel != 'none'
690	  ansible.builtin.debug:
691	    msg: >-
692	      Discord does not publish official aarch64 binaries (no .deb, no
693	      Flatpak ARM build). Skipping. Use a community build like Vesktop on
694	      ARM64 if you need Discord — see https://github.com/Vencord/Vesktop.
695	
696	# --- deb channel ----------------------------------------------------------
697	
698	- name: Check if Discord .deb is installed
699	  when:
700	    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
701	    - target_architecture == 'x86_64'
702	    - discord_channel == 'deb'
703	  ansible.builtin.command: dpkg -s discord
704	  register: discord_check
705	  changed_when: false
706	  failed_when: false
707	
708	- name: Install Discord via .deb
709	  when:
710	    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
711	    - target_architecture == 'x86_64'
712	    - discord_channel == 'deb'
713	    - not (gui_apps_linux_no_root | bool)
714	    - discord_check.rc != 0
715	  become: true
716	  tags: [sudo]
717	  block:
718	    - name: Download latest Discord .deb (redirect from discord.com)
719	      ansible.builtin.get_url:
720	        url: https://discord.com/api/download?platform=linux&format=deb
721	        dest: /tmp/discord.deb
722	        mode: '0644'
723	        timeout: 300
724	      register: discord_dl
725	      ignore_errors: true
726	
727	    - name: Install Discord .deb
728	      when: discord_dl is defined and discord_dl is succeeded
729	      ansible.builtin.apt:
730	        deb: /tmp/discord.deb
731	        state: present
732	      ignore_errors: true
733	  rescue:
734	    - name: Warn Discord .deb install failed
735	      ansible.builtin.debug:
736	        msg: >-
737	          Discord .deb install failed. Fall back to the official tarball at
738	          https://discord.com/api/download?platform=linux&format=tar.gz
739	          (extract to ~/Applications/Discord/ and wire up a .desktop entry),
740	          or switch to Flatpak by setting discordChannel=flatpak in
741	          ~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml.
742	
743	# --- flatpak channel ------------------------------------------------------
744	
745	- name: Install Discord via Flatpak (channel=flatpak)
746	  when:
747	    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
748	    - target_architecture == 'x86_64'
749	    - discord_channel == 'flatpak'
750	    - not (gui_apps_linux_no_root | bool)
751	  block:
752	    - name: Ensure flatpak package is present
753	      become: true
754	      tags: [sudo]
755	      ansible.builtin.apt:
756	        name: flatpak
757	        state: present
758	        update_cache: true
759	        cache_valid_time: 3600
760	
761	    - name: Ensure Flathub remote is configured (per-user)
762	      community.general.flatpak_remote:
763	        name: flathub
764	        flatpakrepo_url: https://flathub.org/repo/flathub.flatpakrepo
765	        method: user
766	        state: present
767	
768	    - name: Install Discord from Flathub (per-user)
769	      community.general.flatpak:
770	        name: com.discordapp.Discord
771	        state: present
772	        method: user
773	        remote: flathub
774	  rescue:
775	    - name: Warn Discord Flatpak install failed
776	      ansible.builtin.debug:
777	        msg: >-
778	          Discord Flatpak install failed. Manual fallback —
779	          `flatpak install flathub com.discordapp.Discord` from a shell,
780	          or set discordChannel=deb in ~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml to
781	          revert to the .deb path.
782	
783	# =============================================================================
784	# Steam — optional gaming bundle via Valve's official apt repository
785	#
786	# Gated by the `installGamingApps` chezmoi prompt, plumbed through
787	# `gui_apps_linux_install_gaming_apps`. Valve's repo publishes an amd64
788	# `steam-launcher` package and an i386 transitional package; adding i386 is
789	# required so Steam can resolve its 32-bit runtime libraries. Avoid hard-coding
790	# old package names like `libgl1-mesa-glx`, which no longer exists on Ubuntu
791	# 24.04 — let apt resolve current dependencies/recommends from the package.
792	# =============================================================================
793	
794	- name: Skip Steam on non-x86_64 Linux
795	  when:
796	    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
797	    - gui_apps_linux_install_gaming_apps | bool
798	    - target_architecture != 'x86_64'
799	  ansible.builtin.debug:
800	    msg: >-
801	      Steam is only installed on x86_64 here. Valve's Ubuntu launcher and
802	      game runtime expect amd64/i386 packages; skipping on {{ target_architecture }}.
803	
804	- name: Skip Steam in noRoot mode
805	  when:
806	    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
807	    - gui_apps_linux_install_gaming_apps | bool
808	    - target_architecture == 'x86_64'
809	    - gui_apps_linux_no_root | bool
810	  ansible.builtin.debug:
811	    msg: >-

57	# OSC 52 clipboard copy: ships stdin bytes through a terminal escape sequence.
58	# Works over SSH with no X/Wayland as long as the terminal (or tmux with

69	    local max_len="${X_OSC52_MAX_BYTES:-75000}"
70	    if (( ${#data} > max_len )); then
71	        err "OSC 52 payload too large (${#data} bytes, cap ${max_len}); most terminals silently drop larger OSC 52 sequences (64-256KB is common, iTerm2 ~1MB)"

 `./docs/tools/clipboard.md`

```text
1	# Clipboard & OSC 52
2	
3	This doc explains how clipboard sync is wired across this dotfiles setup, with a focus on **OSC 52** — the escape sequence that lets a remote SSH session put text on your **local** machine's clipboard.
4	
5	## TL;DR
6	
7	| You are… | Yank in Neovim goes to… | Capture pane (`prefix+y/Y/C-y`) goes to… |
8	|----------|--------------------------|---------------------------------------------|
9	| Local (macOS or Linux desktop) | system clipboard (default provider: `pbcopy` / `wl-copy` / `xclip`) | same, via `tmux load-buffer -w -` which emits OSC 52 *and* sets tmux's paste buffer |
10	| SSH (remote box, with or without tmux) | **local** machine's clipboard (via OSC 52) | **local** machine's clipboard (via tmux → OSC 52) |
11	
12	No extra tools, no X forwarding, no socat listener needed. The only hard requirement is a terminal emulator on your **local** machine that supports OSC 52 (Ghostty, Alacritty, iTerm2, Kitty, WezTerm — all do).
13	
14	## What is OSC 52?
15	
16	`OSC 52` is an ANSI escape sequence:
17	
18	```
19	ESC ] 52 ; c ; <base64-of-data> BEL
20	```
21	
22	Any program that can write to a terminal can emit this sequence; the terminal emulator on the other end decodes the base64 and writes it to the system clipboard. The crucial property: **escape sequences travel up the TTY back to the client terminal**, so this works transparently over SSH, mosh, and nested `tmux ssh` chains — no display server, no socket forwarding.
23	
24	Tradeoffs:
25	
26	- **Write** is ubiquitous. Most modern terminals allow it by default or with a simple opt-in.
27	- **Read** (paste from local clipboard back into remote apps) is much less supported — many terminals refuse for obvious security reasons (a malicious server could exfiltrate your clipboard). Ghostty prompts; Alacritty flat-out ignores it.
28	- A terminal multiplexer (tmux, screen, zellij) sits between the inner app and the outer terminal. It must be configured to either **emit** OSC 52 to its host terminal or **pass through** OSC 52 from inner apps.
29	- **Text only** — OSC 52 carries base64 *text*; it cannot move an **image** (or file object) from your local clipboard into a remote app, and it flows remote→local, the wrong direction for feeding a screenshot to a remote agent. Getting a local screenshot into a remote coding agent (Claude Code / Neovim) is a separate problem — see [`remote-image-paste.md`](./remote-image-paste.md).
30	
31	Reference: [tmux Clipboard wiki](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/wiki/Clipboard), [XTerm control sequences (OSC)](https://www.invisible-island.net/xterm/ctlseqs/ctlseqs.html).
32	
33	## How this repo wires it up
34	
35	Four layers cooperate. Removing any one silently breaks remote-clipboard sync.
36	
37	### 1. Terminal emulator (outer, on your local machine)
38	
39	Must accept OSC 52 writes from whatever is running inside it.
40	
41	**Ghostty / cmux** — [`dot_config/ghostty/config`](../../dot_config/ghostty/config):
42	
43	```conf
44	clipboard-write = allow   # let inner apps set the system clipboard
45	clipboard-read  = ask     # prompt before reads (safer default)
46	```
47	
48	Both match current Ghostty defaults but are pinned explicitly so policy drifts from upstream don't silently break (or weaken) this chain.
49	
50	**Alacritty** — native support, no config needed. Paste from OSC 52 not supported.
51	
52	**iTerm2 / Kitty / WezTerm** — native support. iTerm2 requires `Preferences → General → Selection → Applications in terminal may access clipboard` for reads.
53	
54	### 2. Multiplexer — tmux
55	
56	[`dot_config/tmux/common.conf`](../../dot_config/tmux/common.conf):
57	
58	```tmux
59	set -g set-clipboard on
60	
61	set -as terminal-features ",xterm*:clipboard"
62	set -as terminal-features ",ghostty*:clipboard"
63	set -as terminal-features ",alacritty*:clipboard"
64	
65	set -g allow-passthrough on
66	```
67	
68	- **`set-clipboard on`** — tmux both re-emits OSC 52 to the outer terminal when its own copy-mode yanks, and passes OSC 52 from inner apps (Neovim, less, etc.) through. `external` would only pass through; `on` is a strict superset and simpler.
69	- **`terminal-features …:clipboard`** — tells tmux the outer terminal supports OSC 52 without needing a terminfo `Ms` capability. Many distros ship a `tmux-256color` entry that lacks `Ms`, so declaring the feature directly avoids surprises when `chezmoi apply` is run on a fresh box.
70	- **`allow-passthrough on`** — lets terminal-image protocols (sixel, kitty graphics) work; also covers OSC passthrough for nested multiplexers.
71	
72	**Capture-pane helpers** — [`dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf`](../../dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf) — use the tmux-native idiom rather than shelling out:
73	
74	```tmux
75	bind y   run-shell "tmux capture-pane -p   | tmux load-buffer -w -"
76	bind Y   run-shell "tmux capture-pane -pS - | tmux load-buffer -w -"
77	bind C-y run-shell "tmux capture-pane -pS - | fzf-tmux … | tmux load-buffer -w -"
78	```
79	
80	`load-buffer -w -` reads stdin into tmux's paste buffer *and* (because of `-w`) forwards to the system clipboard via OSC 52. Previously these bindings used a `pbcopy | xclip | xsel` fallback chain that only worked locally — over SSH they copied to the **remote** machine's clipboard, which is useless. The tmux-native form works identically in both places.
81	
82	`set-buffer -w …` offers the same `-w` flag but takes data as an argument, which introduces shell-quoting landmines on multi-line pane content; `load-buffer -w -` reads stdin and sidesteps that.
83	
84	### 3. Editor — Neovim
85	
86	[`dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua`](../../dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua):
87	
88	```lua
89	vim.opt.clipboard = "unnamedplus"
90	
91	if vim.env.SSH_CONNECTION or vim.env.SSH_TTY then
92	  local osc52 = require("vim.ui.clipboard.osc52")
93	  vim.g.clipboard = {
94	    name = "OSC 52",
95	    copy  = { ["+"] = osc52.copy("+"),  ["*"] = osc52.copy("*")  },
96	    paste = { ["+"] = osc52.paste("+"), ["*"] = osc52.paste("*") },
97	  }
98	end
99	```
100	
101	- Locally, LazyVim's default provider is used (`pbcopy`/`xclip`/`wl-copy` — with working paste).
102	- Over SSH, Neovim's built-in `vim.ui.clipboard.osc52` (shipping since Neovim 0.10) emits OSC 52 directly, bypassing any `pbcopy` binary on the remote host.
103	- The check is `SSH_CONNECTION or SSH_TTY` — either is set by `sshd` for an interactive session.
104	
105	Why conditional rather than always-on OSC 52? OSC 52 paste is unreliable (see the terminal table above). Keeping the local provider for local sessions preserves Neovim's paste behaviour; the override only activates when `pbcopy` on the remote is clearly the wrong answer.
106	
107	### 4. Shell CLI — `x` (cross-platform clipboard wrapper)
108	
109	[`dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_x`](../../dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_x) (deployed to `~/.dotfiles/bin/x`) is a Bash wrapper with three subcommands:
110	
111	```bash
112	printf "hello" | x copy        # copy stdin to clipboard
113	x copy path/to/file            # copy file contents
114	x copy-file path/to/file       # copy file object (paste into Finder / Files)
115	x paste                        # print clipboard to stdout
116	x open https://example.com     # open URL/file in default app
117	```
118	
119	Its copy backend tries, in order: `clip.exe` (WSL) → `pbcopy` (macOS) → `wl-copy` (Wayland) → `xclip` → `xsel` → **OSC 52 fallback** writing directly to `/dev/tty`. This means `x copy` Just Works on macOS, Linux desktop, Linux SSH server, WSL, and anything else that can reach a terminal — you never have to think about which backend is available.
120	
121	`x copy-file PATH...` is intentionally separate from `x copy PATH`: it places file objects on the desktop clipboard so a file manager can paste/copy the selected files, instead of pasting the files' text contents. It uses macOS `osascript` on Finder-compatible desktops and Linux `x-special/gnome-copied-files` MIME data via `wl-copy` / `xclip` for common GTK file managers. This is local-desktop only; OSC 52 cannot carry file objects over SSH. For remote hosts, copy contents with `x copy FILE` or copy a path with `realpath FILE | x copy`.
122	
123	The OSC 52 fallback in `x` is also wrapped for tmux:
124	
125	```bash
126	if [[ -n "${TMUX:-}" ]]; then
127	  printf '\033Ptmux;\033\033]52;c;%s\033\033\\\033\\' "$data" > /dev/tty
128	else
129	  printf '\033]52;c;%s\033\\' "$data" > /dev/tty
130	fi
131	```
132	
133	The `DCS tmux; ... ST` wrapper is tmux's passthrough escape — it tells tmux "hand this sequence to the outer terminal as-is", needed because tmux otherwise intercepts OSC 52.
134	
135	## Verifying the chain works
136	
137	On the remote box where Neovim yank is misbehaving, run:
138	
139	```bash
140	# tmux: does it believe the terminal can accept OSC 52?
141	tmux info | grep -Ei 'clipboard|Ms:'
142	# expect: clipboard: true  and an Ms entry that is NOT [missing]
143	
144	# shell: can x copy reach the clipboard?
145	printf "hello from %s" "$(hostname)" | x copy
146	# then Cmd+V / Ctrl+V into a local app → should paste "hello from <remote-host>"
147	
148	# Neovim: which provider is active?
149	nvim -c ':checkhealth provider.clipboard' -c ':only'
150	# expect: OSC 52 under SSH, native under local
151	```
152	
153	If `tmux info` shows `clipboard: false` after editing `common.conf`, remember a running tmux server **keeps its old capability table** — `tmux kill-server` (losing sessions; `tmux-resurrect` can restore them) and re-attach.
154	
155	## Common failure modes
156	
157	| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
158	|---------|-------------|-----|
159	| Yank works outside tmux but vanishes inside tmux (remote) | `set-clipboard off` or server running pre-edit binary | `tmux show -g set-clipboard`; `tmux kill-server` |
160	| `tmux info` shows `Ms: [missing]` | tmux's TERM entry lacks `Ms` *and* no `terminal-features …:clipboard` declared | already handled by [`common.conf`](../../dot_config/tmux/common.conf); on an unusual outer `$TERM`, add another `set -as terminal-features` line |
161	| Ghostty asks about clipboard every yank | `clipboard-read = ask`; Ghostty interprets some writes as reads when apps immediately re-fetch | switch to `clipboard-read = allow` if you trust everything inside your sessions |
162	| Neovim yank works, but `"*p` does nothing over SSH | paste over OSC 52 not supported by outer terminal | expected — use mouse middle-click or re-type; don't fight it |
163	| `prefix+y` still copies to remote clipboard | shim binary `tmux` resolves to an old pre-`load-buffer -w` version | `tmux -V` must be ≥ 3.3 for `load-buffer -w`; this repo enforces ≥ 3.3 via ansible `devtools` role |
164	| Nested tmux (`tmux inside ssh inside tmux`) | inner tmux eats OSC 52 | inner tmux needs `set -g allow-passthrough on`; already on in this config. Double-nested cases may require `Ptmux;…` wrapping |
165	| `x copy` errors with "OSC 52 payload too large" (e.g. copying full pane scrollback over SSH) | payload exceeds the terminal's OSC 52 cap; `x copy` now refuses loudly instead of writing an escape sequence the terminal would silently drop | copy a smaller selection, or raise the cap: `X_OSC52_MAX_BYTES=<n> x copy ...` if your terminal supports more (iTerm2 ~1 MB) |
166	
167	## Design notes / non-defaults
168	
169	- **tmux `set-clipboard`** is `on`, not `external`. `external` disables tmux's own OSC 52 emission from copy-mode; `on` is a superset and keeps `prefix+[` → `y` working.
170	- **Neovim OSC 52 provider** is gated on `SSH_CONNECTION`/`SSH_TTY` rather than always-on, specifically so local paste (`"+p`) continues to work. If you primarily work over SSH and don't mind the paste tradeoff, the `if …` block can be removed.
171	- **`x` CLI ordering** prefers local backends (`pbcopy`, `wl-copy`, etc.) over OSC 52. This is intentional: when `pbcopy` is available, it's faster, doesn't touch the TTY, and works for very large payloads (OSC 52 payloads are size-limited by the terminal — iTerm2 caps at 1 MB, many others at 64-256 KB). Because OSC 52 has no delivery acknowledgment, `osc52_copy()` refuses payloads above `X_OSC52_MAX_BYTES` (default 75000 base64 chars) with an explicit error rather than writing an escape sequence the terminal would silently drop — a plain `write(2)` to `/dev/tty` succeeds either way, so without this guard `x copy` would report success even when nothing reached the clipboard.
172	
173	## Clipboard history (`cb` / `cbl` / `cbe`)
174	
175	OSC 52 covers **sync** — getting yanked text from a remote box to your local clipboard. Clipboard *history* — recalling something you copied an hour ago — is a separate concern with a separate backend, wrapped behind a unified shell API by [`dot_config/shell/56_clipboard_history.sh`](../../dot_config/shell/56_clipboard_history.sh).
176	
177	### Hybrid backend
178	
179	| OS | Backend | Install | CLI surface |
180	|----|---------|---------|------------|
181	| macOS | **Maccy** | `brew install --cask maccy` (signed, healthy on brew, auto-updating, macOS 14+) | None shipped — helper queries Maccy's plaintext SQLite directly |
182	| Ubuntu desktop | **CopyQ** | `sudo apt install copyq` (stock 22.04 / 24.04 repos; ansible role: [`gui_apps_linux`](../../dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml)) | `copyq read / select / eval / size / copy` |
183	| Ubuntu server | — | none | helper prints install hint and returns 1 |
184	
185	Why hybrid rather than CopyQ everywhere: the **CopyQ Homebrew cask** is deprecated (disabled 2026-09-01) because `CopyQ.app` is not signed for macOS Gatekeeper. Only the cask is affected — the upstream project is fine, and the Linux package is unaffected (see [hluk/CopyQ#3498](https://github.com/hluk/CopyQ/issues/3498)). Maccy is the most maintained signed-and-on-brew clipboard manager for macOS; the trade-off is no shipped CLI, so we query the plaintext SQLite at `~/Library/Application Support/Maccy/Storage.sqlite` (cask install) or `~/Library/Containers/org.p0deje.Maccy/.../Storage.sqlite` (Mac App Store sandboxed).
186	
187	### API
188	
189	| Command | Behaviour |
190	|---------|-----------|
191	| `cbl [N]` | List recent `N` clipboard items (default 20), tab-separated `<idx>\t<first-line-preview>`. Filters to UTF-8 plain text only. |
192	| `cb` | Pipe `cbl 100` to fzf → selected item is moved to the top of the stack and copied to the system clipboard. CopyQ uses `copyq select`; Maccy uses `pbcopy` (Maccy then re-records, adding a duplicate at index 0 — known quirk, not a bug). |
193	| `cbe` | Same fzf flow as `cb`, but reads the item into a tempfile, opens `$EDITOR`, then writes the edited contents back to the clipboard. |
194	
195	The first column of `cbl`'s output is:
196	- For CopyQ: the position index (`0` = top of stack)
197	- For Maccy: the SQLite `Z_PK` primary key
198	
199	This is intentional — each backend can address its own items round-trip without translation.
200	
201	### Manual backend override
202	
203	Set `CLIP_BACKEND=copyq` or `CLIP_BACKEND=maccy` to skip autodetect (useful if both are installed on the same mac and you want the more-reliable CopyQ CLI):
204	
205	```sh
206	CLIP_BACKEND=copyq cb     # one-off
207	export CLIP_BACKEND=copyq  # session
208	```
209	
210	Unknown values print a hint and return 1.
211	
212	### Coexistence with Raycast
213	
214	On macOS the new helper does **not** disable Raycast's clipboard module — both will record every `⌘C` independently. Two separate histories, no functional conflict, slight storage duplication. To disable: Raycast → Extensions → Clipboard History → toggle off.
215	
216	### Threat model — secrets in plaintext
217	
218	Both Maccy and CopyQ store unencrypted SQLite. Anything you copy from a terminal / browser / text editor as plain text (e.g. `cat .env`, an API key pasted from Slack) lands in the DB readable by your own shell.
219	
220	What is NOT recorded:
221	- macOS pasteboard items marked `org.nspasteboard.ConcealedType` / `TransientType` / `AutoGeneratedType`. 1Password, Bitwarden, KeePassXC, Keychain Access all set these — secrets pasted via those tools never enter the history.
222	- Anything copied while Maccy's "Ignore Events" toggle (`⌥`-click menu icon) or CopyQ's "Disable Clipboard Storing" is active.
223	
224	For ad-hoc secret pastes, toggle "Ignore" before pasting and toggle off after.
225	
226	### DB paths (for backup / inspection)
227	
228	- Maccy (cask): `~/Library/Application Support/Maccy/Storage.sqlite` (+ `-wal`, `-shm`)
229	- Maccy (Mac App Store): `~/Library/Containers/org.p0deje.Maccy/Data/Library/Application Support/Maccy/Storage.sqlite`
230	- CopyQ: `~/.config/copyq/` on Linux, `~/Library/Application Support/copyq/` on macOS
231	
232	The Maccy schema is documented in the [helper file's header comment](../../dot_config/shell/56_clipboard_history.sh) — verified against `p0deje/Maccy@master` source files (`HistoryItem.swift` + `HistoryItemContent.swift`).

57	# OSC 52 clipboard copy: ships stdin bytes through a terminal escape sequence.
58	# Works over SSH with no X/Wayland as long as the terminal (or tmux with
59	# set-clipboard on) forwards OSC 52. Writes to /dev/tty so it is not captured
60	# by an outer pipeline.
61	osc52_copy() {
62	    [[ -w /dev/tty ]] || return 1
63	    command -v base64 >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
64	
65	    local data
66	    data="$(base64 | tr -d '\n')"
67	    [[ -n "$data" ]] || return 0
68	
69	    local max_len="${X_OSC52_MAX_BYTES:-75000}"
70	    if (( ${#data} > max_len )); then
71	        err "OSC 52 payload too large (${#data} bytes, cap ${max_len}); most terminals silently drop larger OSC 52 sequences (64-256KB is common, iTerm2 ~1MB)"
72	        err "tip: copy a smaller selection, or raise the cap: X_OSC52_MAX_BYTES=<n> x copy ..."
73	        exit 1
74	    fi
75	
76	    if [[ -n "${TMUX:-}" ]]; then
77	        # shellcheck disable=SC1003 # printf consumes the backslash escapes.
78	        printf '\033Ptmux;\033\033]52;c;%s\033\033\\\033\\' "$data" > /dev/tty
79	    else
80	        # shellcheck disable=SC1003 # printf consumes the backslash escapes.
81	        printf '\033]52;c;%s\033\\' "$data" > /dev/tty
82	    fi
83	}

198	copy_file_macos() {
199	    command -v osascript >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
200	
201	    # JXA + NSPasteboard.writeObjects, not AppleScript's `set the clipboard to
202	    # {POSIX file p}`: the latter only writes a legacy Apple Event 'furl'
203	    # descriptor. macOS advertises public.file-url/NSFilenamesPboardType as
204	    # available on it, but only old Carbon-coercion-aware readers (Finder,
205	    # AppleScript itself) can actually resolve that promise. Modern readers
206	    # (Raycast clipboard history, Chromium/Electron incl. Discord) call
207	    # NSPasteboardItem.string(forType:) directly and get nil. writeObjects
208	    # writes a real per-file public.file-url string up front, matching what
209	    # Finder's own Cmd+C produces.
210	    if osascript -l JavaScript - "$@" <<'JXA'
211	ObjC.import("AppKit");
212	function run(argv) {
213	    var pb = $.NSPasteboard.generalPasteboard;
214	    pb.clearContents;
215	    var urls = $.NSMutableArray.alloc.init;
216	    for (var i = 0; i < argv.length; i++) {
217	        urls.addObject($.NSURL.fileURLWithPath(argv[i]));
218	    }
219	    if (!pb.writeObjects(urls)) {
220	        throw new Error("writeObjects failed");
221	    }
222	}
223	JXA
224	    then
225	        return 0
226	    fi
227	
228	    err "copy-file backend failed: osascript"
229	    exit 1
230	}

155	# correctly; legacy `Ctrl+letter` shortcuts in shells / tmux / TUIs keep
156	# their normal encodings.

158	if-shell 'tmux -V | grep -qE "tmux ([3-9]\.[5-9]|[3-9]\.[1-9][0-9]|[4-9]\.)"' \

165	# Declare OSC 52 support explicitly for common outer terminals. tmux 3.2+ only
166	# emits OSC 52 when it believes the outer terminal supports it; most modern
167	# terminals (Ghostty, Alacritty, iTerm2, kitty, WezTerm) do. Without these
168	# hints tmux falls back to terminfo's `Ms` capability, which is absent from
169	# the `tmux-256color` entry shipped by many distros, so yanks from inner
170	# apps (e.g. Neovim over SSH) silently drop.

152	# upstream older-glibc rebuild repo) when oldEL is true.
153	- name: Install Neovim tarball (user-level, no sudo required)

173	    # tags exist — no `stable` floating tag — so we fetch the latest first.

1	---
2	# =============================================================================
3	# niri — scrollable-tiling Wayland compositor (built from source)
4	#
5	# niri (https://github.com/niri-wm/niri) is not packaged in Ubuntu 24.04 apt
6	# (lands in 25.04+), so this role compiles it with cargo and installs the
7	# binary + session/systemd files so GDM (or any DM) shows "niri" as a Wayland
8	# session.
9	#
10	# Scope: Debian-family + x86_64 only. niri targets desktop GPUs; armhf/aarch64
11	# have no practical first-class story here and cargo builds are slow.
12	#
13	# No-op on:
14	#   - macOS  → no Wayland; debug note only.
15	#   - armhf / non-x86_64 → debug note only.
16	#   - noRoot → needs sudo for apt deps + /usr/local + /etc/systemd/user; the
17	#              build alone is useless without them, so the whole role skips.
18	#
19	# User config (~/.config/niri/config.kdl) is managed by chezmoi, NOT ansible —
20	# see dot_config/niri/config.kdl.tmpl. niri also writes a default config on
21	# first launch if none exists.
22	#
23	# NVIDIA: modern drivers (modeset on by default in 580+) run niri out of the
24	# box. The one upstream-recommended tweak is an application-profile that stops
25	# the driver hoarding VRAM in Wayland compositors — written below when an
26	# NVIDIA GPU is detected. See docs/playbooks/niri.md.
27	# =============================================================================
28	
29	# --- Platform / mode banners (skip paths) ------------------------------------
30	
31	- name: Announce niri is Linux-only
32	  when: ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Darwin'
33	  ansible.builtin.debug:
34	    msg: "niri is a Wayland compositor — Linux only. Skipping on macOS."
35	
36	- name: Skip niri on non-x86_64
37	  when:
38	    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
39	    - target_architecture != 'x86_64'
40	  ansible.builtin.debug:
41	    msg: >-
42	      Skipping niri on {{ target_architecture }} — this role targets x86_64
43	      desktops only (cargo builds are slow and GPU support is best on x86_64).
44	
45	- name: Skip niri in noRoot mode
46	  when:
47	    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
48	    - target_architecture == 'x86_64'
49	    - niri_no_root | default(false) | bool
50	  ansible.builtin.debug:
51	    msg: >-
52	      Skipping niri — noRoot mode has no sudo for apt build deps, /usr/local,
53	      or /etc/systemd/user. Install niri manually or grant sudo, then re-run
54	      with --tags niri.
55	
56	# Everything below runs only on Debian x86_64 with sudo available.
57	# --- Build dependencies (apt) ------------------------------------------------
58	
59	- name: Install niri build dependencies
60	  when:
61	    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
62	    - target_architecture == 'x86_64'
63	    - not (niri_no_root | default(false) | bool)
64	  become: true
65	  tags: [sudo]
66	  ansible.builtin.apt:
67	    name:
68	      - gcc
69	      - clang
70	      - libudev-dev
71	      - libgbm-dev
72	      - libxkbcommon-dev
73	      - libegl1-mesa-dev
74	      - libwayland-dev
75	      - libinput-dev
76	      - libdbus-1-dev
77	      - libsystemd-dev
78	      - libseat-dev
79	      - libpipewire-0.3-dev
80	      - libpango1.0-dev
81	      - libdisplay-info-dev
82	    state: present
83	    # Main-archive build deps covered by base's best-effort cache refresh; don't
84	    # re-run apt-get update here (a broken/flaky source would abort the play).
85	    # See pitfalls/apt-update-fails-base-role-empty-error.md.
86	    update_cache: false
87	
88	# --- Decide whether we need to (re)build -------------------------------------
89	
90	- name: Check installed niri version
91	  when:
92	    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
93	    - target_architecture == 'x86_64'
94	    - not (niri_no_root | default(false) | bool)
95	  ansible.builtin.command: niri --version
96	  register: niri_installed
97	  changed_when: false
98	  failed_when: false
99	
100	- name: Decide whether niri needs (re)building
101	  when:
102	    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
103	    - target_architecture == 'x86_64'
104	    - not (niri_no_root | default(false) | bool)
105	  ansible.builtin.set_fact:
106	    # Rebuild when niri is absent OR the installed version string does not
107	    # contain the target tag's version number (v26.04 -> "26.04").
108	    niri_needs_install: >-
109	      {{ niri_installed.rc != 0
110	         or (niri_ref | regex_replace('^v', '')) not in (niri_installed.stdout | default('')) }}
111	
112	# --- Source checkout + cargo build -------------------------------------------
113	
114	- name: Clone / update niri source at {{ niri_ref }}
115	  when:
116	    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
117	    - target_architecture == 'x86_64'
118	    - not (niri_no_root | default(false) | bool)
119	    - niri_needs_install | bool
120	  ansible.builtin.git:
121	    repo: https://github.com/niri-wm/niri.git
122	    dest: "{{ niri_build_dir }}"
123	    version: "{{ niri_ref }}"
124	    depth: 1
125	    force: true
126	
127	- name: Build niri (cargo build --release)
128	  when:
129	    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
130	    - target_architecture == 'x86_64'
131	    - not (niri_no_root | default(false) | bool)
132	    - niri_needs_install | bool
133	  # NOTE: do NOT pass --all-features — some are dev-only and cause issues
134	  # (e.g. indefinite memory growth). Upstream warns against it explicitly.
135	  ansible.builtin.command: cargo build --release --locked
136	  args:
137	    chdir: "{{ niri_build_dir }}"
138	  environment:
139	    PATH: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/share/mise/shims:{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.cargo/bin:{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin:{{ ansible_facts['env']['PATH'] }}"
140	  changed_when: true
141	  timeout: 3600
142	
143	# --- Install artifacts (binary + session + systemd) --------------------------
144	
145	- name: Ensure wayland-sessions dirs exist
146	  when:
147	    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
148	    - target_architecture == 'x86_64'
149	    - not (niri_no_root | default(false) | bool)
150	    - niri_needs_install | bool
151	  become: true
152	  tags: [sudo]
153	  ansible.builtin.file:
154	    path: "{{ item }}"
155	    state: directory
156	    mode: '0755'
157	  loop:
158	    - /usr/local/share/wayland-sessions
159	    - /usr/share/wayland-sessions
160	
161	- name: Install niri artifacts
162	  when:
163	    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
164	    - target_architecture == 'x86_64'
165	    - not (niri_no_root | default(false) | bool)
166	    - niri_needs_install | bool
167	  become: true
168	  tags: [sudo]
169	  ansible.builtin.copy:
170	    src: "{{ niri_build_dir }}/{{ item.src }}"
171	    dest: "{{ item.dest }}"
172	    mode: "{{ item.mode }}"
173	    remote_src: true
174	  loop:
175	    - { src: "target/release/niri", dest: "/usr/local/bin/niri", mode: "0755" }
176	    - { src: "resources/niri-session", dest: "/usr/local/bin/niri-session", mode: "0755" }
177	    # Install the session file to BOTH dirs: /usr/local/share is on the default
178	    # $XDG_DATA_DIRS, but some GDM setups only reliably scan /usr/share — having
179	    # both removes the "niri missing from the gear menu" doubt. Same desktop-file
180	    # ID in two dirs is de-duped by XDG precedence, so only one "Niri" shows.
181	    - { src: "resources/niri.desktop", dest: "/usr/local/share/wayland-sessions/niri.desktop", mode: "0644" }
182	    - { src: "resources/niri.desktop", dest: "/usr/share/wayland-sessions/niri.desktop", mode: "0644" }
183	    - { src: "resources/niri.service", dest: "/etc/systemd/user/niri.service", mode: "0644" }
184	    - { src: "resources/niri-shutdown.target", dest: "/etc/systemd/user/niri-shutdown.target", mode: "0644" }
185	
186	# --- Desktop usability: launcher --------------------------------------------
187	# niri boots to an empty screen; a launcher (Mod+D) is the minimum to not get
188	# stuck. fuzzel is the launcher referenced in config.kdl.
189	#
190	# The Mod+T terminal is alacritty, cargo-built by gui_apps_linux into
191	# ~/.cargo/bin — which is NOT on the GDM/systemd graphical-session PATH. That's
192	# fixed PER-USER in config.kdl's `environment { PATH … }` block (chezmoi
193	# templates the user's own $HOME in), NOT a system-wide /usr/local/bin symlink:
194	# a shared system path pointing into one user's $HOME breaks on multi-user
195	# hosts (permission-denied traversing $HOME, dangling link if that user rebuilds,
196	# and a non-root user controlling a system-PATH binary). So nothing
197	# alacritty-related happens here.
198	# (Zen/VSCode/Cursor/Discord need neither: AppImage abs-paths or /usr/bin.)
199	
200	- name: Install fuzzel (Mod+D app launcher)
201	  when:
202	    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
203	    - target_architecture == 'x86_64'
204	    - not (niri_no_root | default(false) | bool)
205	  become: true
206	  tags: [sudo]
207	  ansible.builtin.apt:
208	    name: fuzzel
209	    state: present
210	    update_cache: false
211	
212	# --- NVIDIA: cap free-buffer-pool VRAM use in Wayland compositors -------------
213	# Upstream-recommended for NVIDIA users (otherwise the driver hoards VRAM).
214	# Harmless to install even on systems whose NVIDIA card isn't the active GPU.
215	
216	- name: Detect NVIDIA GPU (kernel module loaded)
217	  when:
218	    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
219	    - target_architecture == 'x86_64'
220	    - not (niri_no_root | default(false) | bool)
221	  ansible.builtin.stat:
222	    path: /proc/driver/nvidia/version
223	  register: niri_nvidia
224	
225	- name: Ensure NVIDIA application-profiles dir exists
226	  when:
227	    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
228	    - target_architecture == 'x86_64'
229	    - not (niri_no_root | default(false) | bool)
230	    - niri_nvidia.stat.exists
231	  become: true
232	  tags: [sudo]
233	  ansible.builtin.file:
234	    path: /etc/nvidia/nvidia-application-profiles-rc.d
235	    state: directory
236	    mode: '0755'
237	
238	- name: Write NVIDIA application-profile (limit free buffer pool)
239	  when:
240	    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
241	    - target_architecture == 'x86_64'
242	    - not (niri_no_root | default(false) | bool)
243	    - niri_nvidia.stat.exists
244	  become: true
245	  tags: [sudo]
246	  ansible.builtin.copy:
247	    dest: /etc/nvidia/nvidia-application-profiles-rc.d/50-limit-free-buffer-pool-in-wayland-compositors.json
248	    mode: '0644'
249	    content: |
250	      {
251	          "rules": [
252	              {
253	                  "pattern": {
254	                      "feature": "procname",
255	                      "matches": "niri"
256	                  },
257	                  "profile": "Limit Free Buffer Pool On Wayland Compositors"
258	              }
259	          ],
260	          "profiles": [
261	              {
262	                  "name": "Limit Free Buffer Pool On Wayland Compositors",
263	                  "settings": [
264	                      {
265	                          "key": "GLVidHeapReuseRatio",
266	                          "value": 0
267	                      }
268	                  ]
269	              }
270	          ]
271	      }
272

160	#
161	#   {  / }    previous/next prompt (the prompt line itself)
162	#   M-[ / M-] previous/next command output (line AFTER the prompt — usually
163	#             what you want for "skip to the output of the previous command")
164	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
165	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} '{' send-keys -X previous-prompt
166	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} '}' send-keys -X next-prompt
167	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} M-[ send-keys -X previous-prompt -o
168	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} M-] send-keys -X next-prompt -o
169	
170	# =============================================================================
171	# Capture Pane Helpers
172	# =============================================================================
173	
174	# prefix + y: copy visible pane content to system clipboard
175	# `load-buffer -w -` loads into tmux's paste buffer AND forwards to the outer
176	# terminal via OSC 52 (requires `set-clipboard on` in common.conf). This works
177	# over SSH without shelling out to pbcopy/xclip on the remote host.
178	bind y run-shell "tmux capture-pane -p | tmux load-buffer -w - && tmux display-message 'Pane content copied to clipboard'"
179	
180	# prefix + Y: copy full scrollback to system clipboard
181	bind Y run-shell "tmux capture-pane -pS - | tmux load-buffer -w - && tmux display-message 'Full scrollback copied to clipboard'"
182	
183	# prefix + C-y: capture pane into fzf for line-by-line selection, yank chosen lines
184	bind C-y run-shell "\
185	  tmux capture-pane -pS - | fzf-tmux -p 80%,70% --multi --tac --no-sort \
186	    --header 'Select lines to copy (Tab=multi, Enter=copy)' \
187	    | tmux load-buffer -w - && tmux display-message 'Selected lines copied'"
188	
189	# prefix + C-p: copy the current pane's path (session:window.pane) to clipboard.
190	# (Capital P is taken by tmux-floax's scratchpad; lowercase p is previous-window.)
191	# Handy for reconnecting later or telling an AI agent which pane to operate on
192	# (`tmux capture-pane -pt <target>` / `tmux send-keys -t <target> ...`). Same
193	# keyboard equivalent lives in the MouseDown3Pane right-click menu and menu-pane.sh.
194	bind C-p run-shell "tmux set-buffer -w \"#{session_name}:#{window_index}.#{pane_index}\" ; tmux display-message \"Copied pane path: #{session_name}:#{window_index}.#{pane_index}\""
195	
196	# prefix + M-y: copy the LAST command's OUTPUT to clipboard (Warp-style).
197	# Requires OSC 133 markers — if the shell doesn't emit them (non-zsh shell,
198	# DISABLE_OSC133=1, or a remote bash without our hook), selection ends up
199	# empty. Chain: enter copy-mode, jump to start of previous command's output,
200	# begin selection, jump forward to the next prompt (end of output), copy,
201	# flash confirmation.
202	bind M-y copy-mode \; \
203	  send-keys -X previous-prompt -o \; \
204	  send-keys -X begin-selection \; \
205	  send-keys -X next-prompt \; \
206	  send-keys -X copy-pipe-and-cancel "tmux load-buffer -w -" \; \
207	  display-message "Last command output copied to clipboard"
208	
209	# prefix + M-i: copy the LAST command's INPUT LINE (prompt + typed command).
210	# Same dependency on OSC 133 markers. Because we don't emit the B marker
211	# (end-of-prompt), the copied text includes prompt chrome (e.g. "❯ echo hi"
212	# not just "echo hi"). Trim in the paste target if needed. Chain: enter
213	# copy-mode, jump to the previous prompt's A marker, begin selection, jump
214	# forward to the C marker (= start of output = end of input line), copy.
215	bind M-i copy-mode \; \
216	  send-keys -X previous-prompt \; \
217	  send-keys -X begin-selection \; \
218	  send-keys -X next-prompt -o \; \
219	  send-keys -X copy-pipe-and-cancel "tmux load-buffer -w -" \; \
220	  display-message "Last command input (prompt+line) copied to clipboard"
221	
222	# =============================================================================
223	# Vim-Style Pane Navigation
224	# =============================================================================

195:## What You Get
204:- `~/.config/nvim/` - Neovim (LazyVim) configuration; system clipboard via `unnamedplus`, with an SSH-conditional OSC 52 override so remote yanks reach the local clipboard (pairs with tmux `set-clipboard on`, see [docs](docs/tools/tmux/README.md#osc-52-clipboard-ssh-friendly-yank))
217:- `~/.config/ghostty/config` - Ghostty/cmux terminal config (`macos-option-as-alt` for tmux Meta keybindings, disabled ligatures, explicit `clipboard-write = allow` / `clipboard-read = ask` for OSC 52) ([docs](docs/tools/ghostty.md))
228:- `~/.tmux.conf` - Tmux configuration with TPM plugins (resurrect, continuum, tmux-floax floating pane, tmux-fzf for fuzzy keybinding/session/pane search rebound to `prefix+?`, tmux-fzf-url, tmux-open), vim-style copy mode with clipboard yank, capture-pane helpers (`prefix+y`/`Y`/`C-y`), a native popup menu (`prefix+Space` or `prefix+e`, script-driven with submenus and height-aware trimming) with layout/resize/session management, popup shell (`prefix+\``) and lazygit popup (`prefix+G`), a glow-rendered cheatsheet (`prefix+Space` → `?`), vim-style pane nav, `Ctrl+1..9` quick window switching (CSI-u terminals), extended-keys for coding agents (including `Ctrl+/` in Neovim), sesh keybindings (`prefix+g` fzf picker, `prefix+T` television picker, `prefix+O` built-in picker, `prefix+W` window picker, `prefix+S` last), responsive Catppuccin status bar (adapts modules to terminal width for mobile), and config reload on `prefix+R` ([docs](docs/tools/tmux/README.md))
229:- `~/.dotfiles/bin/x` - Cross-platform terminal wrapper for `copy` / `copy-file` / `paste` / `open`; `x copy` has an OSC 52 fallback for SSH text copy, while `x copy-file` copies desktop file objects for Finder / Files paste ([docs](docs/tools/clipboard.md))
231:- `~/.dotfiles/bin/sms` - Huawei router SMS reader (HiLink XML API; verification-code extraction, clipboard integration, TV channel) ([docs](docs/tools/sms.md))
327:- **GUI Apps on Linux** (`gui_apps` tag on `ubuntu_desktop`): [`gui_apps_linux`](dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml) bundles Alacritty (cargo, absolute-path launcher so GNOME does not hide it when `~/.cargo/bin` is absent from the session PATH), AppImageLauncher (PPA with `.deb` fallback, Lite variant for noRoot), VSCode (Microsoft apt repo), Cursor (`.deb`), Google Chrome (`.deb`, x86_64 only — Ubuntu ships no Chromium `.deb`, only a snap shim), Discord (Flatpak default or `.deb`), optional Steam via Valve apt repo when `installGamingApps=true`, Zen Browser (managed AppImage outside AppImageLauncher's watched dirs + stable `.desktop` ID), and `libfuse2` for AppImage compatibility. The role also repairs a disabled GNOME Super key and removes stale user launchers that duplicate a packaged Clash Verge. macOS equivalents ship via [`Brewfile.darwin.tmpl`](dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin.tmpl) (Arc + Discord + optional Steam casks there). See [docs/tools/appimage.md](docs/tools/appimage.md) for AppImageLauncher install paths, `ail-cli` usage, and Ubuntu 24.04 AppArmor gotchas.
328:- **niri** (optional, `installNiri=true`, `ubuntu_desktop` only): [niri](https://github.com/niri-wm/niri) scrollable-tiling Wayland compositor built from source via the [`niri`](dot_ansible/roles/niri/tasks/main.yml) ansible role (binary → `/usr/local/bin`, GDM session + systemd user units, NVIDIA VRAM application-profile when an NVIDIA GPU is present). Starter config at [`dot_config/niri/config.kdl`](dot_config/niri/config.kdl). Full guide: [docs/playbooks/niri.md](docs/playbooks/niri.md).
