<summary>Tool use: **Read**</summary>
 `./docs/tools/clipboard.md`

```text
1	# Clipboard & OSC 52
2	
3	This doc explains how clipboard sync is wired across this dotfiles setup, with a focus on **OSC 52** — the escape sequence that lets a remote SSH session put text on your **local** machine's clipboard.
4	
5	## TL;DR
6	
7	| You are… | Yank in Neovim goes to… | Capture pane (`prefix+y/Y/C-y`) goes to… |
8	|----------|--------------------------|---------------------------------------------|
9	| Local (macOS or Linux desktop) | system clipboard (default provider: `pbcopy` / `wl-copy` / `xclip`) | same, via `tmux load-buffer -w -` which emits OSC 52 *and* sets tmux's paste buffer |
10	| SSH (remote box, with or without tmux) | **local** machine's clipboard (via OSC 52) | **local** machine's clipboard (via tmux → OSC 52) |
11	
12	No extra tools, no X forwarding, no socat listener needed. The only hard requirement is a terminal emulator on your **local** machine that supports OSC 52 (Ghostty, Alacritty, iTerm2, Kitty, WezTerm — all do).
13	
14	## What is OSC 52?
15	
16	`OSC 52` is an ANSI escape sequence:
17	
18	```
19	ESC ] 52 ; c ; <base64-of-data> BEL
20	```
21	
22	Any program that can write to a terminal can emit this sequence; the terminal emulator on the other end decodes the base64 and writes it to the system clipboard. The crucial property: **escape sequences travel up the TTY back to the client terminal**, so this works transparently over SSH, mosh, and nested `tmux ssh` chains — no display server, no socket forwarding.
23	
24	Tradeoffs:
25	
26	- **Write** is ubiquitous. Most modern terminals allow it by default or with a simple opt-in.
27	- **Read** (paste from local clipboard back into remote apps) is much less supported — many terminals refuse for obvious security reasons (a malicious server could exfiltrate your clipboard). Ghostty prompts; Alacritty flat-out ignores it.
28	- A terminal multiplexer (tmux, screen, zellij) sits between the inner app and the outer terminal. It must be configured to either **emit** OSC 52 to its host terminal or **pass through** OSC 52 from inner apps.
29	- **Text only** — OSC 52 carries base64 *text*; it cannot move an **image** (or file object) from your local clipboard into a remote app, and it flows remote→local, the wrong direction for feeding a screenshot to a remote agent. Getting a local screenshot into a remote coding agent (Claude Code / Neovim) is a separate problem — see [`remote-image-paste.md`](./remote-image-paste.md).
30	
31	Reference: [tmux Clipboard wiki](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/wiki/Clipboard), [XTerm control sequences (OSC)](https://www.invisible-island.net/xterm/ctlseqs/ctlseqs.html).
32	
33	## How this repo wires it up
34	
35	Four layers cooperate. Removing any one silently breaks remote-clipboard sync.
36	
37	### 1. Terminal emulator (outer, on your local machine)
38	
39	Must accept OSC 52 writes from whatever is running inside it.
40	
41	**Ghostty / cmux** — [`dot_config/ghostty/config`](../../dot_config/ghostty/config):
42	
43	```conf
44	clipboard-write = allow   # let inner apps set the system clipboard
45	clipboard-read  = ask     # prompt before reads (safer default)
46	```
47	
48	Both match current Ghostty defaults but are pinned explicitly so policy drifts from upstream don't silently break (or weaken) this chain.
49	
50	**Alacritty** — native support, no config needed. Paste from OSC 52 not supported.
51	
52	**iTerm2 / Kitty / WezTerm** — native support. iTerm2 requires `Preferences → General → Selection → Applications in terminal may access clipboard` for reads.
53	
54	### 2. Multiplexer — tmux
55	
56	[`dot_config/tmux/common.conf`](../../dot_config/tmux/common.conf):
57	
58	```tmux
59	set -g set-clipboard on
60	
61	set -as terminal-features ",xterm*:clipboard"
62	set -as terminal-features ",ghostty*:clipboard"
63	set -as terminal-features ",alacritty*:clipboard"
64	
65	set -g allow-passthrough on
66	```
67	
68	- **`set-clipboard on`** — tmux both re-emits OSC 52 to the outer terminal when its own copy-mode yanks, and passes OSC 52 from inner apps (Neovim, less, etc.) through. `external` would only pass through; `on` is a strict superset and simpler.
69	- **`terminal-features …:clipboard`** — tells tmux the outer terminal supports OSC 52 without needing a terminfo `Ms` capability. Many distros ship a `tmux-256color` entry that lacks `Ms`, so declaring the feature directly avoids surprises when `chezmoi apply` is run on a fresh box.
70	- **`allow-passthrough on`** — lets terminal-image protocols (sixel, kitty graphics) work; also covers OSC passthrough for nested multiplexers.
71	
72	**Capture-pane helpers** — [`dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf`](../../dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf) — use the tmux-native idiom rather than shelling out:
73	
74	```tmux
75	bind y   run-shell "tmux capture-pane -p   | tmux load-buffer -w -"
76	bind Y   run-shell "tmux capture-pane -pS - | tmux load-buffer -w -"
77	bind C-y run-shell "tmux capture-pane -pS - | fzf-tmux … | tmux load-buffer -w -"
78	```
79	
80	`load-buffer -w -` reads stdin into tmux's paste buffer *and* (because of `-w`) forwards to the system clipboard via OSC 52. Previously these bindings used a `pbcopy | xclip | xsel` fallback chain that only worked locally — over SSH they copied to the **remote** machine's clipboard, which is useless. The tmux-native form works identically in both places.
81	
82	`set-buffer -w …` offers the same `-w` flag but takes data as an argument, which introduces shell-quoting landmines on multi-line pane content; `load-buffer -w -` reads stdin and sidesteps that.
83	
84	### 3. Editor — Neovim
85	
86	[`dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua`](../../dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua):
87	
88	```lua
89	vim.opt.clipboard = "unnamedplus"
90	
91	if vim.env.SSH_CONNECTION or vim.env.SSH_TTY then
92	  local osc52 = require("vim.ui.clipboard.osc52")
93	  vim.g.clipboard = {
94	    name = "OSC 52",
95	    copy  = { ["+"] = osc52.copy("+"),  ["*"] = osc52.copy("*")  },
96	    paste = { ["+"] = osc52.paste("+"), ["*"] = osc52.paste("*") },
97	  }
98	end
99	```
100	
101	- Locally, LazyVim's default provider is used (`pbcopy`/`xclip`/`wl-copy` — with working paste).
102	- Over SSH, Neovim's built-in `vim.ui.clipboard.osc52` (shipping since Neovim 0.10) emits OSC 52 directly, bypassing any `pbcopy` binary on the remote host.
103	- The check is `SSH_CONNECTION or SSH_TTY` — either is set by `sshd` for an interactive session.
104	
105	Why conditional rather than always-on OSC 52? OSC 52 paste is unreliable (see the terminal table above). Keeping the local provider for local sessions preserves Neovim's paste behaviour; the override only activates when `pbcopy` on the remote is clearly the wrong answer.
106	
107	### 4. Shell CLI — `x` (cross-platform clipboard wrapper)
108	
109	[`dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_x`](../../dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_x) (deployed to `~/.dotfiles/bin/x`) is a Bash wrapper with three subcommands:
110	
111	```bash
112	printf "hello" | x copy        # copy stdin to clipboard
113	x copy path/to/file            # copy file contents
114	x copy-file path/to/file       # copy file object (paste into Finder / Files)
115	x paste                        # print clipboard to stdout
116	x open https://example.com     # open URL/file in default app
117	```
118	
119	Its copy backend tries, in order: `clip.exe` (WSL) → `pbcopy` (macOS) → `wl-copy` (Wayland) → `xclip` → `xsel` → **OSC 52 fallback** writing directly to `/dev/tty`. This means `x copy` Just Works on macOS, Linux desktop, Linux SSH server, WSL, and anything else that can reach a terminal — you never have to think about which backend is available.
120	
121	`x copy-file PATH...` is intentionally separate from `x copy PATH`: it places file objects on the desktop clipboard so a file manager can paste/copy the selected files, instead of pasting the files' text contents. It uses macOS `osascript` on Finder-compatible desktops and Linux `x-special/gnome-copied-files` MIME data via `wl-copy` / `xclip` for common GTK file managers. This is local-desktop only; OSC 52 cannot carry file objects over SSH. For remote hosts, copy contents with `x copy FILE` or copy a path with `realpath FILE | x copy`.
122	
123	The OSC 52 fallback in `x` is also wrapped for tmux:
124	
125	```bash
126	if [[ -n "${TMUX:-}" ]]; then
127	  printf '\033Ptmux;\033\033]52;c;%s\033\033\\\033\\' "$data" > /dev/tty
128	else
129	  printf '\033]52;c;%s\033\\' "$data" > /dev/tty
130	fi
131	```
132	
133	The `DCS tmux; ... ST` wrapper is tmux's passthrough escape — it tells tmux "hand this sequence to the outer terminal as-is", needed because tmux otherwise intercepts OSC 52.
134	
135	## Verifying the chain works
136	
137	On the remote box where Neovim yank is misbehaving, run:
138	
139	```bash
140	# tmux: does it believe the terminal can accept OSC 52?
141	tmux info | grep -Ei 'clipboard|Ms:'
142	# expect: clipboard: true  and an Ms entry that is NOT [missing]
143	
144	# shell: can x copy reach the clipboard?
145	printf "hello from %s" "$(hostname)" | x copy
146	# then Cmd+V / Ctrl+V into a local app → should paste "hello from <remote-host>"
147	
148	# Neovim: which provider is active?
149	nvim -c ':checkhealth provider.clipboard' -c ':only'
150	# expect: OSC 52 under SSH, native under local
151	```
152	
153	If `tmux info` shows `clipboard: false` after editing `common.conf`, remember a running tmux server **keeps its old capability table** — `tmux kill-server` (losing sessions; `tmux-resurrect` can restore them) and re-attach.
154	
155	## Common failure modes
156	
157	| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
158	|---------|-------------|-----|
159	| Yank works outside tmux but vanishes inside tmux (remote) | `set-clipboard off` or server running pre-edit binary | `tmux show -g set-clipboard`; `tmux kill-server` |
160	| `tmux info` shows `Ms: [missing]` | tmux's TERM entry lacks `Ms` *and* no `terminal-features …:clipboard` declared | already handled by [`common.conf`](../../dot_config/tmux/common.conf); on an unusual outer `$TERM`, add another `set -as terminal-features` line |
161	| Ghostty asks about clipboard every yank | `clipboard-read = ask`; Ghostty interprets some writes as reads when apps immediately re-fetch | switch to `clipboard-read = allow` if you trust everything inside your sessions |
162	| Neovim yank works, but `"*p` does nothing over SSH | paste over OSC 52 not supported by outer terminal | expected — use mouse middle-click or re-type; don't fight it |
163	| `prefix+y` still copies to remote clipboard | shim binary `tmux` resolves to an old pre-`load-buffer -w` version | `tmux -V` must be ≥ 3.3 for `load-buffer -w`; this repo enforces ≥ 3.3 via ansible `devtools` role |
164	| Nested tmux (`tmux inside ssh inside tmux`) | inner tmux eats OSC 52 | inner tmux needs `set -g allow-passthrough on`; already on in this config. Double-nested cases may require `Ptmux;…` wrapping |
165	| `x copy` errors with "OSC 52 payload too large" (e.g. copying full pane scrollback over SSH) | payload exceeds the terminal's OSC 52 cap; `x copy` now refuses loudly instead of writing an escape sequence the terminal would silently drop | copy a smaller selection, or raise the cap: `X_OSC52_MAX_BYTES=<n> x copy ...` if your terminal supports more (iTerm2 ~1 MB) |
166	
167	## Design notes / non-defaults
168	
169	- **tmux `set-clipboard`** is `on`, not `external`. `external` disables tmux's own OSC 52 emission from copy-mode; `on` is a superset and keeps `prefix+[` → `y` working.
170	- **Neovim OSC 52 provider** is gated on `SSH_CONNECTION`/`SSH_TTY` rather than always-on, specifically so local paste (`"+p`) continues to work. If you primarily work over SSH and don't mind the paste tradeoff, the `if …` block can be removed.
171	- **`x` CLI ordering** prefers local backends (`pbcopy`, `wl-copy`, etc.) over OSC 52. This is intentional: when `pbcopy` is available, it's faster, doesn't touch the TTY, and works for very large payloads (OSC 52 payloads are size-limited by the terminal — iTerm2 caps at 1 MB, many others at 64-256 KB). Because OSC 52 has no delivery acknowledgment, `osc52_copy()` refuses payloads above `X_OSC52_MAX_BYTES` (default 75000 base64 chars) with an explicit error rather than writing an escape sequence the terminal would silently drop — a plain `write(2)` to `/dev/tty` succeeds either way, so without this guard `x copy` would report success even when nothing reached the clipboard.
172	
173	## Clipboard history (`cb` / `cbl` / `cbe`)
174	
175	OSC 52 covers **sync** — getting yanked text from a remote box to your local clipboard. Clipboard *history* — recalling something you copied an hour ago — is a separate concern with a separate backend, wrapped behind a unified shell API by [`dot_config/shell/56_clipboard_history.sh`](../../dot_config/shell/56_clipboard_history.sh).
176	
177	### Hybrid backend
178	
179	| OS | Backend | Install | CLI surface |
180	|----|---------|---------|------------|
181	| macOS | **Maccy** | `brew install --cask maccy` (signed, healthy on brew, auto-updating, macOS 14+) | None shipped — helper queries Maccy's plaintext SQLite directly |
182	| Ubuntu desktop | **CopyQ** | `sudo apt install copyq` (stock 22.04 / 24.04 repos; ansible role: [`gui_apps_linux`](../../dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml)) | `copyq read / select / eval / size / copy` |
183	| Ubuntu server | — | none | helper prints install hint and returns 1 |
184	
185	Why hybrid rather than CopyQ everywhere: the **CopyQ Homebrew cask** is deprecated (disabled 2026-09-01) because `CopyQ.app` is not signed for macOS Gatekeeper. Only the cask is affected — the upstream project is fine, and the Linux package is unaffected (see [hluk/CopyQ#3498](https://github.com/hluk/CopyQ/issues/3498)). Maccy is the most maintained signed-and-on-brew clipboard manager for macOS; the trade-off is no shipped CLI, so we query the plaintext SQLite at `~/Library/Application Support/Maccy/Storage.sqlite` (cask install) or `~/Library/Containers/org.p0deje.Maccy/.../Storage.sqlite` (Mac App Store sandboxed).
186	
187	### API
188	
189	| Command | Behaviour |
190	|---------|-----------|
191	| `cbl [N]` | List recent `N` clipboard items (default 20), tab-separated `<idx>\t<first-line-preview>`. Filters to UTF-8 plain text only. |
192	| `cb` | Pipe `cbl 100` to fzf → selected item is moved to the top of the stack and copied to the system clipboard. CopyQ uses `copyq select`; Maccy uses `pbcopy` (Maccy then re-records, adding a duplicate at index 0 — known quirk, not a bug). |
193	| `cbe` | Same fzf flow as `cb`, but reads the item into a tempfile, opens `$EDITOR`, then writes the edited contents back to the clipboard. |
194	
195	The first column of `cbl`'s output is:
196	- For CopyQ: the position index (`0` = top of stack)
197	- For Maccy: the SQLite `Z_PK` primary key
198	
199	This is intentional — each backend can address its own items round-trip without translation.
200	
201	### Manual backend override
202	
203	Set `CLIP_BACKEND=copyq` or `CLIP_BACKEND=maccy` to skip autodetect (useful if both are installed on the same mac and you want the more-reliable CopyQ CLI):
204	
205	```sh
206	CLIP_BACKEND=copyq cb     # one-off
207	export CLIP_BACKEND=copyq  # session
208	```
209	
210	Unknown values print a hint and return 1.
211	
212	### Coexistence with Raycast
213	
214	On macOS the new helper does **not** disable Raycast's clipboard module — both will record every `⌘C` independently. Two separate histories, no functional conflict, slight storage duplication. To disable: Raycast → Extensions → Clipboard History → toggle off.
215	
216	### Threat model — secrets in plaintext
217	
218	Both Maccy and CopyQ store unencrypted SQLite. Anything you copy from a terminal / browser / text editor as plain text (e.g. `cat .env`, an API key pasted from Slack) lands in the DB readable by your own shell.
219	
220	What is NOT recorded:
221	- macOS pasteboard items marked `org.nspasteboard.ConcealedType` / `TransientType` / `AutoGeneratedType`. 1Password, Bitwarden, KeePassXC, Keychain Access all set these — secrets pasted via those tools never enter the history.
222	- Anything copied while Maccy's "Ignore Events" toggle (`⌥`-click menu icon) or CopyQ's "Disable Clipboard Storing" is active.
223	
224	For ad-hoc secret pastes, toggle "Ignore" before pasting and toggle off after.
225	
226	### DB paths (for backup / inspection)
227	
228	- Maccy (cask): `~/Library/Application Support/Maccy/Storage.sqlite` (+ `-wal`, `-shm`)
229	- Maccy (Mac App Store): `~/Library/Containers/org.p0deje.Maccy/Data/Library/Application Support/Maccy/Storage.sqlite`
230	- CopyQ: `~/.config/copyq/` on Linux, `~/Library/Application Support/copyq/` on macOS
231	
232	The Maccy schema is documented in the [helper file's header comment](../../dot_config/shell/56_clipboard_history.sh) — verified against `p0deje/Maccy@master` source files (`HistoryItem.swift` + `HistoryItemContent.swift`).
233	
234	## Related docs

237	- [tmux](./tmux/README.md) — "OSC 52 Clipboard (SSH-friendly yank)" section
238	- [Ghostty](./ghostty.md) — terminal-side notes
239	- [`dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_x`](../../dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_x) — the `x` wrapper source

241

244	- [tmux Clipboard wiki](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/wiki/Clipboard)
245	- [Neovim `:help clipboard-osc52`](https://neovim.io/doc/user/provider.html#clipboard-osc52)
246	- [XTerm OSC 52 spec](https://www.invisible-island.net/xterm/ctlseqs/ctlseqs.html#h3-Operating-System-Commands)
247

# 49_x_completion.zsh - tab completion for `x` (clipboard / open helper).
# Source CLI: dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_x (bash hand-rolled subcommand parser).
# Loaded eagerly by load_modular_dir AFTER compinit in dot_zshrc.tmpl, so
# `compdef _x x` is safe.

(( $+commands[x] )) || return 0

_x() {
    local context state state_descr line
    typeset -A opt_args

    _arguments -C \
        '1: :->subcommand' \
        '*::arg:->args'

    case "$state" in
        subcommand)
            local -a subs=(
                'copy:Copy stdin or FILE to system clipboard'
                'copy-file:Copy file objects to the desktop clipboard'

3	# Wraps Maccy (macOS, plaintext SQLite) and CopyQ (Linux, shipped CLI) behind
4	# a unified `cb` / `cbl` / `cbe` API. Replaces the Raycast-specific helper
5	# deleted in 2026-05 — Raycast 1.7+ encrypts its DB with SQLCipher and the
6	# key cannot be recovered without binary RE; see
7	# pitfalls/raycast-clipboard-sqlcipher-key-not-recoverable.md.
8	#
9	# Backend selection (override autodetect with CLIP_BACKEND=copyq|maccy):
10	#   macOS:  prefer Maccy SQLite, fall back to CopyQ if installed manually.
11	#   Linux:  CopyQ only.
12	# No backend → one-line install hint to stderr (ubuntu_server typical case).
13	#
14	# Maccy schema (verified against p0deje/Maccy@master HistoryItem.swift +
15	# HistoryItemContent.swift, 2026-05):
16	#   ZHISTORYITEM(Z_PK, ZAPPLICATION, ZFIRSTCOPIEDAT, ZLASTCOPIEDAT,
17	#                ZNUMBEROFCOPIES, ZPIN, ZTITLE)
18	#   ZHISTORYITEMCONTENT(Z_PK, ZTYPE, ZVALUE, ZITEM -> ZHISTORYITEM.Z_PK)
19	# Core Data dates are seconds since 2001-01-01; add 978307200 for Unix epoch.
20	
21	# ---- backend detection -----------------------------------------------------
22	
23	_clip_maccy_path() {
24	    p="$HOME/Library/Application Support/Maccy/Storage.sqlite"
25	    [ -f "$p" ] && { printf 'maccy:%s\n' "$p"; return 0; }
26	    p="$HOME/Library/Containers/org.p0deje.Maccy/Data/Library/Application Support/Maccy/Storage.sqlite"
27	    [ -f "$p" ] && { printf 'maccy:%s\n' "$p"; return 0; }
28	    return 1
29	}
30	
31	_clip_copyq_ready() {
32	    command -v copyq >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
33	    copyq size >/dev/null 2>&1
34	}
35	
36	_clip_backend() {
37	    case "${CLIP_BACKEND:-}" in
38	        copyq) _clip_copyq_ready && echo copyq ;;
39	        maccy) _clip_maccy_path ;;
40	        '')
41	            if [ "$(uname)" = "Darwin" ]; then
42	                _clip_maccy_path && return 0
43	                _clip_copyq_ready && echo copyq
44	            else
45	                _clip_copyq_ready && echo copyq
46	            fi
47	            ;;
48	        *)
49	            printf 'clipboard-history: unknown CLIP_BACKEND=%s (expected: copyq|maccy)\n' "$CLIP_BACKEND" >&2
50	            return 1
51	            ;;
52	    esac
53	}
54	
55	_clip_hint() {
56	    cat >&2 <<'HINT'
57	clipboard-history: no backend found.
58	
59	  macOS:  brew install --cask maccy   (then launch once from Spotlight)
60	  Linux:  sudo apt install copyq      (autostarts on next X session)
61	
62	See docs/tools/clipboard.md → Clipboard History.
63	HINT
64	}
65	
66	_clip_is_uint() {
67	    case "$1" in
68	        '' | *[!0-9]*) return 1 ;;
69	        *) return 0 ;;
70	    esac
71	}
72	
73	# ---- cbl: list recent N items (tab-separated <idx>\t<first-line>) ----------
74	
75	cbl() {
76	    n=${1:-20}
77	    if ! _clip_is_uint "$n"; then
78	        echo "cbl: argument must be a positive integer (got: $n)" >&2
79	        return 1
80	    fi
81	    b=$(_clip_backend) || { _clip_hint; return 1; }
82	    case "$b" in
83	        copyq)
84	            copyq eval "
85	                var n = Math.min(size(), $n);
86	                for (var i = 0; i < n; i++) {
87	                    var line = read(i).split('\n')[0];
88	                    if (line.length > 0) print(i + '\t' + line + '\n');
89	                }
90	            "
91	            ;;
92	        maccy:*)
93	            db=${b#maccy:}
94	            sqlite3 -readonly -batch "$db" <<SQL
95	.mode tabs
96	.headers off
97	SELECT Z.Z_PK,
98	       substr(replace(CAST(C.ZVALUE AS TEXT), char(10), ' '), 1, 200)
99	FROM ZHISTORYITEM Z
100	JOIN ZHISTORYITEMCONTENT C ON C.ZITEM = Z.Z_PK
101	WHERE C.ZTYPE = 'public.utf8-plain-text'
102	ORDER BY Z.ZLASTCOPIEDAT DESC
103	LIMIT $n;
104	SQL
105	            ;;
106	    esac
107	}
108	
109	# ---- cb: fzf-pick a clip → copy to system clipboard ------------------------
110	
111	cb() {
112	    command -v fzf >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "cb: fzf not found" >&2; return 1; }
113	    b=$(_clip_backend) || { _clip_hint; return 1; }
114	    sel=$(cbl 100 | fzf --no-multi --with-nth=2.. --delimiter='	' --prompt='clip> ') || return 1
115	    idx=$(printf '%s\n' "$sel" | cut -f1)
116	    _clip_is_uint "$idx" || { echo "cb: bad index from fzf: $idx" >&2; return 1; }
117	    case "$b" in
118	        copyq)
119	            copyq select "$idx"
120	            ;;
121	        maccy:*)
122	            db=${b#maccy:}
123	            sqlite3 -readonly -batch "$db" \
124	                "SELECT CAST(ZVALUE AS TEXT) FROM ZHISTORYITEMCONTENT \
125	                 WHERE ZITEM=$idx AND ZTYPE='public.utf8-plain-text' LIMIT 1;" \
126	                | pbcopy
127	            ;;
128	    esac
129	}
130	
131	# ---- cbe: fzf-pick → edit in $EDITOR → write back to clipboard -------------
132	
133	cbe() {
134	    command -v fzf >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "cbe: fzf not found" >&2; return 1; }
135	    b=$(_clip_backend) || { _clip_hint; return 1; }
136	    sel=$(cbl 100 | fzf --no-multi --with-nth=2.. --delimiter='	' --prompt='cb-edit> ') || return 1
137	    idx=$(printf '%s\n' "$sel" | cut -f1)
138	    _clip_is_uint "$idx" || { echo "cbe: bad index from fzf: $idx" >&2; return 1; }
139	    tmp=$(mktemp -t clipedit.XXXXXX) || return 1
140	    case "$b" in
141	        copyq)
142	            copyq read "$idx" > "$tmp"
143	            ;;
144	        maccy:*)
145	            db=${b#maccy:}
146	            sqlite3 -readonly -batch "$db" \
147	                "SELECT CAST(ZVALUE AS TEXT) FROM ZHISTORYITEMCONTENT \
148	                 WHERE ZITEM=$idx AND ZTYPE='public.utf8-plain-text' LIMIT 1;" \
149	                > "$tmp"
150	            ;;
151	    esac
152	    ${EDITOR:-nvim} "$tmp"
153	    if [ -s "$tmp" ]; then
154	        case "$b" in
155	            copyq)  copyq copy - < "$tmp" ;;
156	            maccy:*) pbcopy < "$tmp" ;;
157	        esac
158	    fi
159	    rm -f "$tmp"
160	}
161

clipboard.md
clipboard.zh-TW.md
---
# Clipboard & OSC 52

This doc explains how clipboard sync is wired across this dotfiles setup, with a focus on **OSC 52** — the escape sequence that lets a remote SSH session put text on your **local** machine's clipboard.

## TL;DR

| You are… | Yank in Neovim goes to… | Capture pane (`prefix+y/Y/C-y`) goes to… |
|----------|--------------------------|---------------------------------------------|
| Local (macOS or Linux desktop) | system clipboard (default provider: `pbcopy` / `wl-copy` / `xclip`) | same, via `tmux load-buffer -w -` which emits OSC 52 *and* sets tmux's paste buffer |
| SSH (remote box, with or without tmux) | **local** machine's clipboard (via OSC 52) | **local** machine's clipboard (via tmux → OSC 52) |

No extra tools, no X forwarding, no socat listener needed. The only hard requirement is a terminal emulator on your **local** machine that supports OSC 52 (Ghostty, Alacritty, iTerm2, Kitty, WezTerm — all do).

## What is OSC 52?

`OSC 52` is an ANSI escape sequence:

```
ESC ] 52 ; c ; <base64-of-data> BEL
```

Any program that can write to a terminal can emit this sequence; the terminal emulator on the other end decodes the base64 and writes it to the system clipboard. The crucial property: **escape sequences travel up the TTY back to the client terminal**, so this works transparently over SSH, mosh, and nested `tmux ssh` chains — no display server, no socket forwarding.

Tradeoffs:

- **Write** is ubiquitous. Most modern terminals allow it by default or with a simple opt-in.
- **Read** (paste from local clipboard back into remote apps) is much less supported — many terminals refuse for obvious security reasons (a malicious server could exfiltrate your clipboard). Ghostty prompts; Alacritty flat-out ignores it.
- A terminal multiplexer (tmux, screen, zellij) sits between the inner app and the outer terminal. It must be configured to either **emit** OSC 52 to its host terminal or **pass through** OSC 52 from inner apps.
- **Text only** — OSC 52 carries base64 *text*; it cannot move an **image** (or file object) from your local clipboard into a remote app, and it flows remote→local, the wrong direction for feeding a screenshot to a remote agent. Getting a local screenshot into a remote coding agent (Claude Code / Neovim) is a separate problem — see [`remote-image-paste.md`](./remote-image-paste.md).

Reference: [tmux Clipboard wiki](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/wiki/Clipboard), [XTerm control sequences (OSC)](https://www.invisible-island.net/xterm/ctlseqs/ctlseqs.html).

## How this repo wires it up

Four layers cooperate. Removing any one silently breaks remote-clipboard sync.

### 1. Terminal emulator (outer, on your local machine)

Must accept OSC 52 writes from whatever is running inside it.

**Ghostty / cmux** — [`dot_config/ghostty/config`](../../dot_config/ghostty/config):

```conf
clipboard-write = allow   # let inner apps set the system clipboard
clipboard-read  = ask     # prompt before reads (safer default)
```

Both match current Ghostty defaults but are pinned explicitly so policy drifts from upstream don't silently break (or weaken) this chain.

**Alacritty** — native support, no config needed. Paste from OSC 52 not supported.

**iTerm2 / Kitty / WezTerm** — native support. iTerm2 requires `Preferences → General → Selection → Applications in terminal may access clipboard` for reads.

### 2. Multiplexer — tmux

[`dot_config/tmux/common.conf`](../../dot_config/tmux/common.conf):

```tmux
set -g set-clipboard on

set -as terminal-features ",xterm*:clipboard"
set -as terminal-features ",ghostty*:clipboard"
set -as terminal-features ",alacritty*:clipboard"

set -g allow-passthrough on
```

- **`set-clipboard on`** — tmux both re-emits OSC 52 to the outer terminal when its own copy-mode yanks, and passes OSC 52 from inner apps (Neovim, less, etc.) through. `external` would only pass through; `on` is a strict superset and simpler.
- **`terminal-features …:clipboard`** — tells tmux the outer terminal supports OSC 52 without needing a terminfo `Ms` capability. Many distros ship a `tmux-256color` entry that lacks `Ms`, so declaring the feature directly avoids surprises when `chezmoi apply` is run on a fresh box.
- **`allow-passthrough on`** — lets terminal-image protocols (sixel, kitty graphics) work; also covers OSC passthrough for nested multiplexers.

**Capture-pane helpers** — [`dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf`](../../dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf) — use the tmux-native idiom rather than shelling out:

```tmux
bind y   run-shell "tmux capture-pane -p   | tmux load-buffer -w -"
bind Y   run-shell "tmux capture-pane -pS - | tmux load-buffer -w -"
bind C-y run-shell "tmux capture-pane -pS - | fzf-tmux … | tmux load-buffer -w -"
```

`load-buffer -w -` reads stdin into tmux's paste buffer *and* (because of `-w`) forwards to the system clipboard via OSC 52. Previously these bindings used a `pbcopy | xclip | xsel` fallback chain that only worked locally — over SSH they copied to the **remote** machine's clipboard, which is useless. The tmux-native form works identically in both places.
```

This is intentional: when `pbcopy` is available, it's faster, doesn't touch the TTY, and works for very large payloads (OSC 52 payloads are size-limited by the terminal — iTerm2 caps at 1 MB, many others at 64-256 KB). Because OSC 52 has no delivery acknowledgment, `osc52_copy()` refuses payloads above `X_OSC52_MAX_BYTES` (default 75000 base64 chars) with an explicit error rather than writing an escape sequence the terminal would silently drop — a plain `write(2)` to `/dev/tty` succeeds either way, so without this guard `x copy` would report success even when nothing reached the clipboard.
181:| macOS | **Maccy** | `brew install --cask maccy` (signed, healthy on brew, auto-updating, macOS 14+) | None shipped — helper queries Maccy's plaintext SQLite directly |
182:| Ubuntu desktop | **CopyQ** | `sudo apt install copyq` (stock 22.04 / 24.04 repos; ansible role: [`gui_apps_linux`](../../dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml)) | `copyq read / select / eval / size / copy` |
183:| Ubuntu server | — | none | helper prints install hint and returns 1 |
185:Why hybrid rather than CopyQ everywhere: the **CopyQ Homebrew cask** is deprecated (disabled 2026-09-01) because `CopyQ.app` is not signed for macOS Gatekeeper. Only the cask is affected — the upstream project is fine, and the Linux package is unaffected (see [hluk/CopyQ#3498](https://github.com/hluk/CopyQ/issues/3498)). Maccy is the most maintained signed-and-on-brew clipboard manager for macOS; the trade-off is no shipped CLI, so we query the plaintext SQLite at `~/Library/Application Support/Maccy/Storage.sqlite` (cask install) or `~/Library/Containers/org.p0deje.Maccy/.../Storage.sqlite` (Mac App Store sandboxed).
203:Set `CLIP_BACKEND=copyq` or `CLIP_BACKEND=maccy` to skip autodetect (useful if both are installed on the same mac and you want the more-reliable CopyQ CLI):
245:- [Neovim `:help clipboard-osc52`](https://neovim.io/doc/user/provider.html#clipboard-osc52)
```

1	# 56_clipboard_history.sh — cross-platform clipboard-history helpers.
2	#
3	# Wraps Maccy (macOS, plaintext SQLite) and CopyQ (Linux, shipped CLI) behind
4	# a unified `cb` / `cbl` / `cbe` API. Replaces the Raycast-specific helper
5	# deleted in 2026-05 — Raycast 1.7+ encrypts its DB with SQLCipher and the
6	# key cannot be recovered without binary RE; see
7	# pitfalls/raycast-clipboard-sqlcipher-key-not-recoverable.md.
8	#
9	# Backend selection (override autodetect with CLIP_BACKEND=copyq|maccy):
10	#   macOS:  prefer Maccy SQLite, fall back to CopyQ if installed manually.
11	#   Linux:  CopyQ only.
12	# No backend → one-line install hint to stderr (ubuntu_server typical case).
13	#
14	# Maccy schema (verified against p0deje/Maccy@master HistoryItem.swift +
15	# HistoryItemContent.swift, 2026-05):
16	#   ZHISTORYITEM(Z_PK, ZAPPLICATION, ZFIRSTCOPIEDAT, ZLASTCOPIEDAT,
17	#                ZNUMBEROFCOPIES, ZPIN, ZTITLE)
18	#   ZHISTORYITEMCONTENT(Z_PK, ZTYPE, ZVALUE, ZITEM -> ZHISTORYITEM.Z_PK)
19	# Core Data dates are seconds since 2001-01-01; add 978307200 for Unix epoch.
20	
21	# ---- backend detection -----------------------------------------------------
22	
23	_clip_maccy_path() {
24	    p="$HOME/Library/Application Support/Maccy/Storage.sqlite"
25	    [ -f "$p" ] && { printf 'maccy:%s\n' "$p"; return 0; }
26	    p="$HOME/Library/Containers/org.p0deje.Maccy/Data/Library/Application Support/Maccy/Storage.sqlite"
27	    [ -f "$p" ] && { printf 'maccy:%s\n' "$p"; return 0; }
28	    return 1
29	}
30	
31	_clip_copyq_ready() {
32	    command -v copyq >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
33	    copyq size >/dev/null 2>&1
34	}
35	
36	_clip_backend() {
37	    case "${CLIP_BACKEND:-}" in
38	        copyq) _clip_copyq_ready && echo copyq ;;
39	        maccy) _clip_maccy_path ;;
40	        '')
41	            if [ "$(uname)" = "Darwin" ]; then
42	                _clip_maccy_path && return 0
43	                _clip_copyq_ready && echo copyq
44	            else
45	                _clip_copyq_ready && echo copyq
46	            fi
47	            ;;
48	        *)
49	            printf 'clipboard-history: unknown CLIP_BACKEND=%s (expected: copyq|maccy)\n' "$CLIP_BACKEND" >&2
50	            return 1
51	            ;;
52	    esac
53	}
54	
55	_clip_hint() {
56	    cat >&2 <<'HINT'
57	clipboard-history: no backend found.
58	
59	  macOS:  brew install --cask maccy   (then launch once from Spotlight)
60	  Linux:  sudo apt install copyq      (autostarts on next X session)
61	
62	See docs/tools/clipboard.md → Clipboard History.
63	HINT
64	}
65	
66	_clip_is_uint() {
67	    case "$1" in
68	        '' | *[!0-9]*) return 1 ;;
69	        *) return 0 ;;
70	    esac
```

29	  become: true
30	  tags: [sudo]
31	  ansible.builtin.apt:
32	    update_cache: true
33	    cache_valid_time: 3600
34	  register: base_apt_cache
35	  ignore_errors: true
36	
37	# The apt module swallows the underlying fetch errors (empty msg above), so
38	# re-run `apt-get update` via CLI purely to surface WHICH source is broken.
39	- name: Diagnose broken apt sources (cache update failed)
40	  when:
41	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
42	    - base_apt_cache is failed
43	  become: true
44	  tags: [sudo]
45	  ansible.builtin.command: apt-get update
46	  register: base_apt_diag
47	  changed_when: false
48	  failed_when: false
49	
50	# `Err:` lines (which repo) land on stdout, `E:`/`W:` summaries on stderr.
51	# msg is a list so each broken source renders on its own output line.
52	- name: Report broken apt sources
53	  when:
54	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
55	    - base_apt_cache is failed
56	  tags: [sudo]

58	    base_apt_broken_lines: >-
59	      {{ base_apt_diag.stdout_lines | default([]) | select('match', '^(Err|Ign):.*') | list
60	         + base_apt_diag.stderr_lines | default([]) }}
61	  ansible.builtin.debug:

121	  # Jinja2 templating in ansible reads `${#...}` as a comment block
122	  # (`{# ... #}` in Jinja syntax) and aborts with "unbalanced jinja2 block".
123	  # `${missing[*]:-}` expands to space-joined elements (empty when unset)
124	  # so `[ -z ... ]` cleanly tests "any missing packages" without `{#`.
125	  ansible.builtin.shell: |
126	    set -e
127	    missing=()
128	    for p in git git-lfs curl wget jq tree gcc gcc-c++ make rsync; do
129	      rpm -q "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing+=("$p")
130	    done
131	    if [ -z "${missing[*]:-}" ]; then
132	      echo "ALL_INSTALLED"
133	      exit 0
134	    fi
135	    yum install -y "${missing[@]}"
136	  args:
137	    executable: /bin/bash
138	  register: base_yum_result
139	  changed_when: "'ALL_INSTALLED' not in base_yum_result.stdout"
140	  ignore_errors: true

# =============================================================================
# gui_apps_linux — Ubuntu/Debian desktop GUI app installer
#
# Handles the "desktop-only" category of apps that aren't in the apt default
# repos: Alacritty (cargo), AppImageLauncher (PPA / .deb / Lite), VSCode
# (Microsoft apt repo), Cursor (.deb with graceful fallback), Google Chrome
# (.deb, x86_64-only), Discord (.deb,
# x86_64-only), Steam (Valve apt repo, optional), Zen Browser (AppImage +
# .desktop), libfuse2 (AppImage runtime on Ubuntu 22.04+), and a placeholder
# hook for Antigravity once an official Linux package ships.
#
# No-op on:
#   - macOS  → Brewfile (`cask "alacritty"`, `cask "visual-studio-code"` when
#              you add them) covers the desktop story. This role emits a
#              debug note only on Darwin, no install logic runs.
#   - armhf  → 32-bit ARM has no practical GUI story; cargo builds are slow
#              and AppImages lack first-class armv7 support.
#   - noRoot → `--skip-tags sudo` (set by run_onchange) skips every system
#              apt/deb/PPA task. AppImageLauncher Lite (user-level AppImage)
#              still runs when `gui_apps_linux_no_root=true` is passed via
#              `--extra-vars`.
#
# Editor user-config overlays (settings.json / keybindings.json) are handled
# by chezmoi itself, NOT ansible — see `.chezmoitemplates/editor/` and the
# `modify_settings.json.tmpl` / `create_keybindings.json.tmpl` source files.
#
# Adding a new GUI app: read docs/playbooks/linux-gui-apps.md FIRST. It
# contains the .deb / Snap / Flatpak / AppImage decision tree, the
# "concrete patterns" you'd copy here, and the inventory table you must
# also update so the doc stays in sync with this role.
# =============================================================================

# --- Platform banner ---

- name: Announce gui_apps_linux is Linux-only (macOS uses Brewfile)
  when: ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Darwin'
  ansible.builtin.debug:
    msg: >-
      gui_apps_linux is Linux-only. macOS GUI apps are declared in
      dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin.tmpl (alacritty cask, etc.).

- name: Skip gui_apps_linux on armhf
  when:
    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
    - target_architecture == 'armv7l'
  ansible.builtin.debug:
    msg: >-
      Skipping gui_apps_linux on armhf — no practical GUI stack,
      cargo builds of alacritty are very slow, and upstream AppImages
      do not target armv7.

# =============================================================================
# Alacritty (moved verbatim from the former alacritty role)
# =============================================================================

- name: Install Alacritty build dependencies
  when:
    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
    - target_architecture != 'armv7l'

# Neovim role - install Neovim with version check

- name: Check current Neovim version
  ansible.builtin.shell: nvim --version 2>/dev/null | head -1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+'
  register: nvim_version_check
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false

  ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    nvim_current_version: "{{ nvim_version_check.stdout | default('0.0.0', true) | trim or '0.0.0' }}"

- name: Display current Neovim version
  ansible.builtin.debug:
    msg: "Current Neovim version: {{ nvim_current_version }} (required: >= {{ neovim_min_version }})"

# macOS - use Homebrew
- name: Install Neovim (macOS)
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
  community.general.homebrew:
    name: neovim
    state: latest

# Linux - apt baseline, GitHub release tarball when apt is too old.
# Deliberately NO snap: snaps auto-refresh outside the explicit
# `just upgrade-*` path (violates the install/upgrade split), pollute
# $HOME with ~/snap, and the repo policy keeps snapd off servers —
# see docs/linux-package-sources.md "snap in this repo".
- name: Install Neovim from apt (Debian/Ubuntu)
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
  become: true
  tags: [sudo]
  ansible.builtin.apt:
    name: neovim
    state: present
  register: apt_neovim

- name: Check Neovim version after apt install
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian" and apt_neovim is defined and apt_neovim is succeeded

---
# Linux playbook - Ubuntu/Debian setup
- name: Linux setup
  hosts: local
  gather_facts: true

  pre_tasks:
    # RPi 4 can run a 64-bit kernel (aarch64) with 32-bit userland (armhf).
    # ansible_facts['architecture'] reflects the kernel, which leads to
    # downloading aarch64 binaries that cannot execute.  Detect the real
    # userland architecture and expose it as target_architecture for all roles.
    # Note: set_fact cannot reliably override ansible_facts['architecture']
    # when inject_facts_as_vars=False, so we use a dedicated variable instead.
    - name: Detect userland architecture via dpkg
      ansible.builtin.command: dpkg --print-architecture
      register: dpkg_arch_result
      changed_when: false
      failed_when: false
      tags: [always]

    - name: Set target_architecture from dpkg
      ansible.builtin.set_fact:
        target_architecture: >-
          {{ {'amd64': 'x86_64', 'arm64': 'aarch64', 'armhf': 'armv7l', 'armel': 'armv6l', 'i386': 'i686'}
             [dpkg_arch_result.stdout | trim]
             | default(ansible_facts['architecture']) }}
      when: dpkg_arch_result.rc == 0 and dpkg_arch_result.stdout | trim != ''
      tags: [always]

    - name: Fallback target_architecture to gathered facts
      ansible.builtin.set_fact:
        target_architecture: "{{ ansible_facts['architecture'] }}"
      when: target_architecture is not defined
      tags: [always]

    # Mirrors $oldEL in dot_config/mise/config.toml.tmpl (lines 8-19).
    # CentOS/RHEL 7 ship glibc 2.17; mise's [tools] omits node and rust there
    # (Node 18+/Bun musl/.NET refuse to load; rustup TUNA mirror GCs old
    # versions). Roles use `not (oldEL | default(false))` to skip
    # `mise exec -- npm` and `mise install rust@latest` on this baseline.
    - name: Detect CentOS/RHEL 7 baseline (oldEL)
      ansible.builtin.set_fact:
        oldEL: >-
          {{ ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'RedHat'
             and (ansible_facts['distribution_major_version'] | string) == '7' }}
      tags: [always]

  roles:
    - role: base
      tags: [base]
```

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-08-28 09:46:17Z)**_

I've confirmed the root cause directly on this machine and am waiting for two background exploration agents to map the doc mirrors. Quick summary of what I've found so far:

- **This is a Wayland session** (`niri` compositor) with **zero clipboard CLIs installed** — no `wl-clipboard`, `xclip`, or `xsel`. All three are apt-available.
- **No ansible role installs any of them.** `gui_apps_linux` installs `copyq` (a clipboard *manager* daemon) + `playerctl`/`wmctrl`/`xdotool`, but not the low-level `wl-copy`/`xclip` binaries that lazygit and Neovim shell out to.
- **lazygit Ctrl+O** fails because it looks for `xsel`/`xclip`/`wl-clipboard` specifically.
- **Neovim** `dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua` sets `clipboard = "unnamedplus"` and only overrides to OSC 52 when `SSH_CONNECTION` is set — so locally, with no provider binary present, yanks silently don't reach the system clipboard. Your suspicion is correct; same root cause.
- `docs/tools/clipboard.md` already *assumes* `wl-copy`/`xclip` exist locally ("default provider: pbcopy / wl-copy / xclip") but there's no install story backing that.
- `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_x` already handles Wayland (`wl-copy` → `xclip` → `xsel` → OSC 52 fallback) — it just needs one of those binaries present too.

I'll finalize the plan once the agents report back on README / tool-managers / aliases mirror details.

### 1. Neovim clipboard config

**File: `/home/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua`** — this is the only place `vim.opt.clipboard` / `vim.g.clipboard` is set. Full file (lines 1-20):

```lua
-- Options are automatically loaded before lazy.nvim startup
-- Default options that are always set: https://github.com/LazyVim/LazyVim/blob/main/lua/lazyvim/config/options.lua
-- Add any additional options here

-- System clipboard integration for yank/paste
vim.opt.clipboard = "unnamedplus"

-- Over SSH, route the + / * registers through OSC 52 so yanks land in the
-- LOCAL terminal's clipboard. Without this, the default provider shells out
-- to pbcopy/xclip on the REMOTE host, which is useless for pasting locally.
-- Locally (no SSH), keep LazyVim's default provider so paste also works.
if vim.env.SSH_CONNECTION or vim.env.SSH_TTY then
  local osc52 = require("vim.ui.clipboard.osc52")
  vim.g.clipboard = {
    name = "OSC 52",
    copy = { ["+"] = osc52.copy("+"), ["*"] = osc52.copy("*") },
    paste = { ["+"] = osc52.paste("+"), ["*"] = osc52.paste("*") },
  }
end
```

**NON-SSH (local Ubuntu desktop) case:** The `if` block is skipped entirely, so `vim.g.clipboard` is never set. Neovim falls back to its built-in clipboard-provider autodetection, which shells out to an external binary in this priority order: `wl-copy`/`wl-paste` (wl-clipboard, Wayland) → `xclip` → `xsel` (X11) → others. With only `vim.opt.clipboard = "unnamedplus"` set and no provider binary present, yank/paste to the system clipboard silently does nothing and `:checkhealth provider.clipboard` reports "No clipboard tool found". Note: Neovim has no `+clipboard` build flag (that's Vim); Neovim clipboard support is purely runtime provider-binary detection.

No nvim plugin or other lua file references clipboard (only `dot_config/nvim/lua/exact_plugins/avante.lua:50` mentions `xclip` in a comment about image paste, unrelated).

**File: `/home/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/tmux/common.conf.tmpl`** lines 162-176:

```tmux
# OSC 52 clipboard (works over SSH)
set -g set-clipboard on

# Declare OSC 52 support explicitly for common outer terminals. tmux 3.2+ only
# emits OSC 52 when it believes the outer terminal supports it; most modern
# terminals (Ghostty, Alacritty, iTerm2, kitty, WezTerm) do. Without these
# hints tmux falls back to terminfo's `Ms` capability, which is absent from
# the `tmux-256color` entry shipped by many distros, so yanks from inner
# apps (e.g. Neovim over SSH) silently drop.
set -as terminal-features ",xterm*:clipboard"
set -as terminal-features ",ghostty*:clipboard"
set -as terminal-features ",alacritty*:clipboard"

# Allow OSC passthrough (for terminal images, sixel, etc.)
set -g allow-passthrough on
```

So yes — `set-clipboard on` plus explicit `terminal-features …:clipboard` hints plus `allow-passthrough on` are already present. This means an inner Neovim OSC 52 write passes through tmux to the outer terminal.

144:# shell: can x copy reach the clipboard?
145:printf "hello from %s" "$(hostname)" | x copy
165:| `x copy` errors with "OSC 52 payload too large" (e.g. copying full pane scrollback over SSH) | payload exceeds the terminal's OSC 52 cap; `x copy` now refuses loudly instead of writing an escape sequence the terminal would silently drop | copy a smaller selection, or raise the cap: `X_OSC52_MAX_BYTES=<n> x copy ...` if your terminal supports more (iTerm2 ~1 MB) |
171:- **`x` CLI ordering** prefers local backends (`pbcopy`, `wl-copy`, etc.) over OSC 52. This is intentional: when `pbcopy` is available, it's faster, doesn't touch the TTY, and works for very large payloads (OSC 52 payloads are size-limited by the terminal — iTerm2 caps at 1 MB, many others at 64-256 KB). Because OSC 52 has no delivery acknowledgment, `osc52_copy()` refuses payloads above `X_OSC52_MAX_BYTES` (default 75000 base64 chars) with an explicit error rather than writing an escape sequence the terminal would silently drop — a plain `write(2)` to `/dev/tty` succeeds either way, so without this guard `x copy` would report success even when nothing reached the clipboard.
---
### 4. Shell CLI — `x` (cross-platform clipboard wrapper)

[`dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_x`](../../dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_x) (deployed to `~/.dotfiles/bin/x`) is a Bash wrapper with three subcommands:

```bash
printf "hello" | x copy        # copy stdin to clipboard
x copy path/to/file            # copy file contents
x copy-file path/to/file       # copy file object (paste into Finder / Files)
x paste                        # print clipboard to stdout
x open https://example.com     # open URL/file in default app
```

Its copy backend tries, in order: `clip.exe` (WSL) → `pbcopy` (macOS) → `wl-copy` (Wayland) → `xclip` → `xsel` → **OSC 52 fallback** writing directly to `/dev/tty`. This means `x copy` Just Works on macOS, Linux desktop, Linux SSH server, WSL, and anything else that can reach a terminal — you never have to think about which backend is available.

`x copy-file PATH...` is intentionally separate from `x copy PATH`: it places file objects on the desktop clipboard so a file manager can paste/copy the selected files, instead of pasting the files' text contents. It uses macOS `osascript` on Finder-compatible desktops and Linux `x-special/gnome-copied-files` MIME data via `wl-copy` / `xclip` for common GTK file managers. This is local-desktop only; OSC 52 cannot carry file objects over SSH. For remote hosts, copy contents with `x copy FILE` or copy a path with `realpath FILE | x copy`.

The OSC 52 fallback in `x` is also wrapped for tmux:

```bash
if [[ -n "${TMUX:-}" ]]; then
  printf '\033Ptmux;\033\033]52;c;%s\033\033\\\033\\' "$data" > /dev/tty
else
  printf '\033]52;c;%s\033\\' "$data" > /dev/tty
fi
```

The `DCS tmux; ... ST` wrapper is tmux's passthrough escape — it tells tmux "hand this sequence to the outer terminal as-is", needed because tmux otherwise intercepts OSC 52.

# Clipboard utilities in the chezmoi repo — investigation report

## 1. Where clipboard tools are installed (ansible / Brewfile / task lists)

**The only ansible role that installs anything clipboard-related is `gui_apps_linux`:**

`dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml`

- **Lines 1158–1184 — CopyQ** (clipboard *manager*, ships its own `copyq` CLI):
  ```yaml
  # CopyQ — clipboard manager with scriptable CLI (`copyq read/select/eval/...`)
  # Stock Ubuntu apt repos ship copyq on 22.04 ...
  - name: Install CopyQ via apt (stock repos)
    when:
      - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
      - target_architecture != 'armv7l'
    become: true
    tags: [sudo]
    ansible.builtin.apt:
      name: copyq
      state: present
      update_cache: false
  ```
- **Lines 1185–1215 — `playerctl`, `wmctrl`, `xdotool`** (app-control, not clipboard proper):
  ```yaml
  - name: Install app-control CLI utilities (playerctl, wmctrl, xdotool)
    when:
      - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
      - target_architecture != 'armv7l'
    become: true
    tags: [sudo, app_control]
    ansible.builtin.apt:
      name:
        - playerctl
        - wmctrl
        - xdotool
      state: present
  ```
  The header comment (lines 1193–1196) explicitly notes `wmctrl`/`xdotool` are "X11 window control. No-op on Wayland".

**`xclip`, `xsel`, `wl-clipboard` / `wl-copy` / `wl-paste` are installed by NOTHING.** Repo-wide grep of `dot_ansible/` returns zero install tasks for any of them. They appear only as *strings* inside `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_x` (backend probe list) and in docs.

**Brewfiles:**
- `dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin.tmpl:54` — `cask "maccy"` (clipboard history; macOS has `pbcopy`/`pbpaste` built in).
- `dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.tmpl` and `dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.linux.tmpl` — nothing clipboard-related.

**Platform / profile gating:**
`.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl`
- Line 221 (`ubuntu_desktop`): `TAGS="...,gui_apps"` → CopyQ + xdotool/wmctrl/playerctl get installed.
- Line 225 (`ubuntu_server`) and line 234 (`centos_server`): no `gui_apps` tag → **no clipboard tooling at all**.
- niri gate — line 318: `{{ if and $installNiri (eq .chezmoi.os "linux") (eq .profile "ubuntu_desktop") }}`.

`dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml` itself is entirely `os_family == 'Debian'` gated and no-ops on macOS (lines 36–41) and armhf (lines 43–51).

### The gap (confirmed)

| Scenario | What gets installed | `x copy` / nvim `unnamedplus` backend available? |
|---|---|---|
| **Linux X11 desktop** (`ubuntu_desktop`, no niri) | `copyq`, `xdotool`, `wmctrl` | **No `xclip`, no `xsel`.** CopyQ's daemon doesn't satisfy `x`'s backend chain or Neovim's clipboard provider. Falls through to OSC 52 (needs terminal support) |
| **Linux Wayland desktop** (`installNiri=true`) | `fuzzel` (niri role line 200), `copyq`, `xdotool` | **No `wl-clipboard`.** `niri` role (`dot_ansible/roles/niri/tasks/main.yml`) installs build deps + `fuzzel` only — never `wl-clipboard`. `x copy` on a fresh niri session has only the OSC 52 fallback; `x copy-file` (needs `wl-copy`) has no backend at all |
| **Linux server** (`ubuntu_server`) | nothing | OSC 52 only — which is the correct/only answer for headless, so arguably not a gap |

So yes: **a Linux desktop (X11 or Wayland) never gets a real clipboard CLI (`xclip`/`xsel`/`wl-clipboard`) installed.** Local Neovim `clipboard=unnamedplus` yanks and local `x copy` both silently degrade to OSC 52 (or fail for `x copy-file`).

## 2. How Linux packages are installed / where a clipboard util belongs

Role load order: `dot_ansible/playbooks/linux.yml` (roles listed lines 49+), tag-selected by the `TAGS` string in `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl`.

Relevant roles (each `dot_ansible/roles/<name>/tasks/main.yml`):
- `base` — apt bootstrap, cache, `python3-debian`, keyrings.
- `devtools` — the large cross-platform CLI bundle (bat/eza/fzf/tmux/yazi/…), apt + Linuxbrew. tmux ≥ 3.3 enforcement lives here (`dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` ~lines 2705–2820). **No clipboard tools.**
- `lazyvim_deps` — Neovim/LazyVim runtime deps. **No clipboard provider (`xclip`/`wl-clipboard`) installed** despite `dot_config/nvim` using `unnamedplus`.
- `gui_apps_linux` — desktop GUI apps + CopyQ + xdotool/wmctrl/playerctl. `ubuntu_desktop` only.
- `niri` — Wayland compositor from source + `fuzzel`. `installNiri` + `ubuntu_desktop` only.
- `media_control`, `media_tools` — playerctl (brew side), mpv, etc.

**Natural home for a clipboard CLI:**
- X11/Wayland clipboard CLIs (`xclip`, `xsel`, `wl-clipboard`) for a desktop → **`gui_apps_linux`**, right next to the existing CopyQ / app-control tasks (`dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml:1174–1215`). Same `Debian` + `!= armv7l` + `tags: [sudo]` guard already in place.
- Wayland `wl-clipboard` specifically → **`niri`** role beside the `fuzzel` install (`dot_ansible/roles/niri/tasks/main.yml:200–210`), since niri is the only Wayland surface in the repo and its `config.kdl.tmpl` has no clipboard manager.
- If a local clipboard provider is also wanted for headless-with-X-forwarding or for Neovim parity → **`lazyvim_deps`** or **`devtools`** (cross-platform bundle).

# Lazygit Clipboard Command Configuration

## Placeholder Syntax

The exact placeholder for `os.copyToClipboardCmd` is `{{text}}`. The documentation does not explicitly state whether lazygit shell-escapes or quotes the text before substitution.

## Documentation Quote

"Specify an external command to invoke when copying to clipboard is requested. `{{text}}` will be replaced by text to be copied."

## Example Commands

The documentation provides several example implementations:

**Basic OSC52:**
```yaml
os:
  copyToClipboardCmd: printf "\033]52;c;$(printf {{text}} | base64 -w 0)\a" > /dev/tty
```

**Tmux with passthrough:**
```yaml
os:
  copyToClipboardCmd: printf "\033Ptmux;\033\033]52;c;$(printf {{text}} | base64 -w 0)\a\033\\" > /dev/tty
```

**Smart tmux/non-tmux detection:**
Uses conditional logic to detect the terminal type and apply the appropriate escape sequence.

## os.readFromClipboardCmd

The documentation confirms this setting exists: "A custom command for reading from the clipboard can be set using `os.readFromClipboardCmd: ''`". It's used when pasting commit messages and should output clipboard content to stdout.
```

# ResolvePlaceholderString Analysis

The function performs **plain string replacement without any escaping or shell-quoting**. Here's the relevant code:

```go
func ResolvePlaceholderString(str string, arguments map[string]string) string {
    oldnews := make([]string, 0, len(arguments)*4)
    for key, value := range arguments {
        oldnews = append(oldnews,
            "{{"+key+"}}", value,
            "{{."+key+"}}", value,
        )
    }
    return strings.NewReplacer(oldnews...).Replace(str)
}
```

The implementation uses Go's `strings.NewReplacer()` to directly substitute template placeholders (like `{{key}}` and `{{.key}}`) with corresponding values. No sanitization, escaping, or shell-quoting occurs—values are inserted as-is into the resulting string.
```

# Clipboard Utility Selection Logic

The code checks **only** the `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` environment variable, not `DISPLAY`. Here's the selection order:

1. **Wayland** (if `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` is set): wl-clipboard
2. **xclip**
3. **xsel**
4. **Termux** (Android)
5. **Windows** (powershell + clip.exe)

The init() function verbatim order of preference:

```go
if os.Getenv("WAYLAND_DISPLAY") != "" {
    // Try wl-copy and wl-paste
}
// Try xclip
// Try xsel
// Try termux
// Try powershell + clip.exe
```

Each utility is checked using `exec.LookPath()` to verify availability before settling on it as the default for that system.
```

# Plan: install Linux clipboard CLIs (fix lazygit Ctrl+O + nvim yank)

## Context

On this Ubuntu desktop (Wayland / `niri`), lazygit `Ctrl+O` fails with
`No clipboard utilities available. Please install xsel, xclip, wl-clipboard …`
and Neovim yanks (`clipboard = "unnamedplus"`) silently never reach the
system clipboard. Same root cause for both.

**Root cause:** no ansible role installs `wl-clipboard`, `xclip`, or `xsel`.
`gui_apps_linux` installs CopyQ (a clipboard *manager* daemon — its `copyq`
CLI is not what lazygit/nvim/`x` shell out to) plus `playerctl`/`wmctrl`/
`xdotool`, but never the low-level clipboard binaries. Consequences on a
local Linux desktop:

- **lazygit** — its vendored `atotto/clipboard` looks for `wl-clipboard`
  (when `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` is set) → `xclip` → `xsel`; none exist → error.
- **Neovim** — `dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua` only overrides to
  OSC 52 when `SSH_CONNECTION`/`SSH_TTY` is set. Locally it relies on the
  built-in provider auto-detect (`wl-copy` / `xclip` / `xsel`) → no binary
  → yank is a silent no-op.
- **`x` CLI** (`dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_x`) — `copy_backend` /
  `paste_backend` fall through to the OSC 52-only path locally, and
  `x copy-file` has *no* backend (needs `wl-copy` or `xclip`).

The repo's own `docs/tools/clipboard.md` already *assumes* `wl-copy`/`xclip`
exist locally ("default provider: `pbcopy` / `wl-copy` / `xclip`") with no
install story behind it.

**Intended outcome:** `chezmoi apply` on an Ubuntu desktop installs
`wl-clipboard` + `xclip`, after which lazygit `Ctrl+O`, Neovim yank, and
`x copy` / `x copy-file` all work natively with no per-app config. Docs
stop lying about a provider that isn't installed.

## Approach

### 1. Install the clipboard CLIs — `dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml`

Add one apt task next to the existing CopyQ / app-control block
(after ~line 1215), same guard as its neighbours
(`os_family == 'Debian'`, `target_architecture != 'armv7l'`,
`become: true`, `tags: [sudo]`):

```yaml
# =============================================================================
# Clipboard CLIs — the low-level binaries lazygit (Ctrl+O), Neovim
# (clipboard=unnamedplus), and `~/.dotfiles/bin/x` shell out to. CopyQ above
# is a history *manager*, not one of these.
#
#   - wl-clipboard  wl-copy/wl-paste — native Wayland (niri sessions). Both
#                   nvim's provider and atotto/clipboard (lazygit) prefer it
#                   when $WAYLAND_DISPLAY is set.
#   - xclip         X11 / XWayland fallback. atotto checks xclip before xsel,
#                   so xsel is not needed; omitted to keep the set minimal.
#
# Server profiles deliberately don't get these — headless has no clipboard;
# OSC 52 (tmux `set-clipboard on` + `x`'s /dev/tty fallback) is the answer
# there.
# =============================================================================

- name: Install clipboard CLIs (wl-clipboard, xclip)
  when:
    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
    - target_architecture != 'armv7l'
  become: true
  tags: [sudo]
  ansible.builtin.apt:
    name:
      - wl-clipboard
      - xclip
    state: present
    update_cache: false
```

No change to `dot_config/nvim/**` or `dot_config/lazygit/config.yml` — once
a backend binary exists, both work. Neovim's SSH→OSC 52 branch is unaffected.
`x` needs no change; it already probes `wl-copy` → `xclip` → `xsel` → OSC 52.

### 2. (Pending decision) SSH lazygit `Ctrl+O` routed through `x`

Over SSH, lazygit's native copy targets the *remote* clipboard (useless).
Optional: add to `dot_config/lazygit/config.yml`

```yaml
os:
  copyToClipboardCmd: printf '%s' {{text}} | x copy
```

so `Ctrl+O` uses `x`'s backend chain (local wl-copy/xclip, OSC 52 over SSH).
Caveat: lazygit does **not** shell-quote `{{text}}`
(`utils.ResolvePlaceholderString` is a plain `strings.Replacer`), so text
with spaces / quotes / newlines can break the command. lazygit's own docs
accept this fragility for their OSC 52 recipe. **See question to user.**

### 3. Doc mirrors (same commit — CLAUDE.md cross-file rules)

Tool index (A–Z): new rows `wl-clipboard` / `xclip` (macOS `n/a` — pbcopy built-in; Linux `apt`; role `gui_apps_linux`). Upgrade-automation list (~L977): append to the `playerctl / wmctrl / xdotool` "apt-upgrade" row. |
| `docs/this_repo/tool-managers.zh-TW.md` | mirror all of the above. |

| `docs/tools/clipboard.md` + `.zh-TW.md` | §"How this repo wires it up" / the `x` section: state that `wl-clipboard` + `xclip` are installed by `gui_apps_linux` on desktop profiles (currently the doc implies the provider just exists). Fix the TL;DR "default provider" line to point at the install. If #2 is adopted, add a lazygit note. |
| `README.md` | "What You Get" gui_apps_linux bundle line (~L327): add "clipboard CLIs (wl-clipboard, xclip)". (Line is already stale re CopyQ/xdotool — optionally fold those in too.) |

### 4. New pitfall — `pitfalls/lazygit-ctrl-o-no-clipboard-utilities-nvim-yank-silent.md`

Symptom-titled. Verbatim error string
(`No clipboard utilities available. Please install xsel, xclip, wl-clipboard or Termux:API …`),
the paired nvim-yank-silent symptom, root cause (no role installed the

install wl-clipboard xclip` as the manual one-liner), and the

Add the index line in `pitfalls/README.md`.

   - `nvim` → `yy` on a line → `:checkhealth provider.clipboard` shows
     `wl-copy`/`wl-paste`; paste into another app works.
   - lazygit → `Ctrl+O` on a commit hash → no error, hash in clipboard.
   - `printf hi | x copy && x paste` → `hi`; `x copy-file /etc/hostname`
     no longer errors.
5. `pre-commit run --files <changed>` (shellcheck/shfmt/markdown, redact hook).

## Out of scope

- Server profiles (`ubuntu_server` / `centos_server`) — OSC 52 only, by design.
- The pre-existing "no `x` CLI row in tool-managers Tool index" gap — note it,

```text
# CopyToClipboard Analysis

## The Function

```go
func (c *OSCommand) CopyToClipboard(str string) error {
	escaped := strings.ReplaceAll(str, "\n", "\\n")
	truncated := utils.TruncateWithEllipsis(escaped, 40)

	msg := utils.ResolvePlaceholderString(
		c.Tr.Log.CopyToClipboard,
		map[string]string{
			"str": truncated,
		},
	)
	c.LogCommand(msg, false)
	if c.UserConfig().OS.CopyToClipboardCmd != "" {
		cmdStr := utils.ResolvePlaceholderString(c.UserConfig().OS.CopyToClipboardCmd, map[string]string{
			"text": c.Cmd.Quote(str),
		})
		return c.Cmd.NewShell(cmdStr, c.UserConfig().OS.ShellFunctionsFile).Run()
	}

	return clipboard.WriteAll(str)
}
```

## Key Findings

**Quoting:** Yes—the text is shell-quoted via `c.Cmd.Quote(str)` before substitution into the command template.

**Execution:** The resulting command executes through `c.Cmd.NewShell(cmdStr, ...).Run()`, which appears to invoke a shell with the command string.

**PasteFromClipboard** uses the same `NewShell(...).RunWithOutput()` pattern for reading from the clipboard via custom commands.
```

## Approved Plan:
# Plan: install Linux clipboard CLIs (fix lazygit Ctrl+O + nvim yank)

## Context

On this Ubuntu desktop (Wayland / `niri`), lazygit `Ctrl+O` fails with
`No clipboard utilities available. Please install xsel, xclip, wl-clipboard …`
and Neovim yanks (`clipboard = "unnamedplus"`) silently never reach the
system clipboard. Same root cause for both.

**Root cause:** no ansible role installs `wl-clipboard`, `xclip`, or `xsel`.
`gui_apps_linux` installs CopyQ (a clipboard *manager* daemon — its `copyq`
CLI is not what lazygit/nvim/`x` shell out to) plus `playerctl`/`wmctrl`/
`xdotool`, but never the low-level clipboard binaries. Consequences on a
local Linux desktop:

- **lazygit** — its vendored `atotto/clipboard` looks for `wl-clipboard`
  (when `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` is set) → `xclip` → `xsel`; none exist → error.
- **Neovim** — `dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua` only overrides to
  OSC 52 when `SSH_CONNECTION`/`SSH_TTY` is set. Locally it relies on the
  built-in provider auto-detect (`wl-copy` / `xclip` / `xsel`) → no binary
  → yank is a silent no-op.
- **`x` CLI** (`dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_x`) — `copy_backend` /
  `paste_backend` fall through to the OSC 52-only path locally, and
  `x copy-file` has *no* backend (needs `wl-copy` or `xclip`).

The repo's own `docs/tools/clipboard.md` already *assumes* `wl-copy`/`xclip`
exist locally ("default provider: `pbcopy` / `wl-copy` / `xclip`") with no
install story behind it.

**Intended outcome:** `chezmoi apply` on an Ubuntu desktop installs
`wl-clipboard` + `xclip` + `xsel`, after which Neovim yank and
`x copy` / `x copy-file` work natively, and lazygit `Ctrl+O` is routed
through `x copy` (works local *and* over SSH). Docs stop implying a
provider that isn't installed.

## Approach

### 1. Install the clipboard CLIs — `dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml`

Add one apt task next to the existing CopyQ / app-control block
(after ~line 1215), same guard as its neighbours
(`os_family == 'Debian'`, `target_architecture != 'armv7l'`,
`become: true`, `tags: [sudo]`). Install **`wl-clipboard` + `xclip` +
`xsel`** (xsel included to match lazygit's error text and `x`'s full
backend list):

```yaml
# =============================================================================
# Clipboard CLIs — the low-level binaries lazygit (Ctrl+O), Neovim
# (clipboard=unnamedplus), and `~/.dotfiles/bin/x` shell out to. CopyQ above
# is a history *manager*, not one of these.
#
#   - wl-clipboard  wl-copy/wl-paste — native Wayland (niri sessions). Both
#                   nvim's provider and atotto/clipboard (lazygit) prefer it
#                   when $WAYLAND_DISPLAY is set.
#   - xclip         X11 / XWayland fallback (also `x paste` / nvim on X11).
#   - xsel          named in lazygit's own error text; `x`'s last non-OSC-52
#                   backend. Redundant with xclip for lazygit but ~40KB.
#
# Server profiles deliberately don't get these — headless has no clipboard;
# OSC 52 (tmux `set-clipboard on` + `x`'s /dev/tty fallback) is the answer
# there.
# =============================================================================

- name: Install clipboard CLIs (wl-clipboard, xclip, xsel)
  when:
    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
    - target_architecture != 'armv7l'
  become: true
  tags: [sudo]
  ansible.builtin.apt:
    name:
      - wl-clipboard
      - xclip
      - xsel
    state: present
    update_cache: false
```

No change to `dot_config/nvim/**` — once a backend binary exists it works,
and Neovim's SSH→OSC 52 branch is unaffected. `x` needs no change; it
already probes `wl-copy` → `xclip` → `xsel` → OSC 52.

### 2. Route lazygit `Ctrl+O` through `x` — `dot_config/lazygit/config.yml`

Add an `os:` block:

```yaml
os:
  copyToClipboardCmd: printf '%s' {{text}} | x copy
```

`Ctrl+O` then uses `x`'s backend chain: `wl-copy`/`xclip` locally, OSC 52
(`/dev/tty`, tmux-passthrough-wrapped) over SSH — so it copies to the
*local* clipboard from remote hosts too, unlike lazygit's native path.

**This is safe**, contrary to first read: lazygit shell-quotes the text via
`c.Cmd.Quote(str)` *before* substituting `{{text}}`
(`OSCommand.CopyToClipboard` in `pkg/commands/oscommands/os.go`), then runs
the result through `NewShell`. So `{{text}}` expands to an already-quoted
token (`'my commit subject'`, `$'a\nb'` for newlines); our static `'%s'`
format guards against a leading-dash payload. Only the built-in
`clipboard.WriteAll` path (used when `copyToClipboardCmd` is empty) is
unquoted-stdin — we're replacing it.

Leave `readFromClipboardCmd` unset (native lib is fine for the rare
paste-into-commit-description case; `x paste` can't read over SSH anyway).

**PATH note:** `x` resolves via `$HOME/.dotfiles/bin` on PATH
(`dot_config/shell/00_exports.sh.tmpl`), which covers every normal launch
(shell alias `lg`, tmux `prefix+G`, nvim). A lazygit spawned *directly* by
niri wouldn't have that dir on PATH (niri's `environment.PATH` omits it) —
if that path matters, use `printf '%s' {{text}} | "$HOME/.dotfiles/bin/x" copy`
instead. Decide during implementation; default to bare `x`.

### 3. Doc mirrors (same commit — CLAUDE.md cross-file rules)

| File | Edit |
|---|---|
| `docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md` | § role table (~L424) + apt-deps table (~L854): add `wl-clipboard`, `xclip`, `xsel` to the `gui_apps_linux` rows. Tool index (A–Z): new rows `wl-clipboard` / `xclip` / `xsel` (macOS `n/a` — pbcopy built-in; Linux `apt`; role `gui_apps_linux`). Upgrade-automation list (~L977): append to the `playerctl / wmctrl / xdotool` "apt-upgrade" row. |
| `docs/this_repo/tool-managers.zh-TW.md` | mirror all of the above. |
| `docs/playbooks/linux-gui-apps.md` | Inventory table (~L86, by the CopyQ row): add a row for the clipboard CLIs (`wl-clipboard` / `xclip` / `xsel`; apt; `gui_apps_linux`; gated `profile=ubuntu_desktop` via tag selection). |
| `docs/tools/clipboard.md` + `.zh-TW.md` | §"How this repo wires it up" / the `x` section: state that `wl-clipboard` + `xclip` + `xsel` are installed by `gui_apps_linux` on desktop profiles (the doc currently implies the provider just exists). Fix the TL;DR "default provider" line to point at the install. Add a short "lazygit" note: `Ctrl+O` routed through `x copy` via `os.copyToClipboardCmd`. |
| `docs/tools/git_diff_workflow.md` | ~L16: note the `config.yml` `os.copyToClipboardCmd` addition alongside the existing `git.pagers`/delta mention. |
| `docs/shells/aliases.md` | `lg` row (~L81): no change needed (alias unchanged); optionally footnote that `Ctrl+O` copies via `x`. |
| `README.md` | "What You Get" gui_apps_linux bundle line (~L327): add "clipboard CLIs (wl-clipboard, xclip, xsel)". (Line is already stale re CopyQ/xdotool — optionally fold those in too.) |

### 4. New pitfall — `pitfalls/lazygit-ctrl-o-no-clipboard-utilities-nvim-yank-silent.md`

Symptom-titled. Verbatim error string
(`No clipboard utilities available. Please install xsel, xclip, wl-clipboard or Termux:API …`),
the paired nvim-yank-silent symptom, root cause (no role installed the
binaries; CopyQ ≠ these), fix (`gui_apps_linux` now installs them; `sudo apt
install wl-clipboard xclip xsel` as the manual one-liner), and the
`:checkhealth provider.clipboard` / `wl-paste`/`xclip -o` diagnostics.
Add the index line in `pitfalls/README.md`.

84	### 3. Editor — Neovim
85	
86	[`dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua`](../../dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua):
87	
88	```lua
89	vim.opt.clipboard = "unnamedplus"
90	
91	if vim.env.SSH_CONNECTION or vim.env.SSH_TTY then
92	  local osc52 = require("vim.ui.clipboard.osc52")
93	  vim.g.clipboard = {
94	    name = "OSC 52",
95	    copy  = { ["+"] = osc52.copy("+"),  ["*"] = osc52.copy("*")  },
96	    paste = { ["+"] = osc52.paste("+"), ["*"] = osc52.paste("*") },
97	  }
98	end
99	```
100	
101	- Locally, LazyVim's default provider is used (`pbcopy`/`xclip`/`wl-copy` — with working paste).
102	- Over SSH, Neovim's built-in `vim.ui.clipboard.osc52` (shipping since Neovim 0.10) emits OSC 52 directly, bypassing any `pbcopy` binary on the remote host.
103	- The check is `SSH_CONNECTION or SSH_TTY` — either is set by `sshd` for an interactive session.
104	
105	Why conditional rather than always-on OSC 52? OSC 52 paste is unreliable (see the terminal table above). Keeping the local provider for local sessions preserves Neovim's paste behaviour; the override only activates when `pbcopy` on the remote is clearly the wrong answer.
106	
107	### 4. Shell CLI — `x` (cross-platform clipboard wrapper)
108

5	## TL;DR
6	
7	| You are… | Yank in Neovim goes to… | Capture pane (`prefix+y/Y/C-y`) goes to… |
8	|----------|--------------------------|---------------------------------------------|
9	| Local (macOS or Linux desktop) | system clipboard (default provider: `pbcopy` / `wl-copy` / `xclip`) | same, via `tmux load-buffer -w -` which emits OSC 52 *and* sets tmux's paste buffer |
10	| SSH (remote box, with or without tmux) | **local** machine's clipboard (via OSC 52) | **local** machine's clipboard (via tmux → OSC 52) |
11	
12	No extra tools, no X forwarding, no socat listener needed. The only hard requirement is a terminal emulator on your **local** machine that supports OSC 52 (Ghostty, Alacritty, iTerm2, Kitty, WezTerm — all do).

133	```
134	
135	Its copy backend tries, in order: `clip.exe` (WSL) → `pbcopy` (macOS) → `wl-copy` (Wayland) → `xclip` → `xsel` → **OSC 52 fallback** writing directly to `/dev/tty`. This means `x copy` Just Works on macOS, Linux desktop, Linux SSH server, WSL, and anything else that can reach a terminal — you never have to think about which backend is available.
136	
137	`x copy-file PATH...` is intentionally separate from `x copy PATH`: it places file objects on the desktop clipboard so a file manager can paste/copy the selected files, instead of pasting the files' text contents. It uses macOS `osascript` on Finder-compatible desktops and Linux `x-special/gnome-copied-files` MIME data via `wl-copy` / `xclip` for common GTK file managers. This is local-desktop only; OSC 52 cannot carry file objects over SSH. For remote hosts, copy contents with `x copy FILE` or copy a path with `realpath FILE | x copy`.
138	
139	The OSC 52 fallback in `x` is also wrapped for tmux:

```text
1	# Git Diff Workflow
2	
3	This repo manages a small Git review stack instead of forcing a single tool to do everything:
4	
5	- `delta` is the default pager for normal `git diff`, `git show`, and other CLI diff output.
6	- `diffnav` is a GitHub-style diff navigator with a file tree, useful when you want to move around larger patches quickly.
7	- `gh-dash` is the GitHub dashboard and review UI; its diff pager is configured to call `diffnav`.
8	- `lazygit` stays focused on repo operations inside LazyVim, with `delta` configured as its custom pager.
9	
10	## Managed Config Files
11	
12	This workflow is managed globally through these files:
13	
14	- `~/.gitconfig` keeps `delta` as the default Git pager.
15	- `~/.config/gh-dash/config.yml` sets `pager.diff: "diffnav"`.
16	- `~/.config/lazygit/config.yml` uses LazyGit's current `git.pagers` syntax with `delta`.
17	- `~/.config/bat/themes/tokyonight_night.tmTheme` provides the shared Tokyo Night theme used by `bat` previews.
18	
19	## Why Both `delta` and `diffnav`
20	
21	`delta` is still the best default for everyday Git CLI output. It is fast, readable, and already fits `git diff` and LazyGit well.
22	
23	`diffnav` solves a different problem: navigating large review diffs with a file tree and a GitHub-like layout. That makes it a better fit for `gh-dash` than replacing `delta` everywhere.
24	
25	## `gh-dash` + `diffnav`
26	
27	`gh-dash` is installed as a `gh` extension and reads the global config at `~/.config/gh-dash/config.yml`. This repo intentionally keeps that config minimal:

```text
# Pitfalls

Past traps we've stepped on. Symptoms-first knowledge base — the goal is that
when a problem recurs (on a new machine, after an upgrade, with a new tool
combo), grepping the symptom here lands you on the root cause and workaround
in seconds, instead of re-debugging from scratch.

This folder is `chezmoi`-ignored (see `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` → `pitfalls/**`); it
is repo metadata for maintainers, not user-facing config to deploy.

## Pitfalls vs the rest

This repo has four sibling surfaces with overlapping shapes; pick the right one:

| Surface | Time direction | Question it answers | Access pattern |
|---|---|---|---|
| `docs/tools/<tool>.md` | Present | "How does this tool work / how do I configure it?" | Read top to bottom |
| `docs/this_repo/<topic>.md` | Present | "Why did we architect it this way?" | Read top to bottom |
| `pitfalls/<slug>.md` | **Past** | **"I see error X — has this happened before?"** | **Grep symptoms** |
| `backlog/<slug>.md` | Future | "We thought about doing Y — what was the analysis?" | Index in `TODO.md` |
| `AGENTS.md` Hard invariants | Present | "What rules MUST agents follow?" | Read top to bottom |

A pitfall **graduates** to a Hard invariant in `AGENTS.md` when the trap is
serious enough that you can't rely on memory or grep — typically when (a) it
recurs across machines, (b) it silently corrupts state, or (c) the workaround
is non-obvious and easy to undo by accident. When graduating, leave a
`pitfalls/<slug>.md` as historical record and link to it from the invariant.

## When to add a pitfall doc

Add a `pitfalls/<slug>.md` when you've spent more than ~15 minutes on something
where the answer wasn't googleable, AND any of:

- The symptom is non-obvious from the root cause (`SSH_CONNECTION` cleared
  silently → hostname module disappears, no error)
- The fix is "do nothing different but in a specific order" (sentinel writes
  must come after `wait $pid` for fleet-apply, etc.)
- The same trap could be hit by a new agent / new machine / new contributor
- An upstream bug exists with no ETA — workaround needs to outlive memory
- A specific tool version is required (or forbidden) and the failure mode at
  the wrong version is silent / confusing (e.g. tmux 3.2a popup off-screen)

## When NOT to add a pitfall doc

- Trivially googleable error (the next person will solve in 30 seconds anyway)
- Already covered in `docs/tools/<tool>.md` as part of the tool's normal
  configuration — cross-link from this README's "Cross-referenced pitfalls"
  table below instead of duplicating
- Already a `AGENTS.md` Hard invariant — those have higher priority enforcement
  (cross-link only)
- One-off transient (network glitch, machine-specific config rot) — fix and
  move on

## File template

See [`assets/pitfall-doc.md.template`](#) in the
[`project-knowledge-harness` skill](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/tree/main/skills/local/project-knowledge-harness),
or copy the structure of an existing entry below.

Key sections (different from `backlog/` template — symptom-first, not
```
