# <Title describing the SYMPTOM, not the root cause>

**Symptoms** (grep this section): <verbatim error messages, observable behaviour>
**First seen**: YYYY-MM
**Affects**: <tool/version/OS combo>
**Status**: workaround documented / fixed upstream in vX.Y / WONTFIX

## Symptom

Full error messages (verbatim, not paraphrased — preserves grep-ability).
Reproduction steps if applicable.

## Root cause

Why this happens. Reference source, docs, or upstream issue.

## Workaround

Immediate workaround (commands, config diff). Should be copy-pasteable.

## Prevention

How to avoid stepping on this again. If serious enough, link to the
corresponding `AGENTS.md` Hard invariant.

## Related

Links to `docs/`, sibling pitfalls, `TODO.md` entries (if a real fix is
queued), upstream issues/PRs.
```

## Index

Pitfalls owned by this folder. Keep alphabetical.

| Slug | Symptom keywords | Status |
|---|---|---|
| [`agent-warmup-scheduled-run-hangs-or-blank-under-daemon`](agent-warmup-scheduled-run-hangs-or-blank-under-daemon.md) | launchd/pueue `agent-warmup run` wedges for hours (`state = running`, no log) or finishes with an EMPTY `/usage` panel / blank `capture-pane`; `sample` shows `dyld mapFileReadOnly`; stuck PID is `uv` or `python3 .../agent-warmup`; identical `agent-warmup verify` works by hand | fixed (main-volume stdlib bootstrap · isolated uv-first runtime with startup sentinel/fallback · existing Herdr or GUI tmux backend) |
| [`ansible-folded-scalar-regex-empty-url-silent-skip`](ansible-folded-scalar-regex-empty-url-silent-skip.md) | `~/.local/share/applications/zen-browser.desktop` has a **recent** mtime but `stat ~/Applications/zen.AppImage` → `No such file or directory`; Zen absent from the GNOME launcher (`TryExec=` dangles, so the entry hides rather than erroring); `applaunch Zen` does nothing while `appquit`/`appactivate` still work; the Zen actually running is an unmanaged `zen-x86_64_<hash>.AppImage` frozen at `Version=1.11.5b` / `BuildID=20250419054652`, so Twitch says `Your browser is not currently supported`; ansible reports `failed=0`, `--syntax-check` passes, `rescue:` never fires | fixed — three compounding bugs: `\\.` in a YAML **folded** scalar (`>-`) stays two literal backslashes so the `match` regex never matched and the URL resolved to `''` (double-quoted scalars *do* unescape — the mirror image of [`ansible-when-regex-replace-backslash-strip`](ansible-when-regex-replace-backslash-strip.md)); a **skipped** task passes `is succeeded`, so the icon/`.desktop`/`update-desktop-database` tasks ran for an AppImage never fetched; and `retries:`/`delay:` without `until:` are ignored outright. Now `equalto` (no regex), `is not skipped` guards, an explicit no-match warning, and real `until:` |
| [`ansible-homebrew-expecting-value-line-1-column-1`](ansible-homebrew-expecting-value-line-1-column-1.md) | `Module failed: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)` at a `community.general.homebrew` task (`roles/devtools` resvg), `failed=1`, `20_ansible_roles.sh: exit status 2` — so every later `run_after_` script (bat theme, brew bundle, yazi plugins, completions) is silently skipped; also `brew bundle` "succeeding" while installing nothing | fixed (a fake `brew` stub — `#!/bin/sh`+`exit 0` — satisfied `command -v brew` and returned 0 with empty output for every subcommand; bootstrap now has a glibc >= 2.28 gate so the stub isn't needed, and all probes test `brew --prefix` **output** instead of exit status) |
| [`ansible-js-cli-tools-old-system-node`](ansible-js-cli-tools-old-system-node.md) | `Tag 'js_cli_tools' had failures` / `Tag 'coding_agents' had failures`; `npm WARN EBADENGINE` + `EACCES /usr/local/lib/node_modules`; system node v12.22.9 on Ubuntu jammy | fix paths documented (no in-repo fix yet) |
| [`ansible-missing-sudo-tag`](ansible-missing-sudo-tag.md) | `chezmoi apply` in noRoot mode aborts at one ansible task with `sudo: a password is required` / `Premature end of stream waiting for become success`; works fine on rooted hosts | workaround documented (add `tags: [sudo]`); convention = every `become: true` in `dot_ansible/` must pair with `tags: [sudo]` |
| [`ansible-when-regex-replace-backslash-strip`](ansible-when-regex-replace-backslash-strip.md) | an ansible `when:` / `failed_when:` / `changed_when:` clause combining `regex_replace(...)` with `is version(...)` dies with `The test plugin 'ansible.builtin.version' failed: Version comparison failed: '<' not supported between instances of 'str' and 'int'` — even though **both** operands look purely numeric (`0.7.4` vs `0.8.5`, no `rc`/`dev` component); the byte-identical expression inside `debug.msg: "{{ … }}"` prints the right substring (`0.7.4`); double-escaping to `\\S` / `\\1` works while the single-escaped `when: >-` form keeps failing; error origin points at the task header / `when:` column, never at the regex; ansible-core >= 2.18 + Python 3.13; `ansible-playbook --syntax-check` is clean | fixed (`dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools` extracts the version with `awk '{print $2}'` at the registering step + `set_fact`, so there is no `regex_replace` in `when:` at all) — the conditional lexer strips one extra backslash layer (`\S`→`S`, `\1`→`1`), the pattern stops matching, and `regex_replace` returns the **input unchanged** so `"uv 0.7.4 (…)"` reaches the `version` test; see [ansible#41555](https://github.com/ansible/ansible/issues/41555) |
| [`appimagelauncher-renames-managed-appimage`](appimagelauncher-renames-managed-appimage.md) | Zen has both `zen-browser.desktop` and `appimagekit_*Zen*.desktop`; deleting the latter lasts only until login; older installs vanish after first launch because AIL md5-renamed `zen.AppImage` and left `TryExec` dangling | fixed — AppImageLauncher integrates through both its watched-directory daemon and a `binfmt_misc` execution hook. Zen now lives at the unwatched fixed path `~/.local/opt/zen/zen.AppImage`, launches with the upstream-supported `APPIMAGELAUNCHER_DISABLE=1`, removes stale AIL entries/icons, and uses the single stable ID `zen-browser.desktop` |
| [`apprise-dbus-disabled-in-uv-tool-venv`](apprise-dbus-disabled-in-uv-tool-venv.md) | Claude Code `Stop`/`Notification` hooks produce **no banner and no error**; `apprise --tag desktop --title t --body b` prints nothing and exits `1`; `apprise -vvv` reveals `WARNING - DBus Notification is currently disabled on this system.` plus `WARNING - Failed to load Apprise configuration from file://…/custom.yaml`; `notify-send` works fine by hand and the *system* python imports `dbus` happily | fixed (`uv tool install --force apprise --with dbus-python` — a uv-tool venv can't see distro `python3-dbus`, so the `dbus://` plugin disables itself; the "Failed to load" line means the included config has **zero services**, not bad YAML). `notify.sh` is now apprise → `notify-send`/`terminal-notifier` → log file so it can never fail silently again. Ansible role still unpatched (needs a per-tool OS gate) |
| [`appsrc-tui-subprocess-thread-hang`](appsrc-tui-subprocess-thread-hang.md) | `appsrc tui` opens, paints the `Name  Source  Kind  Size  Path` header, and the table stays **empty forever** (no rows after 10-20s, no crash, no traceback); `tv appsrc` shows `0 / 0` / `Select an entry to preview` while `appsrc scan` in a plain shell happily prints 2266 items; `APPSRC_TUI_DEBUG=/tmp/x appsrc tui` log stops dead at `ctx built -> inventory` or at a random `cli 1500/2193 :: …` with no `inventory=N`; intermittent and stalls at a **different** subprocess each run; a headless `App.run_test()` pilot populates 2276 rows every single time, so the pilot "passes" while the real terminal is dead; `stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL` does not help | fixed (async `@work` worker + `asyncio.create_subprocess_exec` shelling out **once** to `appsrc scan/size --json` instead of thousands of in-thread forks) — blocking `subprocess.run` inside a Textual `@work(thread=True)` races the loop's asyncio child-watcher over reaping, so it deadlocks probabilistically per call; validate in a real tmux PTY, `run_test()` is necessary but not sufficient |
| [`apt-update-fails-base-role-empty-error`](apt-update-fails-base-role-empty-error.md) | `Failed to update apt cache after 5 retries: ''` (empty reason) at base role; `Failed to update cache after 5 retries due to , retrying`; `chezmoi init` exit 1 on Debian/Ubuntu; GFW host with unreachable third-party repo / dead lazygit PPA leftover | fixed (best-effort cache update + CLI diagnostics; lazygit PPA removed + purged; deb822 migration with policy-probe rollback) |
| [`bat-theme-cache-cleared-never-rebuilt`](bat-theme-cache-cleared-never-rebuilt.md) | `[bat warning]: Unknown theme 'tokyonight_night', using default.` on every `bat` call and every `git diff` (delta embeds bat); `bat --list-themes \| grep tokyonight` empty; `ls "$(bat --cache-dir)"` → `No such file or directory`; the managed `.tmTheme` IS present and `chezmoi apply` never fixes it | fixed (run-script `run_onchange_after_` → self-healing `run_after_` with a cache-freshness check; shell only exports `BAT_THEME` when the compiled cache exists) |
| [`bitwarden-ssh-agent-confirm-blocks-remote-git-push`](bitwarden-ssh-agent-confirm-blocks-remote-git-push.md) | `git push` / ssh fails `Connection closed by … port 443` + `Could not read from remote repository` when `$SSH_AUTH_SOCK` is Bitwarden's agent and you're on a remote/headless session; intermittent (first push OK, later fail); `ssh-add -l` still lists the key | by design — disable per-use confirm, approve at the physical screen, `ssh -A` forward, or use HTTPS+PAT |
| [`blesh-set-v-leaks-gexec-wrapper`](blesh-set-v-leaks-gexec-wrapper.md) | `{ _ble_edit_exec_gexec__save_lastarg "$@"; } 4>&1 5>&2 &>/dev/null` printed after every prompt under bash + ble.sh; typed command echoed twice; goes away in fresh terminal; no `+` prefix (so not `set -x`) | workaround = `set +v` in-session; `set -v` is architecturally incompatible with ble.sh's eval-based gexec |
| [`bootstrap-curl-bash-hangs-after-reattaching-tty`](bootstrap-curl-bash-hangs-after-reattaching-tty.md) | `curl … \| bash` of `bootstrap.sh` hangs forever right after `[bootstrap …] stdin is a pipe — reattaching to /dev/tty for interactive prompts`; no `fetching + running …` log; no `uv`/`chezmoi` child process; only happens on certain fresh users / hosts | fixed (`exec </dev/tty` removed mid-script; `/dev/tty` redirected only on the final `exec uv run`) |
| [`bootstrap-no-tty-sudo-prompt-skipped`](bootstrap-no-tty-sudo-prompt-skipped.md) | `[WARN] Could not establish a sudo session (no TTY and sudo needs a password)` then Linuxbrew installer aborts with `Insufficient permissions to install Homebrew to "/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew"`; `mkdir: cannot create directory '/run/user/<UID>': Permission denied`; user verifiably has interactive sudo; CentOS 7 + high-UID AD/LDAP user | workaround documented (`CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` / `just apply-with-sudo` / `NOPASSWD: ALL` sudoers drop-in) |
| [`brew-bundle-redownloads-manually-installed-cask`](brew-bundle-redownloads-manually-installed-cask.md) | `brew bundle` re-downloads cask for `.app` already in `/Applications/`; chains into `process has already locked .incomplete` parallel-fetch errors; `[WARN] Some packages in macOS packages from Brewfile.darwin still failed after 2 attempts` | partial: stale-lock cleanup permanent; `--adopt` pre-flight opt-in via `CHEZMOI_BREW_ADOPT_PREFLIGHT=1` (version-strict + password-storm trade-offs documented) |

# lazygit `Ctrl+O` "No clipboard utilities available" / Neovim yank never reaches the system clipboard

**Symptoms** (grep this section):

- lazygit `Ctrl+O` (copy to clipboard) flashes an error and copies nothing:
  ```
  No clipboard utilities available. Please install xsel, xclip, wl-clipboard or Termux:API add-on for termux-clipboard-get/set.
  ```
- **Paired symptom, same root cause:** in Neovim, `yy` / `"+y` / visual-mode
  `y` put nothing on the system clipboard. Paste into another app gets old
  content. `:checkhealth provider.clipboard` reports:
  ```
  clipboard: No clipboard tool found. :help clipboard
  ```
- `x copy` appears to work but only ever uses its OSC 52 `/dev/tty` fallback
  (nothing lands on a GUI paste); `x copy-file FILE` fails outright:
  ```
  x: no file clipboard backend found.
  ```
- Local Ubuntu desktop session (Wayland / `niri`, or an X11 session) — **not**
  over SSH. Over SSH these all work (OSC 52 path).
- CopyQ is installed and its tray icon is running, yet none of lazygit /
  Neovim / `x` can see a clipboard.

**First seen**: 2026-08
**Affects**: any `ubuntu_desktop` host before this fix; lazygit (all versions),
Neovim (all versions — clipboard support is a runtime binary probe, there is
no `+clipboard` build flag), `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_x`.
**Status**: fixed — `dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux` now installs
`wl-clipboard` + `xclip` + `xsel`; `dot_config/lazygit/config.yml` routes
`Ctrl+O` through `x copy`.

## Root cause

No ansible role installed a clipboard CLI. `gui_apps_linux` installed **CopyQ**
— but CopyQ is a clipboard-*history manager*. Its `copyq` CLI
(`copyq copy` / `copyq clipboard`) is a bespoke interface; it is **not** one
of the binaries the three consumers probe for:

| Consumer | What it shells out to |
|---|---|
| lazygit `Ctrl+O` | vendored `atotto/clipboard`: `$WAYLAND_DISPLAY` set → `wl-copy`; else `xclip`; else `xsel`; else `termux-clipboard-set`. None found → the error above. |
| Neovim `clipboard=unnamedplus` | built-in provider auto-detect: `pbcopy` (macOS) → `wl-copy`/`wl-paste` → `xclip` → `xsel` → … . None found → yank is a silent no-op (`unnamedplus` still "works", it just writes to a register with no OS bridge). |
| `~/.dotfiles/bin/x` | `copy_backend()`: `clip.exe` → `pbcopy` → `wl-copy` (needs `$WAYLAND_DISPLAY`) → `xclip`/`xsel` (need `$DISPLAY`) → **OSC 52 to `/dev/tty`**. `copy_file_backend()` has *no* OSC 52 fallback. |

`dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua` only overrides to the OSC 52 provider
when `SSH_CONNECTION` / `SSH_TTY` is set — so locally it depends entirely on a
provider binary existing. `docs/tools/clipboard.md` already *assumed*
`wl-copy` / `xclip` were present ("default provider …") with no install story.

## Workaround / fix

Immediate, by hand:

```sh
sudo apt install wl-clipboard xclip xsel
```

In this repo (already applied):

- `dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml` — task
  **"Install clipboard CLIs (wl-clipboard, xclip, xsel)"**, next to the CopyQ
  / app-control block, same `os_family == 'Debian'` + `target_architecture !=
  'armv7l'` + `tags: [sudo]` guard. Runs on `ubuntu_desktop` only (via the
  `gui_apps` tag in `run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl`).
- `dot_config/lazygit/config.yml` — adds:
  ```yaml
  os:
    copyToClipboardCmd: "printf '%s' {{text}} | x copy"
  ```
  so `Ctrl+O` uses `x`'s backend chain: `wl-copy`/`xclip` locally, OSC 52 over
  SSH (lazygit's native path would target the *remote's* clipboard). Safe
  because lazygit shell-quotes `{{text}}` via `c.Cmd.Quote` before
  substitution (`OSCommand.CopyToClipboard`).

Server profiles deliberately get **none** of this — headless has no
clipboard; OSC 52 (`set-clipboard on` + `x`'s `/dev/tty` fallback) is the
whole story there.

## Diagnostics

```sh
echo "$XDG_SESSION_TYPE $WAYLAND_DISPLAY $DISPLAY"   # wayland / x11?
command -v wl-copy xclip xsel                        # any backend at all?
printf hi | wl-copy && wl-paste                      # Wayland round-trip
printf hi | xclip -selection clipboard && xclip -selection clipboard -o
nvim --headless -c 'checkhealth provider.clipboard' -c 'q'
```

## Prevention

Rule (see `AGENTS.md` cross-file table): a new tool installed by any
mechanism gets a row in `docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md` § Tool index. The
clipboard CLIs are now listed there and in
`docs/playbooks/linux-gui-apps.md`. Neovim / lazygit / `x` all silently
degrade without them, so the install lives with CopyQ in `gui_apps_linux`
rather than being assumed.

## Related

- [`docs/tools/clipboard.md`](../docs/tools/clipboard.md) — the 4-layer OSC 52
  chain (terminal / tmux / Neovim / `x`) + the lazygit `Ctrl+O` note.
- [`docs/playbooks/linux-gui-apps.md`](../docs/playbooks/linux-gui-apps.md) —
  inventory row.
- `dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua` — the `SSH_CONNECTION` gate on the
  OSC 52 provider.
- atotto/clipboard selection order: `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` → wl-clipboard → xclip →
  xsel (checked with `exec.LookPath`).

````

+- Locally, LazyVim's default provider is used (`pbcopy`/`wl-copy`/`xclip` — with working paste). That provider is a **runtime binary probe** — Neovim has no compile-time `+clipboard`. On macOS `pbcopy` is built in; on a Linux desktop the binary comes from `wl-clipboard` / `xclip`, installed by the [`gui_apps_linux`](../../dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml) role ("Install clipboard CLIs"). Without it, `:checkhealth provider.clipboard` reports "No clipboard tool found" and yank silently no-ops — see [`pitfalls/lazygit-ctrl-o-no-clipboard-utilities-nvim-yank-silent.md`](../../pitfalls/lazygit-ctrl-o-no-clipboard-utilities-nvim-yank-silent.md).

 Why conditional rather than always-on OSC 52? OSC 52 paste is unreliable (see the terminal table above). Keeping the local provider for local sessions preserves Neovim's paste behaviour; the override only activates when `pbcopy` on the remote is clearly the wrong answer.
 
+### 3a. Git TUI — lazygit
+
+[`dot_config/lazygit/config.yml`](../../dot_config/lazygit/config.yml) sets:
+
+```yaml
+os:
+  copyToClipboardCmd: "printf '%s' {{text}} | x copy"
+```
+
+`Ctrl+O` ("copy to clipboard") is routed through `x` instead of lazygit's
+vendored `atotto/clipboard`. Locally that resolves to `wl-copy`/`xclip`; over
+SSH it falls through to `x`'s OSC 52 path, so the yank lands on the **local**
+clipboard from remote hosts too (lazygit's native library would target the
+remote's X/Wayland clipboard). lazygit shell-quotes `{{text}}` before
+substitution, so multi-word commit subjects and paths survive.
+
 ### 4. Shell CLI — `x` (cross-platform clipboard wrapper)
 
 [`dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_x`](../../dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_x) (deployed to `~/.dotfiles/bin/x`) is a Bash wrapper with three subcommands:
@@ -116,7 +132,7 @@ x paste                        # print clipboard to stdout
 x open https://example.com     # open URL/file in default app
 ```
 
-Its copy backend tries, in order: `clip.exe` (WSL) → `pbcopy` (macOS) → `wl-copy` (Wayland) → `xclip` → `xsel` → **OSC 52 fallback** writing directly to `/dev/tty`. This means `x copy` Just Works on macOS, Linux desktop, Linux SSH server, WSL, and anything else that can reach a terminal — you never have to think about which backend is available.
+Its copy backend tries, in order: `clip.exe` (WSL) → `pbcopy` (macOS) → `wl-copy` (Wayland) → `xclip` → `xsel` → **OSC 52 fallback** writing directly to `/dev/tty`. This means `x copy` Just Works on macOS, Linux desktop, Linux SSH server, WSL, and anything else that can reach a terminal — you never have to think about which backend is available. On a Linux desktop the `wl-copy` / `xclip` / `xsel` binaries come from the [`gui_apps_linux`](../../dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml) role; without them `x copy` still works via OSC 52 but `x copy-file` has no backend.
 
 `x copy-file PATH...` is intentionally separate from `x copy PATH`: it places file objects on the desktop clipboard so a file manager can paste/copy the selected files, instead of pasting the files' text contents. It uses macOS `osascript` on Finder-compatible desktops and Linux `x-special/gnome-copied-files` MIME data via `wl-copy` / `xclip` for common GTK file managers. This is local-desktop only; OSC 52 cannot carry file objects over SSH. For remote hosts, copy contents with `x copy FILE` or copy a path with `realpath FILE | x copy`.

```text
 docs/tools/clipboard.zh-TW.md | 19 +++++++++++++++----
 1 file changed, 15 insertions(+), 4 deletions(-)
===
```

- 本機時，使用 LazyVim 預設 provider（`pbcopy`/`wl-copy`/`xclip` — 貼上正常運作）。這個 provider 是**執行期二進制檔偵測** — Neovim 沒有編譯期的 `+clipboard`。macOS 內建 `pbcopy`；Linux 桌面的二進制檔來自 `wl-clipboard` / `xclip`，由 [`gui_apps_linux`](../../dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml) role 安裝（「Install clipboard CLIs」）。沒有它，`:checkhealth provider.clipboard` 會回報「No clipboard tool found」，yank 靜默失效 — 見 [`pitfalls/lazygit-ctrl-o-no-clipboard-utilities-nvim-yank-silent.md`](../../pitfalls/lazygit-ctrl-o-no-clipboard-utilities-nvim-yank-silent.md)。
- SSH 時，Neovim 內建的 `vim.ui.clipboard.osc52`（自 Neovim 0.10 起隨附）直接發出 OSC 52，繞過遠端主機上任何 `pbcopy` 二進制檔。
- 判斷條件是 `SSH_CONNECTION or SSH_TTY` — 任一個都會由 `sshd` 為互動 session 設定。

為何用條件式而非永遠開啟 OSC 52？OSC 52 貼上不可靠（見上方終端機表格）。本機 session 保留本機 provider 可保留 Neovim 的貼上行為；只有當遠端的 `pbcopy` 顯然是錯誤答案時才覆寫。

### 下游消費者 — lazygit `Ctrl+O`

[`dot_config/lazygit/config.yml`](../../dot_config/lazygit/config.yml) 設定：

```yaml
os:
  copyToClipboardCmd: "printf '%s' {{text}} | x copy"
```

`Ctrl+O`（「複製到剪貼簿」）改走 `x`，而非 lazygit 內附的 `atotto/clipboard`。本機會解析為 `wl-copy`/`xclip`；SSH 時則落到 `x` 的 OSC 52 路徑，讓 yank 也能送到**本機**剪貼簿（lazygit 原生函式庫會送到遠端的 X/Wayland 剪貼簿）。lazygit 在代入前會對 `{{text}}` 做 shell 引號處理，因此含空格的 commit 標題與路徑都安全。

### 4. Shell CLI — `x`（跨平台剪貼簿包裝）

[`dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_x`](../../dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_x)（部署到 `~/.dotfiles/bin/x`）是一支 Bash 包裝，含三個子指令：

```bash
printf "hello" | x copy        # 把 stdin 複製到剪貼簿
x copy path/to/file            # 複製檔案內容
x paste                        # 把剪貼簿印到 stdout
x open https://example.com     # 在預設 app 中開啟 URL/檔案
```
```
</details></tool-use>

+[`dot_config/lazygit/config.yml`](../../dot_config/lazygit/config.yml) 設定：
+
+```yaml
+os:
+  copyToClipboardCmd: "printf '%s' {{text}} | x copy"
+```
+
+`Ctrl+O`（「複製到剪貼簿」）改走 `x`，而非 lazygit 內附的 `atotto/clipboard`。本機會解析為 `wl-copy`/`xclip`；SSH 時則落到 `x` 的 OSC 52 路徑，讓 yank 也能送到**本機**剪貼簿（lazygit 原生函式庫會送到遠端的 X/Wayland 剪貼簿）。lazygit 在代入前會對 `{{text}}` 做 shell 引號處理，因此含空格的 commit 標題與路徑都安全。
+
 ### 4. Shell CLI — `x`（跨平台剪貼簿包裝）
```

+#                   Redundant with xclip for lazygit (atotto tries xclip
+#                   first) but tiny; kept so the error's advice always holds.

+# Server profiles deliberately don't get these — headless has no clipboard;
+# OSC 52 (tmux `set-clipboard on` + `x`'s /dev/tty fallback) is the answer
+# there. See docs/tools/clipboard.md.
+# =============================================================================
+

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-08-28 10:14:15Z)**_

Root cause confirmed and fixed. This machine (Wayland/niri, `ubuntu_desktop`) had **no clipboard CLI installed at all** — `gui_apps_linux` installs CopyQ (a history *manager*), but not the `wl-copy`/`xclip`/`xsel` binaries that lazygit, Neovim's clipboard provider, and `x` actually shell out to. Yes, your nvim yank suspicion is the same root cause.

## Changes made

**Install (the actual fix)** — `dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml`: new task installs `wl-clipboard` + `xclip` + `xsel` (Debian, `ubuntu_desktop` only — servers stay OSC 52-only by design), next to the CopyQ/app-control block.

**lazygit** — `dot_config/lazygit/config.yml`: added
```yaml
os:
  copyToClipboardCmd: "printf '%s' {{text}} | x copy"
```
routes `Ctrl+O` through `x`, so it works locally **and** over SSH (native lazygit would copy to the *remote's* clipboard). Safe because lazygit shell-quotes `{{text}}` before substitution (verified in `OSCommand.CopyToClipboard`).

**Neovim** — no change needed. Once a provider binary exists, `clipboard=unnamedplus` works on Wayland (`wl-copy`); the SSH→OSC 52 branch is untouched.

**Docs / mirrors** (per CLAUDE.md cross-file rules): `tool-managers.md` + `.zh-TW` (role table, apt-deps, A–Z index, upgrade list), `linux-gui-apps.md`, `clipboard.md` + `.zh-TW`, `git_diff_workflow.md` + `.zh-TW`, `aliases.md` + `.zh-TW`, `README.md`, plus a new `pitfalls/lazygit-ctrl-o-no-clipboard-utilities-nvim-yank-silent.md` + index row.

## Verification done
- `ansible-playbook --syntax-check` ✅
- lazygit config parses as valid YAML + matches lazygit's schema ✅
- `pre-commit` on all changed files ✅
- `mkdocs build --strict`: 182 warnings **before and after** — zero new (pre-existing anchor drift, tracked in `backlog/mkdocs-anchor-drift.md`)

## What you need to run (needs sudo)

```
! sudo apt install wl-clipboard xclip xsel
```
or `chezmoi apply` (which will run the ansible task). Then test:
- `printf hi | wl-copy && wl-paste`
- nvim `yy` → `:checkhealth provider.clipboard` shows `wl-copy`/`wl-paste`
- lazygit `Ctrl+O` on a commit hash → no error
- `chezmoi apply ~/.config/lazygit/config.yml` first so lazygit picks up the new `os:` block

```text
docs/tools/clipboard.md:189:- **`x` CLI ordering** prefers local backends (`pbcopy`, `wl-copy`, etc.) over OSC 52. This is intentional: when `pbcopy` is available, it's faster, doesn't touch the TTY, and works for very large payloads (OSC 52 payloads are size-limited by the terminal — iTerm2 caps at 1 MB, many others at 64-256 KB). Because OSC 52 has no delivery acknowledgment, `osc52_copy()` refuses payloads above `X_OSC52_MAX_BYTES` (default 75000 base64 chars) with an explicit error rather than writing an escape sequence the terminal would silently drop — a plain `write(2)` to `/dev/tty` succeeds either way, so without this guard `x copy` would report success even when nothing reached the clipboard.
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
173	## Common failure modes
174	
175	| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
176	|---------|-------------|-----|
177	| Yank works outside tmux but vanishes inside tmux (remote) | `set-clipboard off` or server running pre-edit binary | `tmux show -g set-clipboard`; `tmux kill-server` |
178	| `tmux info` shows `Ms: [missing]` | tmux's TERM entry lacks `Ms` *and* no `terminal-features …:clipboard` declared | already handled by [`common.conf`](../../dot_config/tmux/common.conf); on an unusual outer `$TERM`, add another `set -as terminal-features` line |
179	| Ghostty asks about clipboard every yank | `clipboard-read = ask`; Ghostty interprets some writes as reads when apps immediately re-fetch | switch to `clipboard-read = allow` if you trust everything inside your sessions |
180	| Neovim yank works, but `"*p` does nothing over SSH | paste over OSC 52 not supported by outer terminal | expected — use mouse middle-click or re-type; don't fight it |
181	| `prefix+y` still copies to remote clipboard | shim binary `tmux` resolves to an old pre-`load-buffer -w` version | `tmux -V` must be ≥ 3.3 for `load-buffer -w`; this repo enforces ≥ 3.3 via ansible `devtools` role |
182	| Nested tmux (`tmux inside ssh inside tmux`) | inner tmux eats OSC 52 | inner tmux needs `set -g allow-passthrough on`; already on in this config. Double-nested cases may require `Ptmux;…` wrapping |
183	| `x copy` errors with "OSC 52 payload too large" (e.g. copying full pane scrollback over SSH) | payload exceeds the terminal's OSC 52 cap; `x copy` now refuses loudly instead of writing an escape sequence the terminal would silently drop | copy a smaller selection, or raise the cap: `X_OSC52_MAX_BYTES=<n> x copy ...` if your terminal supports more (iTerm2 ~1 MB) |
```
</details></tool-use>

```markdown
# `x copy` over SSH puts nothing on the local clipboard (writes the remote box's clipboard instead of OSC 52)

**Symptoms** (grep this section):

- SSH'd into a Linux desktop; `abspath | x copy`, `cref`, `printf x | x copy`
  all report success but **nothing** appears on the clipboard of the machine
  you're typing on.
- No error. `x paste` on the remote *does* show the text — it went to the
  remote's clipboard.
- Neovim yank over the same SSH session works fine (it lands locally via
  OSC 52), so it looks like an `x`-only bug.
- `echo "$WAYLAND_DISPLAY $DISPLAY"` in the SSH shell is **non-empty**
  (e.g. `wayland-1 :0`) even though you did not `ssh -X`.

**First seen**: 2026-08
**Affects**: `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_x` before the SSH gate; any host
where you are logged in graphically (niri / GNOME) *and* SSH into the same
user account.
**Status**: fixed — `x` sends OSC 52 first when `SSH_CONNECTION` /
`SSH_TTY` / `SSH_CLIENT` is set.

## Root cause

`x`'s `copy_backend()` chose a backend purely by "is `$WAYLAND_DISPLAY` /
`$DISPLAY` set and is `wl-copy` / `xclip` installed?" — with **no SSH
check**. Neovim's `options.lua` gates on `SSH_CONNECTION || SSH_TTY`; `x`
did not.

`WAYLAND_DISPLAY` / `DISPLAY` leak into an SSH shell whenever the same user
has a graphical session: the compositor runs
`systemctl --user import-environment` /
`dbus-update-activation-environment`, `loginctl enable-linger` keeps the
user manager alive, and `pam_systemd` hands the SSH session a slice of that
environment. So `x copy` found `wl-copy` + a live `$WAYLAND_DISPLAY` and
wrote to the **remote** compositor's clipboard.

Installing `wl-clipboard` (see
[`lazygit-ctrl-o-no-clipboard-utilities-nvim-yank-silent.md`](lazygit-ctrl-o-no-clipboard-utilities-nvim-yank-silent.md))
made this *more* likely to bite, because before that there was no `wl-copy`
to pick and `x` fell through to OSC 52 by accident.

## Workaround / fix

Fixed in `executable_x`:

- `is_ssh()` helper (`SSH_CONNECTION` / `SSH_TTY` / `SSH_CLIENT`).
- `copy_backend()`: under SSH, try `osc52_copy` **first**; fall through to
  `wl-copy` / `xclip` / `xsel` only if `/dev/tty` can't be opened (no-PTY
  `ssh`, or a deliberate `ssh -X` wanting the remote X clipboard).
- `osc52_copy()` now does `{ : >/dev/tty; } 2>/dev/null || return 1` instead
  of `[[ -w /dev/tty ]]` — a detached context can have a `/dev/tty` node
  whose `open(2)` returns `ENXIO`; the old test passed and then `base64`
  consumed stdin before the write failed, starving the fallback.
- `copy_file_backend()`: refuses over SSH (a file object can't cross OSC 52).

Manual, pre-fix: `unset WAYLAND_DISPLAY DISPLAY; abspath | x copy`.

If `x copy` over SSH *still* doesn't reach the local clipboard after the fix,
the problem is downstream: the **local** terminal doesn't forward OSC 52, or
a **local** tmux server started before `set-clipboard on` was applied
(`tmux kill-server` and reattach). See [`clipboard.md`](../docs/tools/clipboard.md).

## Related

- [`docs/tools/clipboard.md`](../docs/tools/clipboard.md) § Shell CLI — `x`
  (the SSH ordering note + failure-modes table).
- `dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua` — the `SSH_CONNECTION` gate `x`
  now mirrors.
- [`lazygit-ctrl-o-no-clipboard-utilities-nvim-yank-silent.md`](lazygit-ctrl-o-no-clipboard-utilities-nvim-yank-silent.md)
  — the clipboard-CLI install that surfaced this.

  # shfmt - auto-format bash scripts in place. Same UX as

  # if the hook rewrites a file, pre-commit reports "files were

  # would-be diff but left working tree untouched, forcing a manual

  # with system shfmt defaults (tabs instead of 2-space).
  - repo: https://github.com/scop/pre-commit-shfmt
    rev: v3.10.0-2
    hooks:
      - id: shfmt
        files: '^scripts/[^/]+\.sh$'
        args: [-i, "2", -ci, -bn, -w]

  # block through shellcheck (auto-discovered on PATH — installed above) plus

  # installed by the devtools ansible role (brew on macOS / Linuxbrew on Linux)

  # host without that binary, swap to `id: actionlint` (language: golang,
  # builds its own). Scoped to workflow files. See docs/tools/actionlint.md.
  - repo: https://github.com/rhysd/actionlint

## The SSH `x copy` bug you hit

`x`'s backend picker only looked at `$WAYLAND_DISPLAY`/`$DISPLAY` — no SSH check. Those **leak into your SSH shell** because you're also logged in graphically on that box (niri runs `systemctl --user import-environment` + `loginctl enable-linger`). So `x copy` found `wl-copy` + a live `$WAYLAND_DISPLAY` and wrote to *that box's* clipboard. Neovim didn't have this problem because `options.lua` gates on `SSH_CONNECTION`.

Fixed: `x` now has `is_ssh()` and tries OSC 52 first under `SSH_*` (falls back to the display tools only if `/dev/tty` won't open, for the `ssh -X` case). `x copy-file` now refuses over SSH outright.

## To pick it up (you're on the box now)

```
chezmoi apply ~/.dotfiles/bin/x
```

Then confirm — in your SSH session:

```sh
# root-cause check: are the display vars leaking?
echo "SSH=$SSH_CONNECTION | WL=$WAYLAND_DISPLAY | X=$DISPLAY | TMUX=${TMUX:+yes}"

# does raw OSC 52 reach your LOCAL clipboard? (bypasses x entirely)
printf '\033]52;c;%s\033\\' "$(printf 'osc52-works' | base64 | tr -d '\n')" > /dev/tty
#   → then paste locally. If this doesn't work, the blocker is your
#     outer terminal or a stale LOCAL tmux server (tmux kill-server),
#     not x — see docs/tools/clipboard.md failure-modes table.

abspath | x copy   # should now land locally
```

If you also want the clipboard *install* (`wl-clipboard` etc.) on this box, run `sudo apt install wl-clipboard xclip xsel` or a full `chezmoi apply`.

No — `SSH=` being **empty** is exactly why the fix didn't help. Your connection method is hiding the SSH env vars, so neither `x` nor Neovim can tell this shell is remote:

- `WL=wayland-0 X=:0` → both `x` and nvim pick `wl-copy` and write to **this box's** clipboard
- `SSH=` empty → my `is_ssh()` gate (and nvim's identical `SSH_CONNECTION` gate) never fire

`SSH_CONNECTION`/`SSH_TTY`/`SSH_CLIENT` get stripped by **mosh** (deliberately), and are often absent under **VS Code / Cursor Remote-SSH**, **Eternal Terminal**, etc. A plain `ssh` would have set them.

Two things I need to know to fix it properly:

**1. How do you connect to this box?** (plain `ssh` in a terminal / mosh / VS Code or Cursor Remote-SSH / JetBrains Gateway / Eternal Terminal / a remote desktop like RDP-VNC-NoMachine / something else)

**2. Did the raw OSC 52 line actually work?** Run just this, then paste (Cmd/Ctrl+V) somewhere on your **laptop**:
```sh
printf '\033]52;c;%s\033\\' "$(printf 'osc52-works' | base64 | tr -d '\n')" > /dev/tty
```
Did `osc52-works` land on your laptop's clipboard? (yes / no)

That result decides the fix:
- **yes** → terminal forwards OSC 52; I'll give `x` a remote signal that doesn't depend on `SSH_*` (e.g. an `X_CLIPBOARD=osc52` override in `~/.shellrc.adhoc`, or auto-detect via parent process / `XDG_SESSION_TYPE`)
- **no** → OSC 52 isn't viable on your path; if it's a remote-desktop protocol the box's clipboard *is* the shared one and the sync is the thing to fix instead

```text
#!/bin/sh
# chezmoi modify_ script: overlay a managed herdr config onto ~/.config/herdr/config.toml.
#
# Why: herdr can rewrite this file at runtime (onboarding flag, in-app settings
# popups, [session]/[remote]/[update] state), so tracking it as a plain managed
# file would clobber that writeback and re-trigger onboarding. It was previously
# `create_` (seed-once), but that meant repo edits never reached an
# already-seeded host without a manual refresh. This modify_ overlay enforces
# our managed tables ([theme], [ui], [terminal], [keys]) on every `chezmoi
# apply` while preserving every other top-level key herdr writes back.
#
# How: chezmoi pipes the current target file into stdin; this script prints the
# new contents on stdout.
#
# Merge model — template-as-base, pull-through unmanaged keys:
#   - Base = the managed template (.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml), which
#     carries the comments + the tmux-parity rationale.
#   - For every TOP-LEVEL key in the live file NOT in {theme, ui, terminal,
#     keys}, copy it into the base (preserves onboarding, [session], [remote],
#     [update], [experimental], and any future herdr writeback).
#   - Managed tables are enforced wholesale (template wins) — this is a managed
#     dotfile; in-app theme/label overrides are intentionally re-asserted.
#
# Why tomlkit (not codex's inline emitter): herdr's config has an
# array-of-tables ([[keys.command]]) and comments we want to keep; stdlib
# tomllib is read-only and the codex modify_ emitter can't emit AoT. tomlkit
# round-trips both.
#
# Note: the template is written to a temp file via a heredoc *redirect* (not
# captured with $(...)), because the config body contains a lone backtick
# (`key = "prefix+\`"`) that bash mis-parses as command substitution when a
# quoted heredoc is nested inside $(...). Passing the path to Python sidesteps it.
#
# To manage an additional key: edit .chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml.
# Python runtime: prefer `uv` (guarantees Python >=3.11 → stdlib tomllib), fall
# back to system python3, then to printing the raw template unmodified (a
# fresh-bootstrap host with neither uv nor python3 still gets a full config —
# note we print the TEMPLATE, not stdin, because on a fresh host stdin is empty).
set -eu

tmpl_file=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/herdr-config.XXXXXX")
trap 'rm -f "$tmpl_file"' EXIT INT TERM

cat <<'TOML' > "$tmpl_file"
{{ template "herdr/config.toml" . }}
TOML

live=$(cat)

if command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  set -- uv run --no-project --quiet --with tomlkit --python '>=3.11' python -
elif command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  set -- python3 -
else
  echo "modify_config.toml: neither uv nor python3 found; emitting managed template" >&2
  cat "$tmpl_file"
  exit 0
fi

HERDR_TEMPLATE_FILE="$tmpl_file" HERDR_LIVE="$live" "$@" <<'PYEOF'
import os
import sys

tmpl_path = os.environ["HERDR_TEMPLATE_FILE"]
with open(tmpl_path, "r") as fh:
    template_text = fh.read()


def emit_template():
    sys.stdout.write(template_text)


# Read side: stdlib tomllib (uv guarantees >=3.11); tomli backport otherwise.
try:
    import tomllib  # Python 3.11+
except ModuleNotFoundError:
    try:
        import tomli as tomllib
    except ModuleNotFoundError:
        # No TOML reader → can't safely merge; ship the managed template as-is
        # (loses runtime-key preservation, but keeps the host configured).
        emit_template()
        sys.exit(0)

# Write side: tomlkit preserves comments + array-of-tables. uv installs it via
# --with tomlkit; a bare system python3 may lack it → fall back to raw template.
try:
    import tomlkit
except ModuleNotFoundError:
    print(
        "modify_config.toml: tomlkit unavailable; emitting managed template "
        "(runtime keys not preserved this run)",
        file=sys.stderr,
    )
    emit_template()
    sys.exit(0)

MANAGED = {"theme", "ui", "terminal", "keys"}

live_text = os.environ.get("HERDR_LIVE", "").strip()
doc = tomlkit.parse(template_text)  # base, with comments intact
live = tomllib.loads(live_text) if live_text else {}

# Pull through every top-level key herdr owns at runtime that we don't manage.
for key, value in live.items():
    if key in MANAGED or key in doc:
        continue
    doc[key] = value

sys.stdout.write(tomlkit.dumps(doc))
PYEOF
```
</details></tool-use>

# TRIAL config that mirrors the tmux experience as closely as herdr's
# primitives allow. herdr COEXISTS with tmux — you run one or the other (or
# nest deliberately; see docs/tools/herdr.md "nested inside tmux"). Nothing here

# (dot_config/herdr/modify_config.toml.tmpl). The overlay enforces the tables
# below on every `chezmoi apply` and preserves any keys herdr writes back at
# runtime (onboarding / [session] / [remote] / [update] / [experimental]).
#
# Schema: https://herdr.dev/docs/configuration/

# Full feasibility matrix + behavior model + documented gaps: docs/tools/herdr.md

# NOT gated by enableVimMode: that flag governs shell + tmux modal editing;
# herdr's copy mode (prefix+[) is vi-style natively (h/j/k/l, w/b/e, {/}, v, y).
#
# Prefix is ctrl+b (herdr default, same as tmux). herdr's built-in defaults are
# already close to tmux (prefix+c new tab, prefix+1..9 switch, prefix+h/j/k/l
# focus pane, prefix+v / prefix+minus split, prefix+z zoom, prefix+x close,
# prefix+g session navigator, prefix+w workspace nav, prefix+q detach), so we
# only rebind a couple of keys and add command panes for the tv/lazygit popups.

[theme]
name = "catppuccin"          # mocha (dark)
auto_switch = true            # follow OS light/dark
light_name = "catppuccin-latte"
dark_name = "catppuccin"

[ui]
mouse_capture = true
pane_borders = true
pane_gaps = true
confirm_close = true
show_agent_labels_on_pane_borders = true

# Agent sidebar ordering. herdr's default is "spaces" (grouped by space);
# "priority" turns the panel into an attention queue (blocked/waiting agents
# float to the top) instead of a per-space grouping. With many concurrent agent
# panes the queue is what you actually scan, so this is the more useful default
# here. Valid values: "spaces" | "priority" ("workspaces" is an alias for
# "spaces").
agent_panel_sort = "priority"

# Expanded Agent sidebar row layout. herdr's own default is
#   [["state_icon", "workspace", "tab"], ["agent"]]
# and we append the `$review` metadata token so the review-pending ⭐ (prefix+m /
# hmark) is actually VISIBLE in the sidebar.
#
# Required since herdr 0.7.4: `--custom-status` / the flat `custom_status` field
# were replaced by a namespaced token map, and unlike custom_status a token is
# rendered ONLY where a row layout names it — set a token with no layout entry
# and the flag silently exists in the API but shows up nowhere.
#
# Keep `$review` in sync with TOKEN in dot_config/herdr/executable_review-mark.sh.
# NOTE this pins the layout: upstream changes to the default rows will NOT reach
# us, so re-check this block against `herdr --default-config` on herdr upgrades.
[ui.sidebar.agents]
rows = [
  ["state_icon", "workspace", "tab", "$review"],
  ["agent"],
]

[terminal]
shell_mode = "auto"           # login/non-login auto-detect; follows $SHELL
# CWD policy for new panes/tabs/workspaces (no explicit --cwd). Values:
#   "follow"  = inherit the SOURCE pane/workspace (default)
#   "home"    = $HOME · "current" = herdr's own process dir · or a fixed path
# NOTE (herdr >=0.7.x): with "follow", a NEW TAB inherits the FOCUSED pane's live
# cwd — same as a split. herdr issue #912 changed `follow` so tabs behave like
# splits; the older "new tab opens at the workspace root" was treated as a bug and
# removed. NO new_cwd value opens a new tab at the WORKSPACE ("space") dir — for
# that use the prefix+C command below (derives the space root → tab create --cwd).
# See docs/tools/herdr.md.
new_cwd = "follow"

# --- Built-in action rebinds (tmux muscle memory) ---
# Only existing actions can be rebound; we keep herdr defaults for everything
# not listed here. An action accepts an ARRAY of bindings (herdr docs), so a
# single action can carry both the intuitive key and the tmux-default key.
[keys]
split_vertical = ["prefix+|", "prefix+%"]         # side-by-side (left/right) = tmux prefix+| and prefix+% (-h)
split_horizontal = ["prefix+minus", "prefix+\""]  # stacked (top/bottom)      = tmux prefix+- and prefix+" (-v)
reload_config = "prefix+shift+r"   # tmux: prefix+R
rename_tab = "prefix+,"            # tmux: prefix+, (rename window) — frees prefix+shift+t for the sesh popup below
new_worktree = "prefix+shift+b"    # moved off prefix+shift+g so prefix+G can be lazygit (worktrees handled by wt/wm + herdr-plus auto-layout)

# --- Indexed quick-switch (native herdr actions) ---
# switch_tab (prefix+1..9) is a herdr built-in; add the workspace + agent analogs
# so a number key jumps directly, no navigate mode needed. The "N..M" range form
# is native herdr config syntax (same shape as switch_tab).
# NOTE on the modifier: prefix+SHIFT+digit does NOT work — under the kitty
# keyboard protocol (which herdr uses) shift+1 still carries the printable "!", so
# herdr matches the symbol, not "shift+1". ctrl+digit and alt+digit have no
# printable form, so they disambiguate cleanly. Hence ctrl (workspace) / alt (agent).
switch_workspace = "prefix+ctrl+1..9"    # prefix+ctrl+N → workspace N (shift+N would emit !@#… — unusable)
focus_agent = "prefix+alt+1..9"          # prefix+alt+N  → jump to agent N's pane (herdr tracks agents per pane natively)

# --- Workspace navigate-mode: vim j/k (entered via prefix+w) ---
# prefix+w opens the workspace navigator; navigate_workspace_* are the
# navigate-mode-only movement keys. Add vim j/k alongside the default arrows so
# hjkl muscle memory carries here too. (These fields can't use prefix+/enter/tab/
# left/right or unmodified 1-9 — plain j/k are allowed.)
navigate_workspace_down = ["j", "down"]
navigate_workspace_up = ["k", "up"]

# --- Custom command panes (the tmux-popup recreations) ---
# type = "pane": opens a temporary pane that closes when the command exits —
# herdr's analog of `tmux display-popup -E`. The command runs from the focused
# pane's cwd and gets $HERDR_SOCKET_PATH / $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID /
# $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD in its environment.

[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+G"
type = "pane"
command = "lazygit"
description = "lazygit (popup pane)"
```
</details></tool-use>

51:**Targeting a session from the CLI subcommands**: there is **no `--session`/`--socket` flag** on `workspace`/`tab`/`pane`/`agent`. The only lever is the **`HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`** env var — set it to a session's `socket_path` and every subcommand routes there. Inside a herdr pane it is already exported to the current session's socket, so scripts run *inside* herdr target the current session for free. This is exactly how `hvibe --session NAME` works (see below).
85:The search is bounded by what the live Herdr server still retains: closed panes, output older than the history limit, and alternate-screen content already discarded cannot be recovered. The command runs where the Unix socket is accessible. For a remote server, run the deployed CLI through SSH, for example `ssh server 'herdr-grep --all-sessions -F -- "connection refused"'`; **`herdr --remote` is an interactive thin-client attach, not an RPC prefix for pane subcommands**.
93:- **Every pane has two cwds.** `cwd` = the shell's *startup* directory (fixed at spawn); `foreground_cwd` = the *live* cwd, tracked via **OSC 7** shell integration. A `cd` in the shell updates `foreground_cwd`; the startup `cwd` never changes.
94:- **`cd` inside a child process / subshell doesn't propagate.** Because tracking is OSC 7-based, a `cd` in a subshell that doesn't re-emit OSC 7 — e.g. `chezmoi cd`, which spawns a *new* shell in the source dir — is invisible to herdr. `foreground_cwd` stays put, so the space's git-repo detection and the `prefix+G` lazygit location don't follow the subshell. This is inherent to OSC 7, **not** a herdr bug — expected behavior.
134:| OSC133 copy-mode (`cpout`/`cpblock`) | tmux-specific | **Gap** — `cpcmd` (zsh history) still works |
142:> **Two families of herdr env vars.** The `HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_*` vars above are injected **only** into `[[keys.command]]` invocations. Every shell *running inside a herdr pane* also gets an **ambient** set: `HERDR_ENV=1`, `HERDR_PANE_ID`, `HERDR_TAB_ID`, `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`, and `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` (the current session's socket). Scripts use `HERDR_ENV` as the "am I inside herdr?" test and inherit `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` to target the current session — that's what `hvibe`/`hcode` rely on.
170:| `prefix + f` | `tv fleet-hosts` (SSH picker) | command pane |
174:| `prefix + P` | copy focused pane's **process info** to the clipboard | command pane |
178:| `prefix + d` | copy the **workspace ("space") root dir** — the right-click "Copy dir" herdr doesn't have ([details](#copy-to-clipboard)) | command pane |
247:**Quick Actions** are chezmoi-managed alongside them, under `…/cloudmanic.herdr-plus/quick-actions/` (one TOML per action). The repo ships the six **copy** actions (see [Copy pane + space facts](#copy-to-clipboard)) plus the plugin's five **starter** examples (GitHub / Google / Search Google / Open Repo / Reveal Working Dir), adapted for Linux — macOS `open` → the repo's cross-platform [`x open`](../shells/aliases.md), and the repo-select points at `daviddwlee84/*`. Because this managed dir is non-empty, herdr-plus does **not** auto-seed those examples itself (it only seeds into an *empty* dir), which is why they're vendored here; delete any TOML you don't want. Add your own by dropping a TOML here, or ship a repo-local set in `<repo>/.herdr-plus/quick-actions/`.
253:Most `tv` channels (`tools`, `fleet-hosts`, `mlflow`, `kill-process`, `ssh-config`) have **non-tmux-coupled actions**, so they run unchanged in a herdr command pane — just bind a key to `tv <channel>`. Only the channels whose actions call `tmux …` need herdr-aware variants. Three ship here:
265:herdr detects agent state natively and rolls it up into the sidebar (a blocked agent marks its pane/tab/workspace). Claude Code is detected via **screen-manifest heuristics** (terminal title + OSC progress), not lifecycle hooks. If the heuristics prove insufficient, state can be pushed explicitly:
300:- **pulls through every other top-level key** the live file has (`onboarding`, `[session]`, `[remote]`, `[update]`, `[experimental]`, …) so herdr's runtime writeback survives.
313:## Remote sessions (`herdr --remote`)
315:herdr can run a **local thin client attached to a herdr server on another host over SSH**:
318:herdr --remote <ssh-target> [--session NAME] [--handoff]
319:herdr --remote local_ubuntu          # <ssh-target> is any host/alias from ~/.ssh/config
322:What it does (from <https://herdr.dev/docs/remote>):
324:- SSHes to `<ssh-target>`, detects the remote platform, and **auto-installs a matching herdr server binary there** — the remote does **not** need herdr pre-installed (it does need SSH access + permission to install/run a binary).
325:- Bridges your **local clipboard** (including image paste) to the remote server and keeps your **local keybindings** (`--remote-keybindings server` to use the server's instead).
326:- `--session NAME` picks/creates a named session on the remote; `--handoff` opts into live handoff.
328:**Config** — the `[remote]` block in `config.toml`:
330:- `manage_ssh_config = true` (default) — herdr runs the bridge SSH through a generated config that includes your `~/.ssh/config` first and adds `ServerAliveInterval`/`ServerAliveCountMax` so idle NAT/network timeouts don't drop the session. Set `false` to run plain SSH against your config unchanged.
331:- `remote_image_paste` (`[keys]`) — raw-key image-paste binding, active only under `--remote`.
333:**Troubleshooting `remote platform detection failed: Connection closed by <host> port 22`**: this is a **transient SSH-level close**, not a herdr config problem. Verify the SSH path herdr uses actually works, then just retry:
336:ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=5 <ssh-target> 'uname -sm'   # should print e.g. "Linux x86_64"
339:If plain SSH works, retry `herdr --remote <ssh-target>`; if it keeps failing, check `~/.config/herdr/herdr-client.log` / `herdr.log` right after the failure. Common real causes: SSH auth needing an interactive prompt the bridge can't answer, or sshd rate-limiting rapid connections (`MaxStartups`).
341:## Running herdr nested inside tmux (multi-remote)
343:The repo's default stance is herdr **or** tmux, not nested. But you can deliberately nest — tmux as the outer window manager with several inner herdr clients, some local and some `herdr --remote <host>` to different servers. The catch is the **prefix collision**: both default to `Ctrl+b`, so outer tmux swallows it and inner herdr never sees its prefix ([herdr #759](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/discussions/759)).
349:3. **Don't nest — use herdr's native remoting.** `herdr --remote <target> [--remote-keybindings local|server]` runs a local thin client against a remote herdr server without tmux in the middle, and herdr hosts multiple named sessions itself. For a pure "multiple remotes" need this is often cleaner than nesting; `--remote-keybindings local` (default) keeps your local keymap, `server` uses the remote's.
400:| **cwd** | `--cwd` → `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD` → `herdr pane get` `foreground_cwd` → `$PWD`. Preferring the env var means it still works when the CLI is protocol-mismatched with a stale server |
409:## Copy pane + space facts to the clipboard {#copy-to-clipboard}
411:Six one-keypress "grab this onto the clipboard" ops, all driven by one helper (`~/.config/herdr/pane-copy.sh` = [`dot_config/herdr/executable_pane-copy.sh`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/herdr/executable_pane-copy.sh)). It distills a herdr CLI call into human-readable text and pipes it to the repo's own [`x copy`](../shells/aliases.md) (auto-selects pbcopy / wl-copy / xclip / xsel / OSC 52; `x` is resolved by absolute-path fallback since a command-pane may run without the interactive PATH). The pane defaults to the **current focused pane** (`herdr pane current`); the keybinds pass `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID`, the Quick Actions pass `$HERDR_PLUS_PANE_ID`, and either falls through to the current-pane lookup when empty.
413:| Op | Key | Quick Action | What lands on the clipboard |
456:| Patterns | `http(s)` / `ftp` / `file`, bare `www.` → `http://`, `IPv4[:port]` → `http://`, `git@…` SSH remotes → `https://…`, quoted `"owner/repo"` → `github.com/owner/repo`, `import "pkg"` → `npmjs.com/package/pkg` |
464:The copy-path sibling of the URL picker. `prefix+p` opens an fzf popup of the file paths in the focused pane; pick one (or several) and the path is copied to the clipboard. Lowercase `p` ("copy **p**ath") sits under the uppercase copy family (`prefix+P/D/V/S`), the same `u`/`U` convention. On tmux the analog is the **extrakto** plugin (`prefix + Tab`) — see [tmux keybindings](tmux/keybindings.md).
474:| **Two-tier list** | Paths that **exist** show first (copied as their resolved **absolute** path); everything else — remote / stale / hypothetical — appears below a `── unverified ──` separator (still selectable), so real-but-unresolvable paths aren't lost |
485:- **OSC133 copy-mode** (`cpout` / `cpblock`, prompt-jump, last-output yank) is tmux-specific. herdr's copy mode (`prefix+[`) is vi-style but has no OSC133 prompt-boundary awareness. `cpcmd` (zsh history, multiplexer-agnostic) still works.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-08-28 11:49:21Z)**_

Not expected — and it pins the cause. `SSH_CONNECTION` / `SSH_TTY` / `SSH_CLIENT` are **all empty** in your herdr pane, but `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` / `DISPLAY` are set. And raw OSC 52 to `/dev/tty` **does** reach your laptop.

So: the herdr **server** is a persistent daemon. Its pane environment is frozen to whatever existed when the server first started (a graphical session → `WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-0`), and it never refreshes `SSH_CONNECTION` on new panes the way `tmux` does via `update-environment`. Result: every herdr pane looks "local + Wayland" to `x` and Neovim, so both pick `wl-copy` and write to the **remote box's** clipboard — which you can't see. The `is_ssh()` fix I added can't help because there's no SSH var to detect.

The fix has to key off something that's actually true in a herdr pane. `HERDR_ENV=1` is set in every herdr shell, and a herdr pane's TTY always points at the real client (local or remote) — so OSC 52 is the correct channel there regardless.

**How should `x` (and Neovim) pick the clipboard backend when SSH vars are absent because herdr froze the pane env?**

Options:
- **Auto (HERDR_ENV) + X_CLIPBOARD override** - In a herdr pane (HERDR_ENV=1), try OSC 52 first — correct whether herdr is local or remote. Plus add an explicit `X_CLIPBOARD=osc52|wl-copy|…` env knob for any other case (mosh, VS Code Remote-SSH). Zero per-box config for herdr; escape hatch for the rest.
- **X_CLIPBOARD override only** - Add just the explicit `X_CLIPBOARD` env var. You set `export X_CLIPBOARD=osc52` in ~/.shellrc.adhoc on each box you reach remotely. No behavior change for anyone else, but manual per-box.
- **Auto (HERDR_ENV) only** - Just make herdr panes prefer OSC 52. Simplest, but no knob for mosh / other multiplexers, and local-herdr users lose native wl-copy (paste still works; copy caps at ~75KB before erroring).

**Also apply the same fix to Neovim yank?**

Options:
- **Yes** - Update dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua so it also forces the OSC 52 provider under HERDR_ENV / X_CLIPBOARD, not just SSH_CONNECTION. You said nvim yank has the same problem.
- **No, just x for now** - Only fix the `x` CLI (and cref/abspath which use it). Leave Neovim's clipboard config as-is.


**Answer:** Auto (HERDR_ENV) + X_CLIPBOARD override, Yes

<summary>Tool use: **Write**</summary>

````markdown
# `x copy` / Neovim yank land on the wrong clipboard inside herdr (or any multiplexer that strips `SSH_*`)

**Symptoms** (grep this section):

- Working on a remote box **inside herdr** (or zellij, mosh, VS Code / Cursor
  Remote-SSH). `abspath | x copy`, `cref`, `printf x | x copy` all report
  success but **nothing** reaches the clipboard of the machine you're typing
  on. `x paste` on the remote *does* show the text — it went to the remote's
  clipboard.
- Neovim `yy` / `"+y` over the same session also doesn't reach your local
  clipboard (same root cause).
- `echo "$SSH_CONNECTION | $SSH_TTY | $SSH_CLIENT"` in the pane is **all
  empty**, yet `echo "$WAYLAND_DISPLAY $DISPLAY"` is set
  (e.g. `wayland-0 :0`).
- A raw OSC 52 write **does** work:
  `printf '\033]52;c;%s\033\\' "$(printf hi | base64)" > /dev/tty` lands on
  the local clipboard. So the terminal chain is fine — only `x` / nvim pick
  the wrong backend.

**First seen**: 2026-08
**Affects**: `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_x` and
`dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua` before the `prefer_osc52` /
`HERDR_ENV` gate.
**Status**: fixed — both send OSC 52 first inside herdr/zellij and honour an
`X_CLIPBOARD` override.

## Root cause

Two independent bugs compounding:

1. **Backend chosen by `$WAYLAND_DISPLAY`/`$DISPLAY` presence, with no
   "am I remote?" check.** `x`'s `copy_backend()` and nvim's `options.lua`
   both did this. nvim gated its OSC 52 override on `SSH_CONNECTION` /
   `SSH_TTY`; `x` had no SSH awareness at all.

2. **The herdr server is a persistent daemon and freezes its pane
   environment.** Every shell in a herdr pane inherits the env that existed
   when the *server* first started — a graphical login → `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`,
   `DISPLAY`, `XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland`. It never refreshes `SSH_CONNECTION`
   on a new client attach the way `tmux` does via `update-environment`. So a
   herdr pane over SSH looks *exactly* like a local Wayland terminal:
   `$WAYLAND_DISPLAY` set, `$SSH_*` empty. `x` / nvim pick `wl-copy` and
   write the **remote** compositor's clipboard. mosh (which deliberately
   unsets `SSH_*`) and older VS Code Remote-SSH hit the same shape.

   The herdr pane's **TTY**, however, always proxies to the real client
   (local or remote) — so OSC 52 is the correct channel regardless.

## Workaround / fix

`dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_x`:

- `prefer_osc52()` — true under `SSH_*`, `HERDR_ENV`, or `ZELLIJ`. Used
  instead of the old `is_ssh` gate: try `osc52_copy` first, fall through to
  `wl-copy`/`xclip`/`xsel` only if `/dev/tty` won't open.
- `osc52_copy()` opens `/dev/tty` for real (`{ : >/dev/tty; }`) before
  `base64` consumes stdin, so the fallback still has input.
- `X_CLIPBOARD` env var forces one backend, bypassing autodetect:
  `osc52 | wl-copy | xclip | xsel | pbcopy | clip.exe`. Honoured by `x copy`
  and `x paste`; `x copy-file` refuses under `osc52` / `prefer_osc52`.
- `copy_file_backend()` refuses over SSH/herdr (OSC 52 is text-only).

`dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua`: the OSC 52 provider now activates
on `SSH_CONNECTION` / `SSH_TTY` / `SSH_CLIENT` / `HERDR_ENV` / `ZELLIJ`, or
`X_CLIPBOARD=osc52`; `X_CLIPBOARD=<local tool>` opts back out. Keep this
predicate in sync with `prefer_osc52`.

**For a box you always reach through a multiplexer that hides `SSH_*`**
(and it isn't herdr/zellij — e.g. plain mosh), put this in
`~/.shellrc.adhoc` on that box:

```sh
export X_CLIPBOARD=osc52
```

If `x copy` / yank *still* doesn't reach the local clipboard after this, the
blocker is downstream: the **local** terminal doesn't forward OSC 52, or a
stale **local** tmux server (`tmux kill-server`). Confirm with the raw
`printf '\033]52;c;…'` test above.

## Related

- [`docs/tools/clipboard.md`](../docs/tools/clipboard.md) § Shell CLI — `x`
  and § Editor — Neovim (the `prefer_osc52` predicate + `X_CLIPBOARD` knob).
- [`docs/tools/herdr.md`](../docs/tools/herdr.md) § env vars — `HERDR_ENV=1`
  is the "am I in herdr?" signal; the frozen-env behaviour.
- [`lazygit-ctrl-o-no-clipboard-utilities-nvim-yank-silent.md`](lazygit-ctrl-o-no-clipboard-utilities-nvim-yank-silent.md)
  — the clipboard-CLI install that surfaced this (before it, `x` fell
  through to OSC 52 by accident because there was no `wl-copy` to pick).

````

On macOS `pbcopy` is built in; on a Linux desktop the binary comes from `wl-clipboard` / `xclip`, installed by the [`gui_apps_linux`](../../dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml) role ("Install clipboard CLIs"). Without it, `:checkhealth provider.clipboard` reports "No clipboard tool found" and yank silently no-ops — see [`pitfalls/lazygit-ctrl-o-no-clipboard-utilities-nvim-yank-silent.md`](../../pitfalls/lazygit-ctrl-o-no-clipboard-utilities-nvim-yank-silent.md).
103:- The check is `SSH_CONNECTION or SSH_TTY` — either is set by `sshd` for an interactive session.
107:### Downstream consumer — lazygit `Ctrl+O`
137:**Under SSH** (`SSH_CONNECTION` / `SSH_TTY` / `SSH_CLIENT` set) that order flips: OSC 52 is tried *first*, because a `wl-copy` / `xclip` on the remote box would put the text on the **remote's** clipboard — useless. If `/dev/tty` can't be opened (`ssh` with no PTY), `x` falls back through the display-server tools for the `ssh -X` "I actually want the remote X clipboard" case. `x copy-file` refuses outright over SSH — OSC 52 is text-only and a file object can't cross. Same gate as Neovim's `options.lua`.
184:| `x copy` over SSH puts nothing on the local clipboard (or lands on the *remote* box's) | pre-fix `x` used a local `wl-copy`/`xclip` on the remote whenever `$WAYLAND_DISPLAY`/`$DISPLAY` was set (leaks in via the systemd user session on a box you're also logged into graphically) | fixed — `x` now sends OSC 52 first under `SSH_*`. If it still fails, the *outer* (local) terminal isn't forwarding OSC 52, or the local tmux server predates `set-clipboard on` (`tmux kill-server`) |
189:- **Neovim OSC 52 provider** is gated on `SSH_CONNECTION`/`SSH_TTY` rather than always-on, specifically so local paste (`"+p`) continues to work. If you primarily work over SSH and don't mind the paste tradeoff, the `if …` block can be removed.
```

84	### 3. Editor — Neovim
85	
86	[`dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua`](../../dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua):
87	
88	```lua
89	vim.opt.clipboard = "unnamedplus"
90	
91	if vim.env.SSH_CONNECTION or vim.env.SSH_TTY then
92	  local osc52 = require("vim.ui.clipboard.osc52")
93	  vim.g.clipboard = {
94	    name = "OSC 52",
95	    copy  = { ["+"] = osc52.copy("+"),  ["*"] = osc52.copy("*")  },
96	    paste = { ["+"] = osc52.paste("+"), ["*"] = osc52.paste("*") },
97	  }
98	end
99	```
100	
101	- Locally, LazyVim's default provider is used (`pbcopy`/`wl-copy`/`xclip` — with working paste). That provider is a **runtime binary probe** — Neovim has no compile-time `+clipboard`. On macOS `pbcopy` is built in; on a Linux desktop the binary comes from `wl-clipboard` / `xclip`, installed by the [`gui_apps_linux`](../../dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml) role ("Install clipboard CLIs"). Without it, `:checkhealth provider.clipboard` reports "No clipboard tool found" and yank silently no-ops — see [`pitfalls/lazygit-ctrl-o-no-clipboard-utilities-nvim-yank-silent.md`](../../pitfalls/lazygit-ctrl-o-no-clipboard-utilities-nvim-yank-silent.md).
102	- Over SSH, Neovim's built-in `vim.ui.clipboard.osc52` (shipping since Neovim 0.10) emits OSC 52 directly, bypassing any `pbcopy` binary on the remote host.
103	- The check is `SSH_CONNECTION or SSH_TTY` — either is set by `sshd` for an interactive session.
104	
105	Why conditional rather than always-on OSC 52? OSC 52 paste is unreliable (see the terminal table above). Keeping the local provider for local sessions preserves Neovim's paste behaviour; the override only activates when `pbcopy` on the remote is clearly the wrong answer.

135:**在 SSH 下**（`SSH_CONNECTION` / `SSH_TTY` / `SSH_CLIENT` 有設）順序會顛倒：先試 OSC 52，因為遠端機器上的 `wl-copy` / `xclip` 會把文字放進**遠端**的剪貼簿，毫無用處。若 `/dev/tty` 無法開啟（無 PTY 的 `ssh`），`x` 才退回顯示伺服器工具，涵蓋 `ssh -X`「我真的要遠端 X 剪貼簿」的情況。`x copy-file` 在 SSH 下直接拒絕 — OSC 52 只能帶文字，檔案物件無法跨越。與 Neovim `options.lua` 用同一個判斷閘門。

185:- **`x` CLI 順序**偏好本機後端（`pbcopy`、`wl-copy` 等）而非 OSC 52 —— **SSH 下例外**，此時 OSC 52 優先（遠端機器上的本機後端是錯的機器）。這是刻意的：當本機 `pbcopy` 可用時，它較快、不碰 TTY，且能處理非常大的酬載（OSC 52 酬載受終端機大小限制 — iTerm2 上限為 1 MB，許多其他為 64–256 KB）。SSH 分支會在消耗 stdin 之前真正開啟 `/dev/tty`（而非只做 `[[ -w ]]`），所以無 PTY 的 `ssh` 仍能乾淨地往下退。

138	## Keybindings
139	
140	Prefix is `ctrl+b` (same as tmux). Built-in actions can only be *rebound* (herdr's action set is fixed); everything else is a `[[keys.command]]` custom command. Custom commands receive `$HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD` and run from the focused pane's cwd.
141	
142	> **Two families of herdr env vars.** The `HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_*` vars above are injected **only** into `[[keys.command]]` invocations. Every shell *running inside a herdr pane* also gets an **ambient** set: `HERDR_ENV=1`, `HERDR_PANE_ID`, `HERDR_TAB_ID`, `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`, and `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` (the current session's socket). Scripts use `HERDR_ENV` as the "am I inside herdr?" test and inherit `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` to target the current session — that's what `hvibe`/`hcode` rely on.
143	
144	| Key | Action | Type |
145	|---|---|---|
146	| `prefix + c` / `prefix + 1..9` | new tab / switch tab | built-in default |
147	| `prefix + C` | new tab at the workspace (**space**) root dir — `prefix+c` + mouse "+" stay follow-focused-pane | command pane |

55:**從 CLI 子指令鎖定某個 session**：`workspace`/`tab`/`pane`/`agent` **沒有 `--session`/`--socket` flag**。唯一的槓桿是 **`HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`** 這個環境變數 (env var)——把它設成某 session 的 `socket_path`，所有子指令就會導向該 session。在 herdr pane 內部它已經被 export 成當前 session 的 socket，所以*在 herdr 內*跑的腳本天生就鎖定當前 session。`hvibe --session NAME` 正是靠這個機制運作（見下文）。
81:| 預設範圍 | 有 `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`（Herdr 內部）時搜尋 ambient session，否則搜尋 `default`。`--session NAME` 從 `herdr session list --json` 解析權威 socket；`--all-sessions` 只掃描正在執行的 session。ambient socket 無法唯一對應到 registry 時回傳 2，不會誤標成其他 session。 |
146:> **兩組 herdr 環境變數。** 上面那組 `HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_*` **只**會被注入到 `[[keys.command]]` 的呼叫裡。而每個*跑在 herdr pane 內的 shell* 還會拿到一組**環境值 (ambient)**：`HERDR_ENV=1`、`HERDR_PANE_ID`、`HERDR_TAB_ID`、`HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`、以及 `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`（當前 session 的 socket）。腳本用 `HERDR_ENV` 當作「我在不在 herdr 裡？」的判斷，並繼承 `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` 來鎖定當前 session——這正是 `hvibe`/`hcode` 依賴的東西。
229:- **Attach 感知（像 svibe 的 `$TMUX` 分支）**：從 herdr **內部**跑 → workspace/tab 的 focus 呼叫會切換活著的 client（不開新 client）。從 herdr **外部的一般終端**跑 → 輔助函式會拉起一個 attach 到該 session 的 client，讓新 workspace 真的看得到（herdr 的 `workspace focus` 只會移動*已經 attach* 的 client，所以少了這步，整包會被建在看不見的地方）。`--no-attach` 兩種情況都以 detach 方式建立。判斷依據是環境值 `HERDR_ENV`。
350:注意:本 repo 的 tmux 用了很多 root-table `bind -n C-*` 綁定會**遮蔽**內層 app 的 `Ctrl` 鍵,所以 herdr 的 prefix-free *direct* 終端捷徑在 tmux 下不可靠——透過它的 prefix 觸及 herdr action（用 1 或 2）。herdr 自己的 `allow_nested`（config,預設 `false`）只管 herdr-inside-**herdr**（靠 `HERDR_ENV` 偵測）,不是 herdr-inside-tmux。
399:| **cwd** | `--cwd` → `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD` → `herdr pane get` 的 `foreground_cwd` → `$PWD`。優先用環境變數的好處是：即使 CLI 與舊 server protocol 不相容，它照樣能運作 |

# Shared helpers for bats tests. Source from each .bats file:
#   load "../test_helper.bash"   # or the equivalent relative path
#
# Keep this file tiny. No bats-assert / bats-file / bats-support — plain
# bats built-ins ([ ], run, $status, $output) are enough.

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/.." && pwd)"
if [ "$(basename "$REPO_ROOT")" = "tests" ]; then
  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$REPO_ROOT/.." && pwd)"
fi
export REPO_ROOT

_BATS_STUB_DIRS=()

# Create a temp directory and prepend it to PATH. Exposes the path via
# $BATS_STUB_DIR (not via stdout) so the PATH export actually sticks — using
# command substitution would run this in a subshell and discard the export.
setup_path_stub() {
  BATS_STUB_DIR="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/bats-stub.XXXXXX")"
  _BATS_STUB_DIRS+=("$BATS_STUB_DIR")
  PATH="$BATS_STUB_DIR:$PATH"
  export PATH BATS_STUB_DIR
}

# Cleanup function. Call from your own teardown() if you override it:
#   teardown() { your_cleanup; cleanup_path_stubs; }
cleanup_path_stubs() {
  local dir
  for dir in "${_BATS_STUB_DIRS[@]:-}"; do
    [ -n "$dir" ] && [ -d "$dir" ] && rm -rf "$dir"
  done
  _BATS_STUB_DIRS=()
}

# Default teardown — fires only if the .bats file does not define its own.
teardown() { cleanup_path_stubs; }

+# Reach for OSC 52 before any local wl-copy/xclip/xsel? True when a local

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-08-28 12:20:37Z)**_

Root cause found and fixed. `SSH_CONNECTION` being empty was the real clue: **herdr's server is a persistent daemon that freezes the pane environment** at start — `$WAYLAND_DISPLAY` stays set (stale), `$SSH_*` never gets refreshed (tmux does this via `update-environment`; herdr doesn't). So `x` and nvim both saw "local Wayland" and copied to the remote box's clipboard.

3 commits on `main` (not pushed):

| commit | |
|---|---|
| `28d64aa` | install `wl-clipboard`/`xclip`/`xsel`; lazygit `Ctrl+O` → `x` |
| `f68f649` | `x` sends OSC 52 first under `SSH_*` |
| `1d0a101` | `x` + nvim also detect `HERDR_ENV`/`ZELLIJ`; `X_CLIPBOARD` override |

**What changed in `1d0a101`:**
- `x`'s `prefer_osc52()` now fires on `HERDR_ENV` / `ZELLIJ` too → OSC 52 first (correct whether herdr is local or remote, since the pane TTY always reaches the real client).
- `nvim` `options.lua` — OSC 52 provider now also activates on `HERDR_ENV` / `ZELLIJ`.
- `X_CLIPBOARD` env var forces a backend (`osc52|wl-copy|xclip|xsel|pbcopy|clip.exe`) — for mosh / Remote-SSH boxes where `SSH_*` is hidden and it isn't herdr.
- `x copy-file` refuses under SSH/herdr (can't send file objects over OSC 52).
- `tests/unit/x_cli.bats`: hermetic `setup()`, fixed a stale macOS assertion, +3 tests. **10/10 pass.**

**To pick it up** (in your herdr pane):
```
chezmoi apply
```
That redeploys `~/.dotfiles/bin/x` and `~/.config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua`. Then:
```sh
abspath | x copy          # → your laptop's clipboard now
```
```
In nvim (restart it first): yy → paste on your laptop
```

If you ever hit a box reached via bare mosh / VS Code Remote-SSH (not herdr), add to its `~/.shellrc.adhoc`:
```sh
export X_CLIPBOARD=osc52
```
